The fictional Sultanate of Aryavarta (approx. 500 km north‑south, 300 km east‑west) faces recurrent monsoon floods that isolate riverine districts. The Sultan wishes to revive a state‑run relay communication system based on Ibn Battuta’s description of the Delhi Sultanate’s *uluq* (horse‑post, royal horses every 4 mi) and *dawa* (foot‑post, relay runners every 1/3 mi) to transmit flood‑warning bulletins from the capital to remote outposts within 2 hours. Modern terrain data show that 70 % of the route is flat plain (average speed of horse 12 km/h, runner 6 km/h) and 30 % is hilly forest (horse speed reduced to 8 km/h, runner to 4 km/h). The Sultanate also wants to use the same network to transport perishable mangoes (max allowable transit time 6 h) from orchards to urban markets, generating revenue that could offset the system’s maintenance cost.  
Assuming the capital‑to‑farthest outpost distance is 350 km (measured along the predominant plain‑hill mix), answer the following sub‑parts. All calculations must use the original mile‑based spacings (1 mi = 1.609 km) and incorporate the terrain‑adjusted speeds.

(B) Compute the minimum time required for a flood‑warning message to travel the 350 km route via the *dawa* system, using terrain‑adjusted runner speeds.

A transition metal M forms a metallic hydride MHₓ. 1.00 g of metal powder absorbs 0.042 g of H₂ at 300 K and 1 atm to form a non-stoichiometric hydride. The metal has atomic mass 50.9 g/mol (Vanadium). Determine x in MHₓ and explain why x is not an integer.

IOCL’s board approves a ₹2 lakh crore capex plan to achieve net‑zero emissions by 2046. The plan spans three phases: Phase I (2025‑2030) – ₹50 000 cr on solar‑PV and wind farms; Phase II (2031‑2038) – ₹80 000 cr on green‑hydrogen electrolyzers and carbon‑capture units; Phase III (2039‑2046) – ₹70 000 cr on battery‑storage and bio‑fuel blending units. The finance team must: (1) forecast future electricity prices (influencing solar‑PV viability) and hydrogen demand (influencing electrolyzer utilization) using a Vector Autoregression (VAR) model with inputs: GDP growth, crude oil price, and policy‑stringency index; (2) compute NPV of each phase using a 10% discount rate, incorporating tax shields from accelerated depreciation (30% WDV) and a projected carbon‑credit revenue stream (₹500/ton CO₂e avoided) expected to rise 3% p.a.; (3) conduct a Monte‑Carlo simulation (10 000 runs) varying key assumptions (electricity price volatility σ=15%, hydrogen demand growth μ=8% p.a., σ=12%) to derive the probability that NPV > 0 for each phase; (4) prepare a rolling‑wave plan where detailed budgets are made only for the imminent phase while later phases remain outline plans; (5) monitor actual capex expenditure versus budget quarterly and initiate corrective if variance exceeds ±5%. The CFO asks: (a) which elements of the exercise constitute forecasting versus planning, (b) how the VAR‑derived forecasts become premises for the capital‑budgeting model, (c) what type of plan (strategic, tactical, operational, single‑use) each phase represents, (d) how the cost concept ensures that only relevant cash flows (tax shield, carbon‑credit, incremental capex) are considered, and (e) how the monitoring step links variance analysis to the planning cycle.

(C) Classify each phase of IOCL’s capex plan (Phase I, II, III) as strategic, tactical, operational, or single‑use plans.

A multinational research team overwinters at Concordia Station (Antarctica) for 14 months. During the polar night (≈105 days of continuous darkness), ambient temperature averages –55 °C, wind chill reaches –80 °C, and fresh food supplies run low after month 8. Satellite‑based internet bandwidth is limited to 30 kbps, causing a 2‑hour round‑trip delay for video calls with families. Crew members report heightened irritability, difficulty concentrating, and occasional bouts of hopelessness. The station commander notes that while some view the darkness as a “chance to test endurance” (challenge), others feel it is an “imminent danger to mental health” (threat). Medical logs show a gradual decline in salivary immunoglobulin A (IgA) levels from baseline 180 µg/mL to 95 µg/mL by month 10. The station’s operating agreement is governed by the Antarctic Treaty System, which mandates logistical support and medical evacuation protocols.  
Using this scenario, answer the following sub‑parts.

(A) Which primary appraisal category (harm/loss, threat, challenge, benign‑positive) best describes the perception of a crew member who believes the polar night poses an imminent danger to their mental health?
Compare the density of ice and liquid water at 0°C. Explain the structural reason using hydrogen bonding geometry.

In 2024, a coastal district of Odisha experienced severe cyclonic flooding, displacing ~150 000 people to temporary relief camps. The state government, with NGOs, set up community kitchens providing meals designed to meet caloric needs, reduce psychological trauma, and preserve socio‑cultural identity. Each meal comprised 200 g locally sourced rice (carbohydrate), 100 g dal (protein), 20 g fortified oil (lipid + vitamin A), and 50 g traditional pitha (sweet rice cake) prepared using age‑old recipes from the displaced communities. Psychologists reported a 30 % drop in anxiety scores when familiar flavors were served; sociologists observed increased sharing and bonding during communal eating. Political scientists noted the operation complied with the National Food Security Act (NFSA), ensuring equitable distribution irrespective of caste or religion. Geographers mapped kitchen locations relative to flood‑safe zones and supply‑chain routes, optimizing logistics. Historians traced the pitha recipe to 16th‑century temple offerings, showing how culinary heritage reinforces resilience.  
Using the data above, evaluate how this initiative exemplifies the three functions of food and identify the underlying nutrient contributions and cross‑disciplinary linkages.

(E) Geographers optimized kitchen locations using flood‑safe zones and supply‑chain routes. Describe one geographic factor (physical or human) that influenced site selection and explain how ignoring it could increase the meal’s effective energy cost (kcal per beneficiary) by at least 10 %.

A metropolitan traffic‑management centre uses a real‑time decision module to grant green‑wave priority to emergency vehicles (ambulances, fire trucks). The module evaluates the Boolean expression  

**P = (EmergencyDetected ∧ (RouteClear ∨ AlternateAvail)) ∧ (PedestrianSafe ∧ ¬CongestionSevere) ∧ (TimeWindow ∧ (WeatherGood ∨ LowVisibilityMode))**  

where:  
- **EmergencyDetected** = 1 if GPS + audio‑sirens confirm an emergency vehicle within 500 m of the intersection.  
- **RouteClear** = 1 if all downstream lanes on the primary route have speed >30 km/h and no accidents.  
- **AlternateAvail** = 1 if a pre‑computed detour route exists with capacity >2 veh/min and distance penalty <15 %.  
- **PedestrianSafe** = 1 if crosswalk sensors show no pedestrians in the conflict zone.  
- **CongestionSevere** = 1 if average vehicle density >120 veh/km on any approach.  
- **TimeWindow** = 1 if current time is within the permitted priority window (06:00–22:00).  
- **WeatherGood** = 1 if visibility >5 km and precipitation <0.1 mm/h.  
- **LowVisibilityMode** = 1 if the system has activated a fallback protocol that relies on RFID tags instead of visual detection.  

The city’s GIS layer provides elevation, flood‑risk, and population‑density data for each intersection. Historical data show that during monsoon months, **LowVisibilityMode** is activated 35 % of the time, and **CongestionSevere** correlates positively with population density (r=0.68).  

Students must (a) compute P for a set of five intersections (I1–I5) given the attribute table, (b) analyze how geographical factors (elevation, flood risk) indirectly affect the Boolean variables (e.g., flood‑prone zones increase likelihood of CongestionSevere), (c) relate the system’s design to disaster‑management policy (National Disaster Management Act, 2005) and the principle of *proportionality* in administrative law, and (d) discuss the trade‑off between safety (avoiding false negatives) and efficiency (avoiding false greens) using concepts from Boolean algebra and decision theory.

(E) Discuss how geographical attributes — elevation and flood‑risk level — could indirectly influence the Boolean variables **CongestionSevere** and **LowVisibilityMode** in the priority system. Propose a simple causal model linking GIS data to the probability of these variables being 1, and comment on the implications for equitable emergency response across topographically diverse regions.

In a series LCR circuit used for radio tuning, the coil has resistance 10 Ω and inductance 1 mH. The capacitor is variable. At resonance with a 1 MHz signal, the voltage across the capacitor is measured as 100 V RMS. The source voltage is 1 V RMS. (a) Calculate the quality factor Q of the coil. (b) Determine the capacitance at resonance. (c) If the source frequency drifts to 1.01 MHz, estimate the new power factor and explain whether the circuit will still select the desired station effectively.

A borrower takes a loan of ₹25,00,000 at 9% p.a. reducing balance for 15 years. After 5 years (60 EMIs paid), they want to prepay the loan. Calculate the outstanding principal at that point using the Present Value of remaining EMIs method. Then calculate the total interest saved by prepaying now vs continuing for full term.

You are producing 50 uniform shirts (polyester-cotton blend, 150 g/m²) for a school. Each shirt requires: 1.8 m fabric (112 cm wide), 15 m thread, 12 buttons, 0.3 m fusible interfacing. Fabric costs ₹120/m, thread ₹5/m, buttons ₹2 each, interfacing ₹30/m. Cutting layout yields 2 shirts per 1.8 m length (marker efficiency 85%). Labour: cutting 15 min/shirt, stitching 45 min/shirt, finishing 20 min/shirt. Labour rate ₹80/hour. Overheads 20% of direct cost. Calculate total production cost per shirt and suggest two ways to reduce cost without compromising quality.

A 20‑kg, 10‑year‑old patient with type 1 Gaucher disease exhibits a basal glucocerebroside synthesis rate of 0.02 µmol·min⁻¹·kg⁻¹. Lysosomal glucocerebroside concentration is measured at 0.5 mM (normal ≈ 0.05 mM). Recombinant human glucocerebrosidase (imiglucerase) produced in CHO cells has a specific activity of 2500 U·mg⁻¹ (1 U = 1 µmol·min⁻¹) and follows Michaelis–Menten kinetics with Km = 0.15 mM for the substrate. The enzyme is administered intravenously over 2 h every 2 weeks. Plasma clearance is first‑order with t½ = 30 min, and the volume of distribution is Vd = 0.07 L·kg⁻¹. Only 10 % of plasma‑delivered enzyme reaches lysosomes via mannose‑6‑phosphate receptors. The infusion solution contains enzyme at 10 mg·mL⁻¹. Tubing used for infusion has inner diameter 0.5 mm, length 100 cm, and the fluid viscosity is 1.2 cP. Venous pressure is 5 mmHg.  
Using the data above, answer the following sub‑parts.

(C) Compute the total mass (mg) of enzyme that must be infused over the 2‑h period to reach the plasma concentration at the end of infusion, accounting for first‑order elimination during the infusion.

An HIV‑positive patient is to be initiated on abacavir. The HLA‑B*57:01 allele confers a markedly increased risk of hypersensitivity reaction (HSR). In a North‑Indian cohort the allele frequency of HLA‑B*57:01 is 0.08. The binding affinity (KD) of abacavir to HLA‑B*57:01 measured by surface plasmon resonance (SPR) is 15 µM, whereas to the common HLA‑B*07:02 it is >500 µM (non‑binding). The odds ratio (OR) for HSR in carriers vs. non‑carriers is 45. Assume the baseline risk of HSR in the general population is 0.5 %. A logistic‑regression model predicts probability of HSR as P = 1 / [1 + exp(‑(β0 + β1·X))], where X = 1 for HLA‑B*57:01 carrier, β0 = ln(baseline odds) and β1 = ln(OR). The patient’s HLA typing by PCR‑SSP shows a single band at 260 bp (specific for B*57:01) and no band at 210 bp (B*07:02). Calculate the patient’s absolute risk of HSR, determine whether genotyping is cost‑effective if the test costs ₹1500 and treating an HSR episode averages ₹45 000 (cost‑benefit ratio < 1 favors testing), and discuss the physical principle of SPR that allows KD determination. Finally, comment on the ethical imperative to disclose genetic test results to the patient’s insurance provider.

(E) State the primary ethical concern regarding disclosure of HLA‑B*57:01 genotype results to an insurance provider, and name the principle that protects against such disclosure.
A gift shop owner wants to wrap a box that is 8 cm long, 4 cm wide, and 2 cm high. She has a piece of wrapping paper that is 100 cm². Is it enough? Show your work.

A team wishes to scale up a finite mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF) line from T‑flasks to a 5 L glass‑stone bioreactor. MEFs are anchorage‑dependent, exhibit contact inhibition, and have a finite lifespan of ~30 population doublings before senescence. The culture uses serum‑free medium with a dissolved oxygen (DO) set‑point of 40 % air saturation. The oxygen solubility in the medium at 37 °C is 0.21 mmol L⁻¹·atm⁻¹. The bioreactor is sparged with air (0.21 atm O₂) at 0.5 vvm (volume of gas per volume of liquid per minute). The volumetric mass transfer coefficient kLa is measured as 15 h⁻¹. The maximum specific oxygen uptake rate (qO₂,max) for MEFs is 0.45 mmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹, and the average cell dry weight is 300 pg cell⁻¹. Cell growth follows logistic kinetics with carrying capacity K = 1×10⁸ cells mL⁻¹ and intrinsic rate μmax = 0.03 h⁻¹.  
Assuming steady‑state DO and that oxygen transfer limits growth when OTR < OUR, answer the following.

(E) The bioreactor uses a Rushton turbine impeller of diameter D = 0.1 m. Estimate the Reynolds number (Re) for the liquid phase (ρ = 1000 kg m⁻³, η = 0.0012 Pa·s) at an impeller speed of 60 rpm. State whether the flow is laminar, transitional, or turbulent (use Re < 10 laminar, 10–10⁴ transitional, >10⁴ turbulent).

In 2024, a team of urban engineers discovers an abandoned, intact platform beneath Grand Central Terminal, labeled “Level 3” on old 1930s schematics. The platform contains vintage ticket booths, 1940s-style advertisements, and a functioning telegraph line that sporadically prints messages dated 1918. The city’s mental‑health department commissions a report to decide whether this space should be (a) preserved as a historical artifact, (b) opened as a therapeutic “escape zone” for stressed commuters, or (c) sealed due to safety concerns. As a consultant, you must synthesize: (i) literal details from Finney’s story about Charley’s experience, (ii) the psychiatrist’s interpretation of the third level as a waking‑dream wish‑fulfillment, (iii) Freudian theory of repressed desires surfacing in dreams, (iv) sociological research on urban alienation and commuter stress, and (v) policy frameworks for public mental‑health interventions in transit hubs. Your report must justify each recommendation with evidence from the text and the cross‑disciplinary sources.

(D) Draft a public‑mental‑health policy clause (≤ 25 words) for using historic transit spaces as therapeutic zones, referencing the political‑science node on public mental‑health policy.

A regional planning council in Northeast India (Arunachal Pradesh) must decide between setting up a 1,000 MW Hydroelectric Dam project or a 1,000 MW Solar Park. The region features steep Himalayan mountain slopes, glacier-fed fast-flowing rivers, dense forests, high annual monsoon rainfall, and frequent overcast cloud cover for nearly 6 months a year. Analyze all factors and recommend the most geographically viable energy project.

A bidi roller in Nipani earns ₹50 per 1000 bidis rolled. She works 8 hours a day and rolls 500 bidis per hour. Calculate her daily earnings. If the minimum wage for the region is ₹300/day, what percentage of the minimum wage does she earn? What does this gap illustrate about piece-rate home-based work?

Discuss how the genetic ancestry findings (55 % tribal haplogroups, 40 % Brahmin haplogroups) challenge the traditional varna‑based occupational theory of caste, referencing the tribal‑caste continuum concept.

A biomedical engineer designs a copper‑IUD to maximize Cu²⁺ ion release (which immobilizes sperm) while ensuring the radial stress on the uterine wall stays below its yield limit (≈0.3 MPa). The uterine cavity is approximated as a thin‑walled cylinder of inner radius Rᵤ = 30 mm and length Lᵤ = 70 mm. The IUD stem is a solid copper cylinder of radius r and height h (h ≤ Lᵤ). Cu²⁺ release flux J (mol s⁻¹) is proportional to the exposed copper surface area A₍Cu₎ = 2πrh (lateral area only; ends are embedded in tissue). The proportionality constant k = 2.0 × 10⁻¹² mol cm⁻² s⁻¹. The IUD exerts a radial interference δ = Rᵤ – r (δ > 0 for snug fit). The resulting contact pressure p on the uterine wall is given by p = E·δ/r, where E = 0.5 MPa is the effective Young’s modulus of the myometrium. The hoop (circumferential) stress in the thin wall is σ = p·Rᵤ/t, with wall thickness t = 2 mm.  
**Task:** Determine the optimal stem radius r that maximizes J while keeping σ ≤ σ_yield.

(B) For the same IUD (r = 4 mm, h = 50 mm), compute the hoop stress σ in the uterine wall (in MPa).

A cyclist of total mass 80 kg (including bicycle) climbs a hill of inclination 10° at a constant speed of 5 m/s. The rolling friction and air resistance together exert a constant retarding force of 50 N parallel to the slope. Calculate the instantaneous power the cyclist must deliver. If the cyclist can sustain 400 W, what is the maximum constant speed possible on the same hill? (g = 10 m/s², sin10° ≈ 0.1736, cos10° ≈ 0.9848)

A state government launches the “Village‑Link” scheme to upgrade 15 000 km of Rural Roads (other district roads) to all‑weather standards in the rain‑shadow region of Marathwada, Maharashtra. The scheme aims to reduce post‑harvest losses of soyabean from 12 % to 6 % by improving market access. Current data: Maharashtra’s total rural road length is 210 000 km (≈70 % of state’s road network). The state’s annual soyabean production is 4.5 million tonnes, with an average market price of ₹ 38 000/tonne. The upgrade cost is estimated at ₹ 1 20 000 per km, financed 50 % by state budget, 30 % by centrally sponsored scheme (CSS) for rural infrastructure, and 20 % by village panchayat contributions (via MGNREGA labor). The Panchayati Raj Act (73rd Amendment) delegates responsibility for rural roads to Gram Panchayats, while the State List entry 8 empowers the State Government to construct and maintain State Highways and District Roads.  

Using the information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(C) Estimate the annual monetary value of soyabean loss reduction achieved by the scheme.

In early 2025, a multinational consortium secured a 30‑year lease to extract rare‑earth elements (REEs) from the biodiverse Eastern Ghats, home to 4 million Adivasis belonging to the Kondh, Saora, and Gadaba tribes. The project promises ₹85 000 cr in export revenue but requires clearing 1 200 km² of forest, displacing an estimated 250 000 tribal households and threatening sacred groves. Four response coalitions emerged: (i) **Reformist NGOs** demand a strengthened Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) with mandatory free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) and a revenue‑sharing trust fund; (ii) **Revolutionary Eco‑Socialists** call for the abolition of private mining, advocating community‑controlled stewardship of the Ghats under a constitutional “Ecological Commons” amendment; (iii) **Resistance Groups** (traditional tribal councils) seek to defend existing forest rights under the Forest Rights Act 2006 (FRA) and block further encroachment by setting up vigilance patrols; (iv) **Reactionary Traders’ Association** argues for maintaining the status‑quo of state‑led mineral licensing, claiming that tribal opposition hinders national technological sovereignty and urging stricter anti‑terrorism laws to curb protests. Satellite data shows forest cover loss of 3.2 % per year in the lease area since 2022, while the national average is 0.4 %. The Ministry of Environment issued a draft order allowing “conditional clearance” contingent on compensatory afforestation elsewhere, which tribes contend violates the FRA’s prohibition on non‑forest‑land compensation.

(B) Apply the concept of “relative deprivation” to explain why tribal households perceive deprivation despite the project’s promised national revenue.

A designer is building a microfluidic perfusion system for *Arabidopsis thaliana* callus cultures. The system maintains a constant osmotic potential (Ψₛ) of –0.5 MPa using a sucrose solution. The sucrose concentration required to achieve Ψₛ is given by the van’t Hoff equation Ψₛ = –iCRT, where i = 1 (non‑electrolyte), R = 0.008314 MPa L mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, T = 298 K.  
Auxin (IAA) is supplied at a basal rate of 0.1 µg h⁻¹ mL⁻¹ of culture volume. IAA degrades via first‑order kinetics with rate constant k_deg = 0.02 h⁻¹ (pH 5.8, 25 °C). The system includes a feedback sensor that measures IAA concentration and adjusts the infusion pump to keep the steady‑state concentration at C_set = 0.5 µg mL⁻¹ (optimal for shoot induction).  
The culture vessel has a working volume of 5 mL.  
Assume perfect mixing and that the pump can vary infusion rate linearly with error.  

Answer the following:

(A) Calculate the sucrose concentration (in mol L⁻¹) required to generate an osmotic potential of –0.5 MPa at 298 K.

In FY24, India’s merchandise imports were USD 640 bn (crude oil 30 %, electronics 12 %, gold 8 %, machinery 10 %, others 40 %). Exports were USD 460 bn (petroleum products 15 %, pharmaceuticals 12 %, textiles 8 %, engineering goods 14 %, others 51 %). The government introduced a Production‑Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for advanced chemistry cells (ACC) that is expected to reduce lithium‑ion battery imports by 25 % over two years. Currently, lithium‑ion battery imports account for 40 % of electronics imports. A new maritime corridor via the Suez Canal reduces average shipping distance to Europe by 15 %, lowering freight costs by 10 %. The price elasticity of demand for Indian engineering goods in EU markets is –1.1. Simultaneously, a WTO dispute settlement body has imposed a countervailing duty of 6 % on Indian steel exports, with an estimated elasticity of –0.7 for steel demand in importing countries. Using the data, answer the following.

(B) Estimate the reduction in lithium‑ion battery imports (in USD bn) after the PLI scheme achieves a 25 % cut.

A transgenic rice line expresses a hairpin RNA that yields 21‑nt siRNAs targeting the Lepidoptera gut‑specific enzyme chitin synthase (CHS). The dsRNA precursor is present at **150 ng g⁻¹** fresh leaf weight at the time of spraying. In the field, UV‑B radiation (280‑315 nm) with an average irradiance of **0.8 W m⁻²** drives first‑order photodegradation of the dsRNA with a rate constant **k = 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹** (determined at this irradiance). Pest mortality is observed when the intracellular siRNA concentration in the midgut exceeds **5 nM**, which corresponds to a leaf‑tissue dsRNA level of **~20 ng g⁻¹** (assuming 100 % processing efficiency and uniform distribution). The rice canopy intercepts **60 %** of the incident UV‑B flux. Assume leaf thickness and water content do not affect the rate constant.

(A) Calculate the dsRNA concentration (ng g⁻¹) remaining in the leaf after **4 hours** of continuous UV‑B exposure.

Excavations at Mohenjo‑Daro reveal two massive brick platforms on the citadel, each 45 m × 22 m and 2 m high, subdivided into 12 rectangular rooms with sleeper walls and air‑ducts. Adjacent to the platforms lies a large open courtyard with evidence of grain‑processing tools (querns, sickles). GIS‑based terrain modelling shows the citadel sits on the highest natural levee of the Indus floodplain, 3 m above the surrounding lower town, while the lower town occupies the active floodplain prone to seasonal inundation. Contemporary satellite imagery of modern grain silos in the Punjab region shows a similar preference for elevated, flood‑free sites with easy road access. Using this data, assess how the granaries’ location and design reflect Harappan administrative strategies.

(D) Based on the granary’s placement on the citadel and its association with standardized weights (found nearby), infer which Harappan administrative function is most strongly evidenced and justify with two pieces of archaeological evidence.

AetherSat, founded in 2021, builds low‑cost Earth‑observation satellites for disaster‑management imaging. The founders aim for a 12% EBITDA margin within four years (organisational objective), to provide free satellite data to NGOs during floods and cyclones (social objective), and to offer engineers a patent‑sharing scheme, continuous learning sabbaticals, and equity‑based rewards (personal objective). To meet these goals, AetherSat must plan satellite design cycles, organise a supply chain for radiation‑hardened components, staff aerospace engineers, software developers, and regulatory liaisons, direct teams toward performance milestones and compliance with the Indian Space Policy, and control costs via earned value management (EVM) and variance analysis. Coordination between the R&D team (payload design), the regulatory team (licensing and frequency allocation), and the operations team (launch and ground‑station coordination) is essential to avoid costly launch delays. The firm uses management accounting to compute the cost per satellite (₹45 crore) and applies Ind AS 16 for property, plant and equipment. Economically, the company evaluates the social return on investment (SROI) using a discount rate of 7% and estimates that each hour of early‑warning imagery saves ₹5 lakh in disaster‑related losses. The board asks which integrated set of management objectives, functions, accounting, economic, and legal‑policy concepts best explains how AetherSat can achieve its triple bottom line while navigating high‑tech uncertainty.

(B) Which management function is primarily responsible for ensuring that R&D, regulatory, and operations teams work in tandem to meet launch schedules?

Two years after COVID‑19 school closures, a metropolitan education department surveys 200 government and private schools in Bengaluru to assess the prevalence of specific learning disabilities (SLD) among adolescents aged 13‑19 and the adequacy of inclusive practices. The survey covers 50,000 students, using DSM‑5‑based screening tools administered by school psychologists. Results show an overall SLD prevalence of 12%, with dyslexia (45% of SLD cases), dyscalculia (30%), and dysgraphia (25%). Concurrently, 68% of teachers report insufficient training in differentiated instruction, and 54% of parents express concern about social stigma affecting their child’s school participation. The department plans to implement a tiered Response‑to‑Intervention (RTI) model, allocate ₹120 crore over three years for teacher training, assistive technology, and counseling services, and partner with NGOs to run peer‑support circles. The initiative draws on adolescent development theory (Erikson’s identity vs. role confusion), cognitive psychology (working memory deficits in SLD), sociology of education (labeling theory and peer influence), educational law (RTE Act 2009 Sections 12‑16 on inclusive education), and urban geography (digital access disparities affecting online remedial modules). The goal is to raise the proportion of SLD students receiving appropriate accommodations from 35% to 70% within two years.

(C) The program allocates ₹120 crore over three years for teacher training, assistive technology, and counseling. If 40% of the budget is for assistive technology, 35% for teacher training, and the remainder for counseling, what is the annual expenditure on counseling?

Three partners (X, Y, Z) operate a social enterprise partnership manufacturing affordable solar lanterns for rural households. Their partnership deed (1 Apr 2023) stipulates: profit sharing ratio 3:2:1; fixed capitals X ₹5,00,000, Y ₹3,00,000, Z ₹2,00,000; interest on capital @10% p.a.; monthly salary X ₹20,000 (managing), Y ₹15,000 (technical); commission to Z @5% of net profit after charging such commission; guarantee to Z that total appropriation (interest+salary+commission+profit share) ≥ ₹3,00,000 p.a., deficiency borne by X and Y in 3:2; interest on drawings @12% p.a. (product method). Drawings: X ₹10,000 at beginning of each quarter; Y ₹15,000 at end of each half-year; Z ₹5,000 per month at beginning. Past adjustment: interest on drawings for 2022-23 omitted (X ₹1,20,000, Y ₹1,80,000, Z ₹60,000 evenly throughout, rate 12%, avg period 6 months). Net profit before appropriations 2023-24: ₹12,00,000. Government grant ₹2,00,000 for clean energy credited to capital reserve. Partners evaluate “inclusive development” (Development) via per capita income from firm (Per Capita Income (Pci) Of A State).

(D) Prepare Profit & Loss Appropriation Account for 2023-24 and Partners’ Capital & Current Accounts (fixed capital method).

A private company plans to deploy a low‑Earth‑orbit (LEO) satellite constellation operating at 12 GHz (Ku‑band) to provide broadband internet. Each satellite transmits with an average power of 5 W via a parabolic antenna of gain 45 dBi. The ground‑station receiver has an effective aperture of 0.5 m² and a system noise temperature of 50 K. The link must close with a minimum received power of –120 dBm to achieve a target bit‑error rate. Using Maxwell’s equations, the displacement current concept justifies the propagation of the 12 GHz wave through vacuum. The company’s finance team models the monthly operating cost (in USD) as a function C(f) = α f² + β f + γ, where f is the carrier frequency in GHz, α = 2 × 10³, β = –1.5 × 10⁴, γ = 5 × 10⁴.  

(a) Verify that the displacement current density J_D = ε₀ ∂E/∂t is non‑zero for the sinusoidal electric field of the 12 GHz wave and explain why it is essential for sustaining the wave in vacuum.  
(b) Determine the free‑space path loss (in dB) for a slant range of 800 km, using the Friis transmission equation and the given antenna gains.  
(c) Calculate the received power (in dBm) and state whether the link budget meets the –120 dBm requirement.  
(d) Find the frequency f (in GHz) that minimizes the operating cost C(f) and compute the corresponding minimum cost.  
(e) If the company decides to shift to 24 GHz (Ka‑band) to double the data rate, quantify the change in path loss (in dB) and comment on the trade‑off between bandwidth and link margin, assuming all other parameters remain unchanged.

(E) If the carrier frequency is doubled to 24 GHz, calculate the change in free‑space path loss (ΔL_p) and discuss the impact on link margin.

The Madhya Pradesh Tourism Directorate proposes a “Jain Heritage Circuit” linking five major pilgrimage sites: Shravanabelagola (Karnataka), Palitana (Gujarat), Khajuraho (Madhya Pradesh), Chandragiri (Karnataka) and Sonagiri (Madhya Pradesh). Expected annual visitor flow is 5 lakhs, with average spending of ₹2,000 per visitor. The circuit must (i) respect sectarian sensitivities (Digambara monks practice nudity; Shvetambara monks wear white clothes), (ii) comply with constitutional protections for religious minorities, (iii) minimize travel distance starting and ending at Bhopal, (iv) assess socio‑economic impact on local artisan communities whose livelihoods depend on stone‑carving and miniature painting, and (v) ensure financial viability over a 10‑year horizon with an initial investment of ₹120 crore, a discount rate of 8 %, and maintenance costs estimated at 15 % of gross revenue.  

Distance matrix (km) – *Bhopal* as hub:  

| From\To | Shravanabelagola | Palitana | Khajuraho | Chandragiri | Sonagiri |
|---------|------------------|----------|-----------|-------------|----------|
| Bhopal  | 800 | 900 | 400 | 850 | 200 |
| Shravanabelagola | – | 1100 | 900 | 300 | 750 |
| Palitana | 1100 | – | 1000 | 1150 | 850 |
| Khajuraho | 900 | 1000 | – | 800 | 350 |
| Chandragiri | 300 | 1150 | 800 | – | 700 |
| Sonagiri | 750 | 850 | 350 | 700 | – |

(A) Based on the sectarian practice of monastic nudity, which artistic convention is most likely to be observed in Digambara‑majority Jain temples compared to Shvetambara‑majority temples?

Rahul is solving a "water jug" problem: Jug A (8L), Jug B (5L), Jug C (3L). Initially A=8L, B=0, C=0. Goal: get exactly 4L in A and 4L in B. He *mentally* tries: pour A→B (A=3,B=5,C=0), pour B→C (A=3,B=2,C=3), pour C→A (A=6,B=2,C=0), pour B→C (A=6,B=0,C=2), pour A→B (A=1,B=5,C=2), pour B→C (A=1,B=4,C=3), pour C→A (A=4,B=4,C=0) — success. He then *physically* executes these pours. Analyse Rahul's *mental trial phase only* using the NCERT definition: "Thinking is a higher mental process through which we manipulate and analyse the acquired or existing information by means of abstracting, reasoning, imagining, problem solving, judging, and decision-making."
Interpret the physical meaning of the optimal altitude h*≈285 km in terms of communication link budget and satellite lifetime.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you're scrolling through a podcast app: a political commentary episode from the 1930s sounds ______ different from a modern TED Talk for students.

GreenGen Biotech, a partnership firm operating a chain of botanical gardens and biotech research labs (referencing taxonomic hierarchy Taxonomic Hierarchy and botanical garden management Taxonomic Aids), has three partners: Dr. Arora (botany), Dr. Basu (biotech), and Dr. Chawla (commercialization) sharing profits 5:3:2. Dr. Chawla retires on 31-Mar-2025. The partnership deed stipulates goodwill valuation at 3 years' purchase of super profits. Super profit = Average adjusted profit – Normal profit. Normal profit = Capital employed × Normal rate of return. The normal rate of return is benchmarked to the 10-year government bond yield (7%) plus a risk premium derived from the difference between national per capita income growth (Per Capita Income (Pci) Of A State: 6.2%) and the firm's sectoral growth (12%), yielding 11.2%. The firm's average adjusted profit after tax (3 years) is ₹48 lakh. Capital employed (net assets at fair value) is ₹3.2 crore. Existing goodwill of ₹15 lakh appears in books. The continuing partners decide to settle goodwill by adjusting capital accounts in gaining ratio without raising a goodwill account. Revaluation reveals: land appreciates by ₹40 lakh (botanical garden land), patents (biotech IP) depreciate by ₹8 lakh, and a contingent liability of ₹5 lakh for environmental compliance (Public Facilities: public facilities regulation) is recognized. General reserve stands at ₹24 lakh. The retiring partner's loan is to be paid in 4 equal annual installments with 10% interest. The firm's tax rate is 25%.

(B) Pass journal entries for (i) writing off existing goodwill, (ii) adjusting retiring partner's goodwill share through capital accounts, (iii) revaluation of assets/liabilities.

In early 2025, the federal government of the fictional union “Euroterra” ratified the **Treaty of Verdun‑II**, which transferred the historically bilingual region **Nordland** (population 3.2 million, 68% speakers of Nordish, 30% speakers of Eurotese, 2% other) from the Eurotese‑dominant state of Westaria to the Nordish‑dominant state of Ostara. Article 7 of the treaty mandates that, within 18 months, all public schooling in Nordland must switch exclusively to Eurotese as the medium of instruction, citing “administrative uniformity.” Nordish‑speaking parents protest, fearing erosion of cultural identity.  

Lena, a 16‑year‑old Nordish‑speaking student at Gymnasium Nord, awakens late on the first day of the new policy. She recalls her teacher, Mr. Keller, announcing a surprise test on Nordish grammar—a topic she neglected while dreaming of the spring fair outside. She considers skipping school to join friends at the riverside, where Ostaran soldiers drill near the old timber mill. The morning is bright; birds chirp at the forest edge. Despite the temptation, Lena decides to attend, dreading a scolding. In class, Mr. Keller, dressed in his best coat, announces that this is the last Nordish lesson; from tomorrow, only Eurotese will be used. He reads aloud a poignant passage about the mother tongue, his voice trembling. Lena, who previously mocked Nordish as “backward,” suddenly feels a deep ache, realizing she can barely write a simple sentence correctly. She watches Mr. Keller write “Vive la Nordisch!” on the blackboard with unusual care, noting the old map of Nordland on the wall and the pigeons cooing on the roof. After class, she walks home, the usual playground noise now sounding like a solemn hymn.  

Using the data above, answer the sub‑parts.

(E) Synthesize the English, historical, political‑science, and geographical insights to argue whether Lena’s final reaction (walking home hearing the playground as a hymn) signifies *internalized resistance* or *passive grief*. Support your claim with at least two interdisciplinary evidences.
A rhombus-shaped field has diagonals measuring 48 metres and 36 metres. The farmer wants to plant grass on the field at a cost of ₹25 per square metre. Find the total cost of planting grass.

A Bengaluru‑based AI‑health startup launches a 6‑month “Innovator Fellowship” for 120 engineering graduates. Selection uses three tools: (i) the Mayer‑Salovey‑Caruso Emotional Intelligence Test (MSCEIT) – yielding scores on Perceiving, Using, Understanding, Managing emotions; (ii) the Differential Aptitude Test (DAT) – measuring verbal reasoning, numerical ability, abstract reasoning, space relations, mechanical reasoning, and language usage; (iii) the Torrance Tests of Creative Thinking (TTCT) – yielding fluency, originality, elaboration, resistance to premature closure, and abstractness of titles. Concurrently, each fellow provides a saliva sample for cortisol awakening response (CAR) – a biological marker of stress reactivity – and a baseline polygenic score for serotonin transporter (5‑HTTLPR) linked to affective regulation. The startup’s finance team projects that a 1‑point increase in average MSCEIT Managing‑emotions score reduces employee turnover cost by ₹1.2 lakhs per annum, while a 1‑point increase in DAT numerical ability raises project‑completion speed, saving ₹0.8 lakhs per fellow per year. The HR head asks: (a) Which EI branch most strongly predicts lower CAR after controlling for 5‑HTTLPR? (b) If the fellowship aims to maximize net financial gain (turnover savings + speed savings) subject to a budget that allows only 80 fellows to receive a premium EI‑training module (cost ₹15,000 each), how should they allocate the training based on baseline MSCEIT scores? (c) Assuming a threshold IQ of 115 (WAIS‑IV) is required for high‑level abstract reasoning in DAT, what proportion of fellows would be excluded if the current sample mean IQ is 110 (SD=12)? (d) How would a 10 % increase in the heritability estimate of 5‑HTTLPR (from 0.40 to 0.44) affect the predicted change in CAR per unit MSCEIT Managing‑emotions score, assuming a linear gene‑environment interaction model? (e) Draft a simple cost‑benefit inequality that justifies offering the premium EI‑training to fellows whose baseline MSCEIT Managing‑emotions score is below a cutoff C, expressing C in terms of the given cost and benefit parameters.

(A) Using the MSCEIT branches, which one shows the strongest negative correlation with cortisol awakening response (CAR) after adjusting for 5‑HTTLPR polygenic score, assuming the following standardized beta coefficients from a multiple regression: Perceiving = ‑0.12, Using = ‑0.08, Understanding = ‑0.15, Managing = ‑0.22?

SteelForge Ltd., an established steel manufacturer, plans to expand capacity by 30%. It opts for a rights issue of equity shares and a private placement of debentures.  
- Current equity: 5,00,000 shares of Rs 10 face value, market price Rs 25.  
- Rights issue: 1 new share for every 5 held at Rs 18 per share (including premium). Payment: Rs 5 on application, Rs 8 on allotment (including premium), Rs 5 on call.  
- Private placement: 2,000 debentures of Rs 1,000 face value issued at 8% discount, redeemable at par after 5 years, interest 6% p.a. payable yearly.  
- The expansion is expected to increase EBITDA by Rs 2 crore per year. The company’s current debt‑equity ratio (book) is 0.4. Tax rate 30%.  
- The price elasticity of demand for steel is –0.8; a planned 5% price increase is anticipated to boost contribution margin.  
Using the data, answer the following.

(A) Compute the amount of share capital and securities premium credited on allotment of rights shares.

During a novel respiratory virus outbreak in 2025, the government mandates a contact‑tracing app that collects GPS location, Bluetooth proximity data, and voluntary health symptoms. Data are stored centrally for 180 days and shared with law‑enforcement for “public order” purposes. Civil‑society groups argue that the scheme infringes on privacy and enables profiling of marginalized communities, while public‑health officials claim it reduced the effective reproduction number (R₀) from 2.8 to 1.2. Historical analogies are drawn to wartime surveillance in WWII Europe (The Roman Empire (27 BCE‑style reasoning), and scholars reference the Belgian power‑sharing model to suggest oversight mechanisms. The state’s finance ministry estimates the program’s operational cost at ₹4 crore per month, based on server maintenance and personnel.
Using the information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(D) Apply the Belgian power‑sharing model (The Belgian Accommodation Model) to propose an oversight mechanism for the tracing app that ensures minority community representation.

The Andaman & Nicobar Islands face intermittent disruption of inter‑island ferry services due to cyclonic swells (average 5‑day outage per year). To ensure timely delivery of vaccines and emergency medicines, the Ministry of Health proposes a drone corridor connecting Port Blair to three remote islands (Havelock, Neil, and Little Andaman). Each drone (fixed‑wing VTOL) has a payload of 10 kg, cruising speed 80 km/h, range 150 km, and requires 0.5 kWh per km electricity. Electricity is supplied by diesel generators on the islands (specific fuel consumption 0.25 L/kWh, diesel price ₹90/L, emission factor 2.68 kg CO₂/L). The government plans to subsidize electricity at ₹4/kWh for drone operations. In 2023, the islands consumed 1.2 million doses of vaccine annually, requiring 2 kg of cargo per dose (including packaging).  
Using the information, answer the following.

(C) Compute the annual CO₂ emissions (in tonnes) associated with generating the electricity for drone operations, assuming diesel generators supply all electricity, using the given specific fuel consumption and emission factor.

Indian Oil Corporation Ltd. (IOCL) aims to achieve net‑zero operational emissions by 2046 through a ₹2 lakh crore investment in renewable energy, waste‑management, and biodiversity projects. The corporate planning team must first forecast future energy demand under three scenarios: (i) baseline GDP growth of 6% p.a., (ii) accelerated green‑policy scenario with 8% p.a. renewable adoption, and (iii) shock scenario where a global carbon tax reduces fossil‑fuel demand by 4% p.a. Forecasts are to be made for the next 10 years using a simple trend‑line method based on historical petrol‑sales data (average annual growth 5.2% ±0.8%). Simultaneously, the finance division prepares a capital budget for the ₹2 lakh crore outlay, classifying expenditures into capital‑work‑in‑progress (CWIP) and revenue‑expense heads, and applies a 10% discount rate to compute NPV. The board asks: (a) which elements constitute planning versus forecasting, (b) how the forecast assumptions become planning premises, (c) what type of plan (strategic, operational, or single‑use) each activity represents, and (d) how cost‑concept principles ensure that only relevant future costs are included in the investment decision.

(C) Classify the following IOCL activities as strategic, operational, or single‑use plans: (i) Setting the 2046 net‑zero vision, (ii) Preparing the annual capital budget for renewable projects, (iii) Launching a pilot waste‑recycling plant in Gujarat.

A 2025 research symposium on “Literature and Social Reform” presents a 180‑word excerpt from Prasad’s 1938 short story where the protagonist, a widowed schoolteacher, establishes a night‑class for village girls, defying patriarchal norms. Accompanying data: (i) 1921 Census shows female literacy at 1.6 % versus male literacy at 9.8 %; (ii) the 1917‑1918 Women’s Suffrage Bill (though unsuccessful) demanded voting rights for women; (iii) the 1950 Constitution’s Article 15(3) empowers the State to make special provisions for women and children; (iv) a 2022 NITI Aayog report notes that districts with ≥30 % female secondary‑school enrollment have 12 % lower infant mortality. Participants must, in a 12‑minute discussion, (i) infer Prasad’s implied message about women’s agency, (ii) locate a symbol that represents that message, (iii) trace how early suffrage efforts sought to alter the socio‑educational landscape depicted, (iv) evaluate whether Article 15(3) provides a sufficient legal backbone for initiatives like the night‑class, and (v) craft a discussion point linking literary evidence, historical suffrage, and constitutional provision to a present‑day policy suggestion for girls’ STEM outreach.

(E) Construct a discussion point that links Prasad’s symbol, the suffrage movement’s goal, and Article 15(3) to recommend a present‑day policy for girls’ STEM engagement.
Fill in the blank: You traditionally grow tall, local wheat ______ that yield 800 kg/hectare.

Design a research plan to investigate how the *amara-nayaka* system (military chiefs holding territory) functioned in the 1520s, using ONLY sources available by 1900 (i.e., before modern archaeology). List the source types, their specific contributions, and one major gap that would remain.
True or False: Macro and micro minerals are inorganic elements required by the body in relatively large (macro: >100 mg/day) and trace (micro: <100 mg/day) amounts respectively.

The RBI conducts an outright OMO purchase of ₹20,000 crore of government securities from commercial banks. The current currency-deposit ratio (cdr) is 0.2 and the reserve-deposit ratio (rdr) is 0.1. Calculate the maximum potential increase in money supply (M3). Assume no change in cdr or rdr.

The Forest Department of Chhattisgarh proposes diverting 800 hectares of Very Dense Forest (VMDF, canopy >70%) in Hasdeo Arand for coal mining. The forest currently provides: carbon sequestration (12 tC/ha/yr), watershed services to 50 villages (population 75,000), habitat for 15 Schedule-I species, and NTFP income of ₹18,000/ha/yr for 2,000 tribal households. The mine promises ₹2,500 crore revenue over 30 years and 1,200 jobs. Using a 5% discount rate and TEEB India values, calculate the Net Present Value (NPV) of ecosystem services lost over 30 years and compare with mine revenue. Should the diversion be approved on economic grounds alone?

Following the 2025 Lok Sabha election, a coalition government led by the Hyderabad‑based regional party is formed with support from three OBC‑based micro‑parties and two smaller national parties. The coalition’s CMP includes a clause that any new central‑government‑funded digital infrastructure project must allocate 20% of its procurement budget to firms certified as “OBC‑inclusive” (minimum 30% OBC workforce). The Finance Ministry warns that this procurement condition could raise project costs by 8‑12%, potentially breaching the fiscal deficit target of 5.8% of GDP. Simultaneously, the GST Council is debating whether to treat the OBC‑inclusive certification as a subsidy that attracts countervailing duties under GST compensation cess. The coalition’s internal coordination committee meets weekly to resolve disputes, but a faction within the national partner argues that the reservation clause undermines merit‑based procurement and should be replaced by a skill‑gap‑training fund financed through a small cess on digital services.

(A) Determine whether the coalition’s weekly coordination committee satisfies the constitutional requirement for aid and advice to the President under Article 75, given that the committee includes non‑ministerial party representatives.

In 2025, a multinational AI‑data‑labeling firm, “VeriData,” operates a remote‑work hub in Patna employing 8,000 mostly‑young workers to annotate images for autonomous‑vehicle training. Workers are paid per task via an opaque algorithm that reduces rates when productivity dips, effectively imposing a **digital piece‑rate system** reminiscent of colonial tinkathia. Internal surveys reveal that 62 % feel compelled to accept arbitrarily low pay because refusing leads to de‑activation of their accounts (loss of livelihood). A coalition of workers invokes Gandhi’s “conflict of duties,” claiming a moral duty to resist exploitative algorithms versus a duty to sustain family income. They organize a silent‑online protest (changing profile pictures to a spinning charkha) and petition the Ministry of Labour under the **Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020**, alleging psychological harm and unfair labor practices. The firm’s defense cites consent via click‑wrap agreements and argues that algorithmic wage‑adjustment is a legitimate business efficiency measure. Using the Indigo chapter, concepts from social psychology (group conformity, moral disengagement), and sociological theories of digital labor, answer the following.

(C) From a social‑psychology perspective (Psychology), which factor most strongly explains why 62 % of workers accept low pay despite perceiving it as unfair?

Why does the Census definition require 75% of *male main workers* specifically to be in non-agricultural work, rather than 75% of *total workers* or *total population*? What would happen to the urban count if the threshold were lowered to 50%?

Read the following scenario and answer the questions that follow.

"In 2018, a whistleblower in a state health department leaked documents showing that a company blacklisted for supplying spurious drugs in three states was awarded a ₹200 crore contract after the Health Minister allegedly intervened. The whistleblower was later suspended on charges of 'violating conduct rules.' The state Lokayukta investigated but could not proceed because the Minister's prior sanction was required under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which the Governor refused. The case is now in the High Court."

(a) Identify the specific institutional gap that allowed the Minister to block the investigation. 
(b) Explain how the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 attempted to fix this gap for central ministers, and why the same fix may not apply to state ministers. 
(c) Evaluate whether the judiciary can effectively fill this accountability vacuum in the interim.

A startup produces eco-friendly water bottles. Fixed costs are ₹5,00,000 per month. Variable cost per bottle is ₹40. They plan to sell 10,000 bottles per month. They want a 25% markup on total cost per unit. Calculate the selling price per bottle using cost-plus pricing.

Case Study: Rohan, 11 years, 35 kg, active football player (training 1.5 hr/day, 5 days/week). His mother packs: 3 aloo parathas (90g wheat + 75g potato + 10g oil), 100g curd, 1 banana. She says "He eats everything and asks for more." Using ICMR 2020 and sports nutrition principles, evaluate if this tiffin meets his NEEDS (not just RDA). Calculate his estimated energy requirement (EER) using FAO/WHO/UNU formula for active boys: EER = 88.5 - 61.9×age + PA×(26.7×wt + 903×ht) + 25, where PA=1.58 for active, ht=1.45m. Compare tiffin energy to 1/3 EER. Also assess protein, calcium, iron adequacy. Recommend 2 specific modifications with quantities.

A prototype smart contact lens contains a circular parallel‑plate capacitor (radius = 2 mm, plate separation = 10 µm) filled with a biocompatible dielectric (relative permittivity εᵣ = 3.2). The lens is driven by a sinusoidal voltage source V(t) = V₀ sin(ωt) with V₀ = 3 V and f = 1 kHz. The time‑varying voltage creates a displacement current I_d that produces a magnetic field detectable by a miniature pickup coil (N = 50 turns, radius = 1 mm) placed coaxially 0.5 mm above the lens. The induced emf in the coil is used to telemeter glucose‑dependent changes in εᵣ.  
Assume free‑space permeability μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H m⁻¹ and ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹.  
**(a)** Derive the expression for the instantaneous displacement current I_d(t).  
**(b)** Compute the peak magnetic field B₀ at the location of the pickup coil.  
**(c)** Determine the peak emf ε₀ induced in the pickup coil.  
**(d)** If the dielectric constant changes by Δεᵣ = 0.05 due to glucose variation, find the fractional change in the peak emf.  
**(e)** The lens costs $120, lasts 2 years, and has no salvage value. A conventional glucose strip costs $0.50 per test, used 4 times/day. Using a discount rate of 6 % yr⁻¹, compute the NPV of the lens over its lifetime and state whether it is economically viable.

(D) If glucose alters the dielectric constant by Δεᵣ = 0.05, compute the fractional change in the peak emf.
Fill in the blank: This is exactly what faced ______ scholars in early 1800s India.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a ______ collector reviewing the 2011 Census report for your area: the overall literacy rate is 73%, but female literacy is only 64.6% while male literacy is 80.9%, and the SC female literacy rate is even lower.

In the Himalayan state of Uttarakhand, the 2023 Rural Health Survey found that 27% of elderly residents reported suicidal ideation, linked to declining agricultural yields due to erratic monsoon patterns and the out‑migration of 62% of youth aged 18‑35 to urban centers. Simultaneously, a linguistic study of local dialects noted the erosion of traditional caregiving terminology, such as ‘सेवा’ (service) replaced by ‘सहायता’ (assistance), indicating shifting attitudes. The government’s ‘Manasik Swasthya Abhiyan’ allocated ₹450 crore for elderly mental health in hill states, yet field reports indicate only 30% of funds reach remote blocks due to difficult terrain and limited personnel. The story ‘ल्वजंक्ल की >कसाईम’ uses specific lexical choices and grammatical structures to depict the elderly couple’s helplessness. Analyze how the author’s vocabulary, syntax, and narrative comprehension strategies reveal the psychological and geographical drivers of elder neglect, and evaluate whether policy interventions targeting mental health and mountain livelihoods address the root causes shown in the text.

(B) Analyze the use of passive voice in the sentence “उनकी दवाइयाँ बच्चों द्वारा समय पर नहीं दी जातीं” and explain how this grammatical choice reflects the elderly couple’s lack of agency in the story.

In Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, an NGO establishes a roadside stand selling organic turmeric to combat farmer suicides. Modeled after Frost's poem, the stand aims to bypass exploitative middlemen. Initial urban response mirrors the poem: commuters either ignore it or complain about traffic obstruction. After 8 months, sales cover only 40% of costs. The NGO collaborates with an economics department to apply factors of production (land, labor, capital, entrepreneurship) and references colonial land revenue systems ( zamindari, ryotwari) from India's history that entrenched peasant debt. Data shows: land productivity declined 30% due to soil degradation (labor-intensive restoration needed), labor wages rose 25% post-MGNREGA implementation, capital investment required ₹5 lakhs/unit for drip irrigation, and entrepreneurial efforts face bureaucratic delays in FSSAI certification. Historical analysis reveals 1880s Deccan Riots were sparked by similar debt traps under British ryotwari surveys.

(D) Identify the ironic situation (Irony and paradox in 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers') in the NGO's economics collaboration. Explain why it constitutes tragic irony using the concept of opportunity cost from factors of production.

A consignment of 500 kg of certified organic cumin seeds arrives at Mumbai port from Ethiopia, labelled “Net Weight 500 kg ± 0.5 %”. The importer’s weighbridge shows a reading of 497 kg, while the port authority’s calibrated scale records 498.5 kg. The importer claims the discrepancy arises from moisture loss during transit (estimated 0.3 % weight loss) and seeks clearance. The customs officer suspects short‑weighting and invokes the Legal Metrology Act, 2009. Simultaneously, an environmental NGO argues that the long‑haul transport (Ethiopia → Djibouti → Mumbai) incurs 0.04 t CO₂ per ton‑km, contributing to climate impact, and demands a carbon‑offset fee under India’s National Clean Energy Fund. A trade association cites the WTO Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT), asserting that India’s domestic weight tolerance (±0.5 %) must not be more restrictive than international standards (ISO 22000 allows ±1 %). Using the data, assess the legal metrology compliance, the validity of the moisture‑loss defence, the WTO TBT implication, and the environmental liability.

(D) Compute the CO₂ emissions attributable to the transport of the 500 kg consignment over a distance of 7 200 km (Ethiopia–Djibouti–Mumbai) using the emission factor 0.04 t CO₂ per ton‑km, and state whether the resulting emissions qualify for a levy under India’s National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF) which taxes emissions > 0.1 t CO₂ per consignment.

Compare the social constraints on Eveline (a 19-year-old Dublin shop girl in 1904) with those on the grandmother in Class 9's "How I Taught My Grandmother to Read" (Krishtakka, a 62-year-old village woman in 1990s Karnataka). Identify one structural similarity and one crucial difference in how gender and tradition operate.

A defence contractor requires a lightweight, high‑tenacity nylon 6,6 fabric for parachute canopies. The fabric must be woven on a rapier power loom using 840 denier nylon yarn. Design calls for a 3/1 twill (warp‑face) weave to balance strength and packability. Required specifications: width 150 cm, EPI = 45, PPI = 30, target areal density ≤ 200 g/m². The plant is located in the Visakhapatnam‑Chennai industrial corridor. Students must evaluate yarn suitability, compute cover factor, predict mechanical behaviour, and assess how the Make‑in‑India defence policy influences location decisions and technology transfer.

(C) Explain how the 3/1 twill weave influences (i) tear strength, (ii) abrasion resistance, and (iii) dimensional stability under cyclic loading, relative to a plain weave of same yarn and sett.

A window is in the shape of a rectangle surmounted by a semicircle. The total perimeter of the window is 10 m. Find the dimensions of the window that admit maximum light (i.e., maximize the area). 
(a) Draw a labeled diagram and define variables.
(b) Write the area A as a function of one variable using the perimeter constraint.
(c) Find the critical point and verify it gives maximum area using the second derivative test.
(d) State the dimensions (radius of semicircle, height of rectangle) and maximum area.

After the Corus acquisition, Tata Steel reports a net profit of ₹8,000 crores for the fiscal year. The company has 1,000 crore equity shares of face value ₹10 each (paid‑up capital = ₹10,000 cr). The board is debating three dividend payout policies: 20 %, 40 % and 60 % of net profit. Dividend distribution tax (DDT) has been abolished, but dividend income is taxable at 10 % in the hands of shareholders. The firm must retain at least ₹3,000 crores for future capital expenditure. Under the Companies Act, 2013 a company may declare dividend only out of profits and may not exceed 40 % of its paid‑up capital in any year (to ensure adequate retention). Using this information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(B) Determine the retention ratio and verify whether the retained earnings satisfy the ₹3,000 crore capex requirement for each policy.

In June 2024 a 3‑minute video went viral on a popular Indian short‑form platform showing a group of elderly fishermen on North Sentinel Island (Andaman) refusing to engage with a government‑sponsored tourism project. The video, captioned “When progress feels like invasion”, garnered 4.2 million views, 68 % of comments expressed solidarity with the elders, and sentiment‑analysis tagged the dominant emotion as “anger”. A sociologist noted that the elders’ monologues echoed the frustration of isolated communities facing rapid modernization, reminiscent of the post‑Emergency period (1975‑77) when many rural voices felt silenced. A legal expert pointed out that the government’s proposal invoked Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of expression) but also raised concerns under Article 21 (right to life) regarding forced relocation.  
Using this scenario, analyze how Yashpal’s “cktkj n'kZu” employs the island setting, the old man's monologues, and the bird motif to critique modern humanity's relationship with anger. Your answer must integrate literary analysis with the historical (post‑Independence), political (Fundamental Rights), and sociological (social conflict) dimensions presented above.

(C) Analyze the bird motif in “cktkj n'kZu” as a symbol of fleeting hope amidst anger, and evaluate whether the viral video’s imagery (e.g., birds flying over the protest) reinforces or contradicts this symbolism.

Priya (Hindu, 24) and Rahul (Hindu, 26) married in 2020. In 2023, Priya files for divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act (mutual consent). Rahul agrees. They file a joint petition. After the first motion, Rahul withdraws consent before the second motion. Priya argues the cooling-off period of 6 months should be waived under *Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur* (2017). Will the court grant the waiver? Explain the legal position step by step.

A 2022 WHO report on Iraqi adolescent PTSD notes that 31% exhibit flashbacks triggered by loud noises resembling aerial strikes. The report quotes the poem’s lines:
“धड़कता दिल रुक‑रुक कर,
हवाई जहाज़ की साया में सोता बचपन.”
Students receive the complete stanza (8 lines) containing the lexical items **धड़कता**, **दिल**, **रुक‑रुक**, **हवाई जहाज़**, **साया**, **सोता**, **बचपन**, **तलाश**. Students must map the logical flow, evaluate the use of historical analogy, assess the rebuttal, identify rhetorical metaphors, and judge overall persuasiveness.

(A) Identify the central thesis of the white paper and state in which paragraph it is explicitly stated.

In 1952 the State of Punjab adopted a land ceiling of 30 acres per family under the First Five Year Plan. Survey data showed 1,20,000 cultivating families, of which 15 % held more than the ceiling. The Republic of Lumbia, a federal nation with three major ethnic regions (North, Central, South), entered Stage II of the demographic transition in 2020. In early 2025 a consortium of foreign ed‑tech MNCs (MetaLearn Inc., a US‑based VR platform, and EuroSkill Ltd., a German‑based credentialing body) partnered with a chain of private engineering colleges affiliated to the “Global Tech Universities Alliance” (GTUA) to launch “V‑Campus”, a metaverse‑enabled virtual classroom offering immersive labs, AI‑tutored problem‑solving, and internationally recognised micro‑credentials. Historically, the British colonial railway network in India (1850‑1947) facilitated movement of goods, troops, and administrators, but also created a “rail‑elite” of urban merchants, princely states, and British officials who gained preferential access to markets and administrative posts, while vast rural populations remained isolated.

A municipal officer (Ms. Patel) presents a redevelopment plan for a slum locality to a group of resident representatives. After a severe flood in the Gangetic plains, a NGO sets up a temporary community kitchen for 500 displaced persons. The kitchen receives a daily food budget of ₹150 per person (₹75,000 total). A biotech lab immunizes BALB/c mice with recombinant HER2 extracellular domain. After 4 weeks, spleen cells are harvested (≈2×10⁸ viable B‑cells). A *Pichia pastoris* strain is engineered to secrete a single‑chain variable fragment (scFv) of a therapeutic antibody under the strong AOX1 promoter. The scFv contains one N‑glycosylation site (Asn‑X‑Ser/Thr) that, if processed in yeast, yields high‑mannose glycans leading to rapid clearance. To improve pharmacokinetics, the strain is co‑expressed with a heterologous β‑1,4‑galactotransferase (GalT) and sialyltransferase (ST6Gal1) to enable galactosylation and sialylation in the Golgi.  
The fermentation will be run in a 100 L bioreactor (working volume 80 L) with the following parameters:  
- Initial glycerol (carbon source) concentration: 50 g L⁻¹ (used for biomass induction).  
- Methanol feed (inducer) starts after glycerol depletion, with a feed rate F(t) to be determined.  
- Biomass yield on glycerol Yₓ/₍gly₎ = 0.45 g g⁻¹; on methanol Yₓ/₍MeOH₎ = 0.35 g g⁻¹.  
- Maximum specific growth rate on methanol μ_max,MeOH = 0.18 h⁻¹; Monod constant Kₛ,MeOH = 0.05 g L⁻¹.  
- Specific scFv production rate qₚ = 0.015 g g⁻¹ h⁻¹ (growth‑associated).  
- Oxygen transfer capacity: kLa = 200 h⁻¹ (achievable with pure O₂ enrichment and high agitation).  
- Dissolved oxygen set‑point: 30 % of air saturation (C* = 0.009 mol L⁻¹ at 30 °C, 1 atm, pure O₂ → C* ≈ 0.021 mol L⁻¹).  
- Oxygen yield on biomass Yₓ/ₒ₂ = 0.85 g g⁻¹.  
- The culture pH drifts due to acid production; a phosphate buffer (pKₐ₂ = 7.2) at 0.05 M is used, with acid production rate rₐ = 0.02 mol L⁻¹ h⁻¹ (constant).  
- The goal is to maintain pH = 6.0 throughout the fed‑batch (to keep GalT/ST activity optimal) while avoiding oxygen limitation and minimizing ethanol formation (which occurs if methanol concentration exceeds 0.5 g L⁻¹).  

**Tasks:**  
1) Derive the methanol feed rate F(t) (in g h⁻¹) required to maintain a constant specific growth rate μ = 0.12 h⁻¹ (below μ_max to reduce overflow).  
2) Calculate the oxygen uptake rate (OUR) at this μ and verify that the supplied OTR (using kLa and C* − C_L) is sufficient.  
3) Determine the acid neutralisation rate (base addition) needed to keep pH = 6.0 given the buffer system.  
4) Estimate the scFv titre after 24 h of methanol feeding, assuming no product degradation.  
5) Explain how the co‑expression of GalT and ST influences the N‑glycan profile and the consequent in vivo half‑life of the scFv.

(B) Calculate the oxygen uptake rate (OUR) in mol L⁻¹ h⁻¹ at the steady μ = 0.12 h⁻¹ and X = 20 g L⁻¹, using Yₓ/ₒ₂ = 0.85 g g⁻¹, and compare it with the maximum OTR achievable with kLa = 200 h⁻¹, C* = 0.021 mol L⁻¹ (pure O₂) and C_L = 0.3·C*.

A satellite’s solar‑panel surface temperature \(T(t)\) (°C) is regulated by an onboard heater that switches on when the panel temperature falls below \(-30^\circ\)C and switches off when it rises above \(-10^\circ\)C. During one orbit the temperature can be modeled as  

\[
T(t)=
\begin{cases}
-20-5\sin\!\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{45}\right), & 0\le t< 30\ \text{min} \\[6pt]
-12+3e^{-(t-30)/20}, & 30\le t< 70\ \text{min} \\[6pt]
-8+2\cos\!\left(\dfrac{\pi (t-70)}{40}\right), & 70\le t\le 110\ \text{min}
\end{cases}
\]

where \(t\) is time measured from the start of the orbit (in minutes). The heater’s switching instants correspond to the points where the piecewise definition changes (at \(t=30\) min and \(t=70\) min). Using the definition of continuity, determine whether the temperature function is continuous at these switching times.  

Relevant physics: the orbital period is 90 min, but the heater logic creates a 110‑min thermal cycle due to eclipse‑induced cooling (orbital mechanics node). Relevant chemistry: the panel material’s linear thermal expansion coefficient \(\alpha = 12\times10^{-6}\ \text{K}^{-1}\) is used to compute induced stress if a discontinuity existed (thermal expansion node).

(D) Classify the type of discontinuity (removable, jump, infinite) at t=30 min and t=70 min for \(T(t)\).

A geostationary satellite transmits data via a 1550‑nm laser to a ground station. The uplink employs a graphene‑based electro‑absorptive modulator placed inside a micro‑cavity (length = 10 µm, effective mode area = 0.5 µm²). Applying a gate voltage V_g(t) = V₀ sin(ωt) modulates the graphene’s surface conductivity σ(ω), which changes the cavity’s effective refractive index n_eff and thus the resonance condition. The time‑varying index produces a displacement current density **J_d** = ε₀∂E/∂t + ∂P/∂t within the cavity mode, which in turn alters the cavity’s quality factor Q and the output power P_out.  
Given: ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹, μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ H m⁻¹, cavity resonance frequency ω₀ = 2πc/λ ≈ 1.215 × 10¹⁵ rad s⁻¹, V₀ = 2 V, ω = 2π × 10 GHz = 6.283 × 10¹⁰ rad s⁻¹, graphene’s linear‑response conductivity change Δσ = (e²/4ħ)·(V₀/E_F) with Fermi energy E_F = 0.3 eV. The cavity stores energy U = ½ ε₀n_eff²∫|E|² dV. Assume the electric field amplitude inside the cavity is E₀cav = √(2P_in/(ε₀n_effc A_eff)), with input power P_in = 10 mW, n_eff ≈ 2.0, c = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, A_eff = 0.5 µm².  
**(a)** Derive the expression for the displacement current density J_d(t) in the cavity, showing explicitly how the gate‑voltage‑induced conductivity change modulates the polarization term.  
**(b)** Calculate the peak vacuum displacement current density magnitude (ε₀∂E/∂t)ₚₑₐₖ inside the cavity.  
**(c)** Estimate the peak polarization current density magnitude (∂P/∂t)ₚₑₐₖ due to the graphene‑induced index change, using the relation Δn_eff ≈ (Z₀/2)·Δσ, where Z₀ = √(μ₀/ε₀) ≈ 377 Ω.  
**(d)** Using coupled‑mode theory, the fractional change in output power ΔP_out/P_out ≈ (2/Q)·(Δn_eff/n_eff)·(ω/ω₀)². If the unloaded Q = 5000, compute ΔP_out/P_out for the given parameters.  
**(e)** The satellite’s optical transmitter costs $4.2 M, has a 7‑year life, and requires $150 k/yr for station‑keeping. A competing RF Ka‑band transmitter costs $2.8 M, lasts 5 years, with $80 k/yr power‑amplifier maintenance, and needs replacement after 5 years. Using a discount rate of 4 % yr⁻¹, compute the NPV of each option over a 10‑year horizon (replace RF unit after 5 years). Which link is more economical?

(E) Compute the NPV of the satellite optical link (cost $4.2 M, life 7 yr, maintenance $150 k/yr) and the RF Ka‑band link (cost $2.8 M, life 5 yr, maintenance $80 k/yr, replacement after 5 yr) over a 10‑year horizon at a discount rate of 4 % yr⁻¹. State which is more economical.

In 2024 a newly formed Eurasian trade bloc debates adopting a transparency initiative inspired by Gorbachev’s Glasnost to curb corruption in its customs union. A research team investigates whether increased use of a government‑provided smartphone learning app reduces face‑to‑face social interaction among adolescent girls (14‑18 years) in five remote tribal villages of Arunachal Pradesh. They collect:

The Sardar Sarovar Project (SSP) on the Narmada River envisages a 138 m high gravity dam providing irrigation to ~1.8 million ha across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra, and generating 1 450 MW of hydro‑power. In 2025, the Delimitation Commission of India is tasked with revising the number of reserved seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) in State Legislative Assemblies. Fill in the blank: Imagine you're in a CUET group ______ round where the prompt is: "Science fiction predicts future technology — discuss with examples from Asimov's essay." You have 2 minutes to prepare.

In 2024, Gujarat’s cotton farmers faced a 30 % price swing due to global demand fluctuations, with the spot price moving from ₹58 000/qtl to ₹75 000/qtl within six months. To mitigate risk, a cooperative introduced a futures contract on the National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) with a lot size of 25 qtl, margin requirement of 5 % of contract value, and daily settlement. "GreenFields Agro Ltd." needs funds for three purposes: (A) Purchase of tractors worth ₹2 crore (useful life 10 years), (B) Fertilizer inventory for kharif season (4 months cycle, ₹50 lakh), (C) Cold storage facility (useful life 7 years, ₹3 crore). A 2024 NITI Aayog discussion paper on “Climate‑Resilient Agriculture” adopts the imagery from *fcLdksgj dh ekVh*—the butterfly’s fragile wings, the biting winter chill, and the mother’s milk—as metaphors for monsoon variability, cold‑wave stress, and the essential nature of groundwater irrigation, respectively. A neuro‑technology startup releases a prototype wrist‑band that monitors cortical activity and, in real time, projects subtle visual patterns onto the user’s retina via augmented‑reality glasses. The patterns are designed to fade when the user’s attention wavers, aiming to reduce mind‑wandering. During a pilot study with 80 participants, the following observations were recorded:
- When the projected pattern resembled Woolf’s ambiguous “mark” (low‑contrast, irregular shape), 62 % of participants reported increased self‑reflection, 24 % reported anxiety, and 14 % felt no change.
- Participants scoring high on the **Mindful Attention Awareness Scale (MAAS)** showed a 1.9 × greater likelihood of interpreting the mark as a cue for introspection rather than anxiety.
- The device’s algorithm adjusts pattern complexity based on recent gaze‑tracking data: if a user fixates on the pattern for >2 seconds, the algorithm simplifies it; if gaze shifts rapidly, the pattern becomes more complex.
- Post‑study interviews indicated that users who described the mark as a “reminder of nature’s continuity” (e.g., likening it to a leaf vein) reported lower stress scores, whereas those who likened it to a “social judgment symbol” (e.g., a frown) reported higher stress.
- Ethicists raised concerns that the technology could reinforce **algorithmic paternalism** (the device deciding what visual cue is “best” for the user), potentially infringing on cognitive autonomy.
Using Woolf’s secondary themes, concepts from cognitive psychology (attention, mindfulness), neuro‑ethics, and design ethics, answer the sub‑parts below.

(D) Propose a design modification that leverages the secondary theme “solace found in nature’s continuity” to reduce anxiety among users who interpret the mark as a social‑judgment symbol, and justify using one concept from design ethics.

AgriFuture Coop runs a vertical farm producing lettuce (L) and fish (F) in an aquaponic system. Resources: 10 000 sq ft of stacked growing area (capital), 30 workers (labour) @ ₹ 600/day, and 5 000 L of nutrient‑rich water (biological input). Each sq ft yields 0.2 kg lettuce/day or supports 0.05 kg fish/day (if allocated to fish tanks). The coop can sell lettuce at ₹ 40/kg and fish at ₹ 250/kg. Nutrient water recycling efficiency is 80 % (20 % loss per cycle). The coop must decide (i) what mix of lettuce, fish, and mushrooms to produce, (ii) whether to use labour‑intensive harvesting (requires 2 workers/1 000 sq ft) or capital‑intensive automated conveyors (requires 1 conveyor/500 sq ft costing ₹ 3 lakh), and (iii) how to distribute output between local (₹ 35/kg lettuce, ₹ 220/kg fish) and premium (₹ 45/kg lettuce, ₹ 280/kg fish) markets.

(B) Compute the angle φ between the line‑of‑sight vector û and the antenna normal n̂.

The Ministry of Health is designing a “National Climate‑Smart Nutrition Program” (NCSNP) for children aged 2‑5 years in rain‑fed agrarian zones. The program must (i) meet ICMR RDAs for energy (1200 kcal), protein (16 g), iron (8 mg), and vitamin A (400 µg RE) per child per day using locally grown foods; (ii) account for projected climate impacts: a 15 % decline in photosynthetic efficiency of C₃ crops (wheat, rice) and a 5 % increase for C₄ crops (millets, sorghum) due to rising temperatures; (iii) allocate land resources optimally: each hectare of C₄ cereal yields 2.5 t of grain (85 % carbohydrate) under current climate, while each hectare of C₃ cereal yields 3.0 t grain (78 % carbohydrate); (iv) ensure meal plans are culturally acceptable, favoring millet‑based dishes; and (v) monitor cost, targeting ≤ ₹8 per child per day.  
As a policy analyst, you must (a) assign the candidate local foods (bajra, jowar, wheat, rice, moong dal, spinach, oil, jaggery) to ICMR food groups, (b) compute the minimum land area (in hectares) required to supply the carbohydrate portion of the RDA assuming only C₄ cereals are used, (c) explain how the altered photosynthetic efficiency shifts the optimal crop mix between C₃ and C₄ groups, (d) evaluate whether the iron RDA can be met without animal sources using the given plant foods, and (e) propose a cost‑effective cooking‑fuel strategy that preserves micronutrients (e.g., using lid‑closed steaming to retain vitamin A).

(E) Propose a cooking‑fuel and method combination that maximizes retention of vitamin A (β‑carotene) in spinach while minimizing fuel consumption, justifying your choice based on heat transfer principles and the thermal degradation kinetics of β‑carotene (first‑order rate constant k = 0.02 min⁻¹ at 100 °C, doubling every 10 °C rise).

After the 2024 Lok Sabha election, no party secures a majority. (E) Draw a parallel between the Weimar Republic’s coalition fragility (historical analogy) and the potential instability of the present Indian coalition, focusing on the role of ideological extremism. A public‑private partnership plans to use the West Coast Canal (NW‑3) for moving liquid chlorine from the Kochi refinery to a fertilizer plant in Mangalore, a distance of 350 km via the canal and connecting road legs. A mid‑size manufacturing firm offers interest‑free loans to employees for skill‑upgradation. The loan amount is ₹1,20,000, repayable in 24 equal monthly installments recovered directly from salary. A 2024 Hindi protest song against digital surveillance, titled “अंधेरे में दीप”, goes viral on social media. The opening verse: “सरकारी निगरानी की आँखें जैसे काँच की शिकारी, हमारे सपनों को टुकड़े‑टुकड़े कर देती हैं।” The chorus repeats: “हमारा संघर्ष एक ज्वाला है, जो अंधेर को जलाकर उजाला लाती है।” Later, the bridge describes: “हर क्लिक की आवाज़ जैसे सीटी की तेज़ फूँक, जो भीड़ के दिलों को धड़काने का काम करती है।” The song’s metadata shows it was shared 2.3 million times in 48 hours, with peak engagement in metropolitan areas having >60 % youth (18‑25) population density.  
Students must: (a) identify the visual and auditory imagery in the opening line and chorus, (b) unpack the metaphor of “ज्वाला” (flame) for struggle, (c) explain how the imagery amplifies arousal and identity fusion per crowd‑psychology models, and (d) relate the song’s viral spread to social‑movement resource‑mobilization theory, considering digital‑network metrics.

A Wheatstone bridge uses a nichrome wire as the unknown resistance R₄ in arm DA. The ratio arms are R₁ = 100 Ω and R₂ = 200 Ω (fixed). The Government of India aims to provide 100 Mbps broadband connectivity to all 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) under the BharatNet project by 2026.
