A large conglomerate announces a CSR initiative to construct 200 000 affordable housing units in the peri‑urban zone of Pune over seven years. The project expects to house 600 000 net rural‑to‑urban migrants (average household size 3.2). Current Pune metropolitan urban share (2021) is 34.5% of Maharashtra’s urban population; Maharashtra’s urban population is 50.8 million, giving Pune ≈17.5 million urban residents. The city’s natural increase rate is BR = 18, DR = 5 per 1 000. Reclassification of surrounding villages as census towns is anticipated to add 0.25% to the urban share per year due to spill‑over effects. The housing project requires an upfront capital outlay of ₹5,000 crore, financed through equity (30%) and debt (70%) at 8% annual interest. Expected annual rental income from occupied units is ₹600 crore, with operating expenses at 20% of rental income. Depreciation is straight‑line over 20 years.  
Using this information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(E) Estimate the change in Pune’s urban share of Maharashtra’s total urban population after seven years if the project successfully houses the projected migrants, assuming Maharashtra’s urban population grows at a constant annual rate of 2% (driven by natural increase and other migration) and no other changes in Pune’s boundaries.

Fill in the blank: Imagine standing in the ______ Ghats during monsoon — the air is thick with moisture, water drips from leaves even without rain, and the forest floor is dim because the canopy blocks 95% of sunlight.

A wildlife NGO, “SaveStripe”, plans a fundraising campaign using the legend of the Tiger King to solicit donations for tiger reserves in the Satpura‑Maikal landscape. The NGO’s briefing note provides the following data: Pratibandapuram (fictional) is approximated at 22.5° N, 78.0° E, located in a tropical dry deciduous forest zone with mean annual rainfall of 1200 mm, teak and sal as dominant flora, and a prey base of chital and sambar at 25 animals/km². Human population density in the surrounding districts is 150 persons/km², with a history of 12 tiger‑related conflict incidents per year. The NGO must decide whether to (i) highlight the literal geographic facts to establish credibility, (ii) infer the suitability of this habitat for a viable tiger population based on prey density and forest cover, (iii) analyze the symbolic role of the tiger in the story, (iv) calculate the minimum forest area needed to support a breeding tiger pair (assuming 500 kg of meat per tiger per year and 200 kg of usable meat per chital), and (v) assess local attitudes using a recent sociological survey showing 60 % view tigers as a threat, 30 % as a cultural symbol, and 10 % as a conservation priority.  
Based solely on this scenario, answer the sub‑parts below.

(D) Using the prey base data, calculate the minimum forest area (in km²) required to support one breeding tiger pair (male + female) for one year, assuming each tiger needs 500 kg of meat annually and each chital provides 200 kg of usable meat.

In FY20 (2019‑20) India imported semiconductors worth USD 2.1 billion, mainly from Taiwan and South Korea. By FY23 (2022‑23) this rose to USD 5.4 billion due to the Production‑Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for fabs. Over the same period, India’s pharma exports to the USA grew from USD 4.8 billion to USD 6.2 billion. Total merchandise imports increased from USD 450 billion (FY20) to USD 610 billion (FY23); exports rose from USD 300 billion to USD 420 billion. A new FTA with ASEAN, effective FY24, cuts tariffs on electronic components by 30 %. The average price elasticity of demand for imported electronic components is –0.8. India’s major container port (Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust) presently handles 10 million TEUs at 70 % utilisation. A WTO dispute panel has ruled that India’s export subsidies on textiles violate WTO rules; if upheld, partner countries may impose a retaliatory tariff of 5 % on Indian textile exports.

(C) Assuming the ASEAN FTA reduces tariffs on electronic components by 30 % and price elasticity of demand is –0.8, estimate the percentage change in quantity of electronic component imports from ASEAN.

A wearable health‑monitor records the electromyographic (EMG) signal from a muscle fiber. The signal is modeled as a sinusoidal current I(t) = I₀ sin(2πft) with peak amplitude I₀ = 5.0 µA and frequency f = 200 Hz. This current passes through the moving coil of a galvanometer identical to that in Seed 1 (N = 200, A = 2.0 cm², B = 0.5 T, k = 2.0×10⁻⁴ N·m rad⁻¹). The coil’s resistance is R = 12 Ω (assumed temperature‑independent for simplicity). The galvanometer is shunted with a resistor Rₛ to convert it into a micro‑ammeter capable of measuring the RMS value of the EMG current.  

Using τ = NIAB, kφ = τ, and the shunt relation I_total = I_G + I_S (where I_G is coil current, I_S shunt current), answer the following.

(E) If the muscle fires in bursts of duration 5 ms repeating every 50 ms, compute the average power dissipated in the coil over one cycle.

A national health ministry partners with NGOs to implement “Anemia‑Free Villages” in 80 districts. Each district receives iron‑folic acid (IFA) tablets, nutrition education, and deworming kits. Biological baseline: mean hemoglobin (Hb) = 10.2 g/dL (SD = 1.5) in women aged 15‑49; target after 12 months: ≥ 11.5 g/dL. Process monitoring tracks: (i) tablets distributed (monthly), (ii) attendance at counseling sessions, (iii) stock‑out incidents, (iv) expenditure on procurement and logistics. At month 6, a concurrent financial audit reveals that 15 % of the budget was spent on transportation due to remote terrain, while only 60 % of planned tablets reached end‑users because of stock‑outs. At month 12, an external evaluation measures Hb, conducts cost‑effectiveness analysis (incremental cost per g/dL Hb gain), and assesses sustainability via community ownership scores. Identify the M&E components, classify the financial and biological indicators, and evaluate whether the program met its output and outcome targets.

(C) Which biological concept explains why iron‑folic acid supplementation raises hemoglobin levels?

In 1975, a village dairy cooperative society (DCS) in Kaira district collects 500 litres/day from 200 members. The district union pays ₹4.50/litre (fat-corrected). The DCS incurs ₹0.50/litre for transport, ₹0.30/litre for testing/staff, and retains ₹0.20/litre for building corpus. Calculate the net price per litre received by a member who supplies 3 litres/day with 4.5% fat (standard fat = 4%). If the same farmer sold to a local trader at ₹3.50/litre flat rate, what is his daily gain from the cooperative?

A chemist prepares an azo dye by coupling diazonium salt of p‑nitroaniline (generated in situ from p‑nitroaniline, NaNO₂, HCl at 0‑5 °C) with N,N‑dimethylaniline (DMA) in alkaline medium (pH ≈ 9). The coupling follows pseudo‑first‑order kinetics with respect to diazonium concentration (k_obs = 2.5 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ at 25 °C). The dye’s absorbance at λ_max = 480 nm follows Beer‑Lambert law (ε = 1.8 × 10⁴ L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹). After 10 min of reaction, the absorbance is measured as 0.72 in a 1 cm cuvette. Assuming the initial concentration of p‑nitroaniline was 2.0 × 10⁻³ M and that diazonium formation is quantitative and instantaneous, determine (a) the rate constant k (true second‑order) if DMA is in large excess (10 × [diazonium]₀), (b) the concentration of unreacted diazonium after 10 min, and (c) whether the observed absorbance matches the predicted concentration of product. Discuss how electron‑withdrawing nitro group on the diazonium moiety influences both the diazonium stability (via resonance) and the coupling rate (via electrophilicity).

(D) Predict the absorbance of the azo dye product after 10 min assuming that each diazonium molecule that reacts yields one dye molecule (1:1 stoichiometry) and that the product’s ε at 480 nm is 1.8 × 10⁴ L mol⁻¹ cm⁻¹. Compare with the measured absorbance of 0.72.

In March 2025 a commodities trading desk launched a marketing campaign titled “सुनहरा मक्का, लाभ की फसल” (Golden Maize, Harvest of Profit), borrowing the metaphor of golden maize from the poem “मक्क” to promote maize‑futures contracts. The campaign claimed that the poem’s imagery of maize turning “golden” under the sun predicts a imminent price surge due to anticipated monsoon shortfall. Analysts from the Ministry of Economics noted that the campaign coincided with a 7 % rise in maize‑futures open interest and a 0.4 % increase in spot prices over two weeks. Behavioral psychologists warned that the metaphor could trigger the *representativeness heuristic*, leading traders to overestimate price moves based on superficial similarity. Students must: identify the literal metaphor in the poem, infer its intended financial implication, apply concepts of cognitive bias to assess trader behavior, interpret the market data to evaluate the campaign’s impact, and construct a nuanced argument weighing poetic license against market manipulation risk, using a PEEL framework with at least two textual and two data‑based evidences.

(E) Construct a PEEL argument weighing poetic license against market‑manipulation risk, using (i) the literal metaphor from the poem, (ii) its inferential financial implication, (iii) the cognitive‑bias analysis, and (iv) the market‑data evaluation as evidence. Conclude whether regulators should treat the campaign as permissible expression or potential misleading advertisement.

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has approved a pilot smart city project, **“Aarav Nagar”**, to be developed on the floodplain of the River Mahanadi in Chhattisgarh. The proposed site spans **25 km²**, currently comprising three revenue villages with a combined population of **18 000** (2023 Census). The state government projects an influx of **2.2 lakh** residents over the next 15 years due to IT‑park and logistics‑hub incentives. The project must comply with the **74th Constitutional Amendment**, which mandates constitution of Municipal Corporations with elected councils, and allocate at least **30 %** of the municipal budget to infrastructure services. Preliminary hydrological studies indicate a **1‑in‑20‑year** flood risk, necessitating elevated platforms and storm‑water drainage design. The finance department estimates a **per‑capita annual expenditure of ₹12 000** for core services (water, sanitation, solid waste, street lighting). As a geography analyst, you are tasked to (i) classify the existing settlement and the projected urban agglomeration using Census of India criteria, (ii) determine the appropriate urban local body structure, (iii) compute the required annual municipal revenue, (iv) assess flood vulnerability in relation to settlement location, and (v) recommend policy measures linking urbanisation trends and the Smart Cities Mission.

(D) Using the concept of flood risk (1 in 20 year flood), explain why locating the smart city on the floodplain increases vulnerability, and propose two mitigation measures that align with the Smart Cities Mission guidelines.

SolarTech Pvt. Ltd. manufactures solar panels. During FY 2023‑24 it reports:  
- Total value of output (at market price) = ₹ 50 crore.  
- Intermediate consumption: purchase of silicon wafers ₹ 20 crore, electricity ₹ 2 crore, packaging material ₹ 1 crore.  
- Self‑consumption: 5 % of its output is used for lighting its own office (valued at market price).  
- Imputed rent for the owned factory building = ₹ 1.5 crore per year.  
- Sale of second‑hand machinery = ₹ 0.5 crore (treated as a financial transaction).  
- Purchase of equity shares of another firm = ₹ 3 crore (pure financial asset).  
- Depreciation on plant & machinery = ₹ 4 crore.  
- Indirect taxes (excise duty) on output = ₹ 3 crore.  
- Government subsidy per unit produced = ₹ 1 crore (lump‑sum).  
- Net factor income from abroad (NFIA) = +₹ 0.8 crore (inflow).  

Assume no change in inventories and that all values are at market price unless stated otherwise. Using the Value Added Method, compute the contribution of SolarTech to national income and identify the necessary journal entries for self‑consumption and purchase of intermediate goods.

(B) Derive Net Domestic Product at Market Price (NDPmp) from GVAMP by adjusting for depreciation.

To curb reliance on imported solar photovoltaic (PV) modules, India raises the basic customs duty on solar cells from 10 % to 40 % and introduces a ₹15 000 crore Production Linked Incentive (PLI) for domestic module manufacturers. The policy targets an annual domestic capacity addition of 25 GW by 2027. Data shows that before the duty hike, 85 % of modules installed in India were imported (mainly from China and Vietnam). After one year, domestic module production rises from 2 GW/year to 8 GW/year, while imports fall to 60 % of total installations. The southern states (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh) host 55 % of the new domestic capacity due to existing electronics clusters, whereas the northeastern states receive <2 % of the allocation. Environmental groups warn that accelerated mining for silica and rare earths in tribal areas may exacerbate ecological degradation. Using the concepts of economic nationalism, deindustrialisation, and federal resource distribution, evaluate the policy’s socio‑economic and environmental implications.

(D) Using informal labour sociology, assess the likely impact of the DRS on the occupational health of informal e‑waste workers, assuming that a shift of 30 % of their workload to formal channels reduces exposure to hazardous acid leaching by 40 % but increases ergonomic strain due to increased transportation distances by 20 %.

The Government of India approved a semiconductor fabrication plant in Sanand taluka, Gujarat, with an investment of INR 1,20,000 crore. The plant is expected to create 1,50,000 direct jobs over a five‑year construction and operational phase (2024‑2029). Currently, Sanand taluka has a population of 2,00,000 spread over 500 km². Anticipated labor inflow includes 60,000 workers from within Ahmedabad district (intra‑district), 50,000 from neighboring Rajasthan (inter‑state), and 40,000 from Madhya Pradesh (inter‑state). Push factors in the source regions comprise recurring drought, declining agricultural wages, and limited non‑farm employment. Pull factors are the high‑skill wages (average INR 25,000 per month) and housing subsidies offered by the state. The fab’s water requirement is estimated at 20 million cubic metres per year, drawing from the Narmada basin, which has triggered a water‑sharing dispute between Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh under the Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal (a civics‑power‑sharing issue). The state government has earmarked INR 5,000 crore as capital subsidy and projects cumulative tax revenue of INR 8,000 crore over the subsequent decade.

(C) Using a push‑pull framework, identify two push factors and two pull factors influencing migration to the semiconductor plant, and explain how the Narmada water‑sharing dispute acts as a push factor.

A national streaming platform commissions a live‑telecast debate titled “English vs. Regional Languages: The Future of Indian Education”. The virtual studio replicates the setting of *Broken Images*: a massive plasma screen displays real‑time Twitter trends, a semi‑circular ‘telly’ table holds tablets showing language‑usage statistics, and a row of muted monitors in the background streams archival footage of 1960s language riots. The host, Manjula (mid‑30s, fluent in Kannada and English), wears a lapel mic and a red “ON AIR” bulb glows above the table. Prior to going live, the director cues a countdown; the plasma screen flickers showing a T. S. Eliot line: “A heap of broken images…”. During the debate, a panelist argues that English is a colonial lingua‑franca that unlocks global opportunities, while another counters that privileging English erodes indigenous knowledge systems. The studio lighting shifts from cool blue (neutral) to warm amber when the discussion turns to cultural identity, and the plasma screen intermittently freezes on images of protest signs in Devanagari and Kannada scripts. The audience (both live and 2.3 million online viewers) sees the host’s reflected image split between the plasma screen and a monitor showing a Karnataka folk‑dance troupe. The director later notes that the red bulb stayed on for 17 seconds longer than scheduled, unintentionally highlighting the host’s strained smile.

(A) Identify two specific stage directions from the scenario that establish the television‑studio setting and explain how each contributes to the atmosphere of technological surveillance.

A brass rod (K = 109 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) of length 20 cm and cross-section 2 cm² is joined to a steel rod (K = 50 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) of length 30 cm and cross-section 3 cm². The free end of brass is at 120°C and the free end of steel is at 20°C. Calculate the heat current through the combination and the temperature at the junction.

A pharmaceutical company synthesizes the ketone intermediate **4‑phenyl‑2‑butanone** (used in an antihypertensive agent) via the dialkylcadmium route: benzoyl chloride (C₆H₅COCl) reacts with dimethylcadmium [(CH₃)₂Cd] to give the ketone after eliminating CdCl₂. The reaction is performed in anhydrous THF at –78 °C to avoid over‑addition (which would give a tertiary alcohol). The plant has 2.00 kg of benzoyl chloride and excess dimethylcadmium. Cadmium waste is toxic; regulations limit Cd²⁺ discharge to 0.1 ppm in effluent. Students must (i) calculate the theoretical ketone yield, (ii) determine the mass of CdCl₂ waste produced, (iii) assess whether the waste concentration meets the limit assuming a 500 L aqueous wash, (ii) model the reaction rate as pseudo‑first‑order in acyl chloride (k = 2.5×10⁻³ s⁻¹) and find the time needed for 95 % conversion, and (iv) discuss how temperature affects both rate and side‑reaction probability using Arrhenius parameters (Eₐ = 45 kJ mol⁻¹ for desired path, Eₐ,side = 70 kJ mol⁻¹ for over‑addition). Cross‑subject links: chemistry (acyl chloride + CdR₂), math (exponential decay, solving for time), biology (toxicity thresholds), physics (Arrhenius equation, temperature dependence).

(D) Using the Arrhenius equation, estimate the ratio of rate constants k_desired/k_side at –78 °C (195 K) given Eₐ,desired = 45 kJ mol⁻¹ and Eₐ,side = 70 kJ mol⁻¹, assuming equal pre‑exponential factors.

A state education department aims to reduce physical aggression among middle‑school students in three districts: District X (highly urban, 80% migrant labour children), District Y (semi‑urban, mixed caste composition), and District Z (rural, predominantly agrarian families). Preliminary surveys reveal that students scoring high on the 16PF factor **Vigilance** (suspiciousness) and low on **Rule‑Consciousness** tend to exhibit more aggressive incidents. The department proposes a two‑pronged intervention: (1) Social‑Emotional Learning (SEL) modules targeting self‑regulation, and (2) Restorative‑justice circles informed by local cultural norms. Using Allport’s secondary traits, Cattell’s source‑surface framework, self‑efficacy, cultural self‑construal (individualistic vs collectivist), and cross‑subject insights from sociology (caste‑based stratification), political science (state education policy under Article 21A), and geography (urban‑rural migration patterns), answer the following.

(E) Propose a policy evaluation framework that integrates (i) quantitative trait‑based pre‑post measures, (ii) qualitative sociological focus groups, and (iii) geographical mapping of incident hotspots, citing how each component satisfies validity and fairness criteria (referencing c12_pol_cbse_01_001, c12_soc_cbse_01_002, c12_geo_cbse_01_004).

Build a "Product Comparison" snippet for two smartphones. Requirements: (1) Main heading "Smartphone Comparison 2024", (2) Two product sections each with model name as subheading, (3) In each, show price with `<del>` old price and `<ins>` new price, (4) Highlight "5G ready" with `<mark>`, (5) Show battery capacity as 5000 mAh with "mAh" as subscript? Actually mAh is a unit, not subscript. Better: show chemical formula for lithium-ion battery: LiCoO₂. (6) Add a footnote reference¹ for "prices subject to change" using `<sup>`. (7) Use `<small>` for the footnote text at bottom.

The Ministry of Rural Development wants to evaluate the effectiveness of MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act) in reducing rural poverty in State X. They have block-level data for 50 blocks over 3 years: (1) Person-days of employment generated per household, (2) Percentage of households below poverty line (BPL), (3) Average agricultural wage rate. Describe the specific statistical application used at each stage: (a) Calculating the state-level average person-days from block data, (b) Finding if blocks with higher person-days show lower BPL percentage, (c) Predicting next year's BPL percentage if person-days are increased by 20%, (d) Presenting the finding to the Cabinet in a one-page note.

In Varanasi, handloom units generate ~12 kg of cotton scrap per loom per month. A new state “Zero Waste Textiles” policy (aligned with UN SDG 12) mandates 50% reduction in textile waste by 2026. Preliminary surveys show: 70% of weavers are unaware of recycling options; 40% believe scrap has no market value; social norm data indicates that 60% would adopt recycling if peers do. The extension team has ₹1,80,000, 2 technical experts, and access to a community radio station. They must select appropriate communication media, set measurable targets, and evaluate using both output (kg diverted) and outcome (income change) indicators.

(A) Calculate the monthly cotton scrap generated by 150 looms and the target reduction mass under the policy.

BioNova Inc., a biotech startup, has just received FDA fast‑track approval for its CRISPR‑based therapy “CureX” that treats a rare genetic disorder. The therapy is priced at **$150,000 per dose**. At this price, the firm expects to sell **200 doses per month**.  
Simultaneously, a rival firm launches a substitute therapy priced at **$130,000 per dose**. The CFO must record the **$12 million** of R&D incurred during the trial phase under GAAP, deciding whether to expense or capitalize the cost. The finance team wants to estimate the **price elasticity of demand** using the midpoint formula to evaluate a potential 10 % price cut. Assume all other determinants (income, tastes, number of buyers) remain unchanged except for the FDA approval (which raises expectations) and the rival’s price (a substitute).

(B) Using the midpoint formula, calculate the price elasticity of demand for CureX if the price is reduced from $150,000 to $135,000 and the quantity demanded rises from 200 to 260 doses per month.
A company declares a 12% dividend. A student calculates income on 500 shares of face value ₹10 as 12% of (500 × market price ₹25) = ₹1,500. Is this correct? Explain why or why not.

A satellite‑based quantum key distribution (QKD) system encodes binary bits onto the phase ϕ of single‑photon pulses transmitted from a low‑Earth‑orbit transmitter to a ground receiver. The encoding follows the map  
\[
ϕ(b_1,b_2)=\frac{\pi}{4}\bigl(2b_1+b_2\bigr),\qquad b_1,b_2\in\{0,1\},
\]
so that the four possible phase states are {0, π/4, π/2, 3π/4}.  
The transmitter’s internal clock drifts linearly with temperature: the actual emitted phase is ϕ′=ϕ+δ(t), where δ(t)=γ·(T(t)−T₀), T(t)=T₀+ΔT sin(ωt) is the temperature variation (°C), γ=0.05 rad/°C, ΔT=2 °C, ω=2π/24 h⁻¹, and T₀=20 °C.  
The receiver applies a temperature‑compensating phase shift −δ(t) before measurement. However, due to finite electronics bandwidth, the compensation is effective only for |δ(t)|≤δ_max, where δ_max=0.2 rad. Outside this window the receiver applies a fixed shift −δ_max·sgn(δ(t)).  
The overall transformation from input bits (b₁,b₂) to detected phase ψ after compensation must be (i) injective (different bit‑pairs give different ψ), (ii) surjective onto the set of distinguishable phase bins used by the receiver (four bins of width π/2 centered at 0,π/4,π/2,3π/4), (iii) invertible to recover bits from ψ, (iv) composable with a classical error‑correction function *E*(ψ)=⌊ψ/(π/4)⌋ mod 4 (which maps ψ to an integer 0‑3), and (v) still bijective when the temperature amplitude ΔT is increased to 5 °C (testing robustness).

(C) Assuming ΔT is increased to 5 °C (so that γ·ΔT=0.25 rad>δ_max), derive the piecewise expression for ψ(t) and determine the set of possible detected phases.

A student writes the following algorithm for the kirana store problem: "Input prices. Calculate total. If total > 500, give 10% discount. Add 5% GST. Print final amount." Identify two missing details that would cause incorrect results when coded.

A biotech firm has developed a transgenic wheat line (WT‑DREB2) that overexpresses a dehydration‑responsive element‑binding protein, conferring 30 % yield increase under water‑stress conditions. Before open‑field release, the company must design a public engagement strategy addressing: (i) farmers in semi‑arid Punjab (low literacy, rely on radio), (ii) urban consumers concerned about allergenicity (high internet usage, prefer infographics), (iii) policymakers needing biosafety data (require quantitative risk models), and (iv) NGOs monitoring gene flow to wild relatives (need spatial‑temporal dispersal models). The firm provides: (a) pollen dispersal data showing a Gaussian spread with σ = 12 m; (b) in‑vitro protein digestibility assay indicating 95 % similarity to native wheat allergen profile; (c) a chemical kinetic model for degradation of the novel protein in soil (first‑order, k = 0.025 day⁻¹); (d) a survey of 500 urban respondents showing 62 % acceptance when presented with a risk‑benefit infographic versus 38 % with raw data. Using this information, devise an engagement plan that selects appropriate communication formats, establishes feedback loops, and quantifies expected outreach effectiveness.

(A) Calculate the effective half‑life (in days) of the transgenic protein in soil using the given first‑order degradation constant k = 0.025 day⁻¹.

A government press release states: "The country's GDP grew by 7.2% in 2023-24. Agriculture grew by 3.5%, Industry by 8.1%, and Services by 7.8%. In the previous year, overall GDP growth was 6.8%, with Agriculture at 4.2%, Industry at 7.5%, and Services at 7.0%." (a) Present this data in a clear table with appropriate title, stubs, captions, and unit of measurement. (b) Explain why the textual presentation makes it difficult to answer: "Which sector contributed most to the acceleration in GDP growth?" (c) Suggest one diagrammatic form that would best highlight the sectoral growth changes.

The Ministry of Rural Development maintains an **EMPLOYEE** table (`emp_id PK`, `name`, `grade`, `basic_salary`, `da_percent`, `hra`, `state_code`, `last_appraisal`). A new pay‑commission report mandates: (i) increase `basic_salary` by 12% for all employees in grades 10‑12 whose `state_code` belongs to a list of drought‑affected states (provided in table **DROUGHT_STATE**(`state_code`)); (ii) set `hra` to 20% of the revised `basic_salary` for those same employees; (iii) remove duplicate entries where the same `emp_id` appears more than once (keep the row with the latest `last_appraisal` timestamp). The ministry also needs to know how many rows will receive the salary hike and how many duplicate rows will be removed before performing the actions.

(B) Using an aggregate function, write a SELECT statement that returns the number of employees who will receive the salary hike (same criteria as Part A).

A team of aerospace engineers is designing a passive electrostatic dust‑mitigation system for the solar panels of a Mars rover. The panels are coated with a thin transparent conductive layer (indium tin oxide) held at a controllable potential V_p relative to the Martian ground (considered an infinite conducting plane at zero potential). Dust particles (silica spheres, radius 1 µm, acquired charge ±5e due to triboelectric charging) experience an electrostatic force **F** = q**E** that can lift them off the surface if the upward force exceeds their weight (effective weight on Mars: m·g_Mars, g_Mars = 3.71 m/s²). The engineers model the panel as a finite circular disc of radius R = 10 cm, biased at V_p = +200 V, positioned a distance d = 2 mm above the ground. They need to ensure that (i) field lines from the panel terminate on the ground without crossing, (ii) the field line density directly yields the lift force on a particle, and (iii) the field does not exhibit local maxima that could cause particle redistribution rather than removal.  
Students must derive the vertical electric field just above the panel surface using the method of images for a disc above a plane, evaluate whether a typical dust particle will be lifted, and discuss how the field line representation guarantees the correctness of the force calculation.

(D) Explain why the electric field lines from the disc must terminate on the ground plane without forming any closed loops.
Explain in your own words why the setting of a "London suburb in the 1950s" is crucial to understanding the conflict in "Mother's Day".

In mid‑2025, India and Bangladesh resume talks over the sharing of the Teesta River’s dry‑season flow. Bangladesh argues that India’s upstream barrages, built after the 1972 Indo‑Bangladesh Treaty of Friendship, have reduced downstream flow by 30 % during March‑May, threatening its boro rice harvest. India cites its own agricultural needs in West Bengal and Assam, referencing the 1996 Ganges Treaty as a model for equitable sharing. The negotiations are framed within India’s “Neighbourhood First” policy, but security analysts warn that water scarcity could fuel insurgent recruitment in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, a region with historical ties to separatist movements. The Ministry of External Affairs asks the Policy Planning Division to draft a brief that (i) references the historical water‑management practices of ancient Mesopotamian city‑states (c11_hist_cbse_01_009) to argue for cooperative basin management, (ii) evaluates the economic impact on India’s agricultural GDP using input‑output tables, and (iii) proposes a confidence‑building measure (CBM) involving joint hydrological data sharing, to be overseen by a SAARC‑affiliated technical committee. The Finance Ministry simultaneously requests a cost estimate for installing real‑time flow‑monitoring stations along the border, to be reflected in the next fiscal year’s budget.

(B) The Ministry of Agriculture provides an input‑output coefficient: a 10 % reduction in Teesta water availability lowers West Bengal’s boro rice output by 4 % and Assam’s by 2 %. If the current combined boro rice contribution to agricultural GDP is ₹ 1,80,000 crore, estimate the loss in agricultural GDP due to a 30 % water‑flow reduction.

A youth‑led online campaign "#SpeakSilent" releases posters showing a cracked pen nib whose ink drips to form a chain. The tagline reads “Speak freely, but stay silent”. The campaign protests recent internet shutdowns in a state during demonstrations, invoking Article 19 of the Constitution. The cracked pen symbolises suppressed expression; the ink chain represents the link between speech and democratic rights. Historically, similar imagery (broken typewriter) appeared during the 1975‑77 Emergency press censorship. Students must identify the verbal irony in the tagline, decode the two symbols, explain how irony and symbolism jointly reinforce the critique of shutdowns, compare the campaign with Emergency‑era posters, and evaluate its impact using supplied awareness data.

(E) The campaign reached 2.5 million impressions. A pre‑campaign survey showed 22 % awareness of Article 19 among 18‑25‑year‑olds; post‑campaign awareness rose to 38 %. Calculate the absolute increase (in percentage points) and the relative increase (in percent) in awareness.
Fill in the blank: Imagine a 32-year-old woman in Delhi who has been trying to conceive for 18 months with regular ______ intercourse — she represents the 1 in 6 Indian couples facing infertility.

IndicSoft, a Bengaluru‑based artificial‑intelligence startup, was founded in 2010 by visionary entrepreneur Arvind Nehru, who built the company into a market leader with a 45% share in the domestic AI‑analytics sector. Arvind died unexpectedly in 2023 after a prolonged illness, leaving a 60% equity stake held by a trust controlled by the founding senior team (the 'Syndicate') comprising the CTO, CFO, and Head of Sales. The incumbent CEO, Priya Gandhi, Arvind’s protégé, holds the remaining 40% and has cultivated a loyal base among junior engineers and regional clients. The company’s Articles of Association require a board vote to appoint a new Chairperson; the Syndicate backs their senior vice‑president, Neelam Reddy, while Priya proposes supporting an independent industry expert, V. V. Giri, as a consensus candidate. She invites board members to vote according to their conscience, bypassing the Syndicate’s official slate. The vote results in a narrow win for Giri, prompting the Syndicate to convene an extraordinary general meeting and expel Priya from the board for violating party discipline. Simultaneously, the company’s auditors flag discrepancies in the financial statements because the Syndicate‑controlled trust had not disclosed related‑party transactions, raising concerns about transparency and accountability.

(A) In the IndicSoft scenario, after the founder's death, the Syndicate's attempt to impose their preferred chairperson mirrors which concept from the Congress split of 1969?

A business in Delhi must pay ₹12 lakh to a vendor in Chennai today. The vendor insists on immediate credit confirmation. Compare NEFT, RTGS, and a demand draft on: (a) settlement finality time, (b) maximum amount limit, (c) availability on a Sunday. Recommend the best option with justification.

In 2024, a 22‑year‑old woman from a small village in Bundelkhand accepts a software‑testing job in Bengaluru. Her father records a short farewell video on his smartphone, showing her packing a trunk while he recites a couplet from the poem “Lajja ka Lekh.” The video is uploaded to a regional language platform and receives 2.3 million views within 48 hours. Comments praise the father’s emotion, criticize the lack of local industry, and demand better skill‑development schemes. A state politician cites the clip in a debate on the “Migration Relief Bill,” arguing that outward migration from agrarian districts weakens food security. Simultaneously, a geography researcher uses satellite‑derived NDVI data to show a 15 % decline in cropland vigor in the father’s district over the past decade, linking it to water‑stress‑induced out‑migration.  
Using this scenario, students must (i) extract secondary themes from the poem (e.g., societal expectations, economic pressure, cultural identity), (ii) trace how these themes intersect with the father’s grief, and (iii) connect the poem’s concerns to historical migration trends post‑1991 liberalisation, contemporary political discourse on migrant workers’ rights, and geographical push‑factors such as declining agricultural productivity.

(C) Identify one literary device (imagery or metaphor) used to convey the secondary theme of “cultural identity and tradition” and explain its effect on the reader’s perception of the father’s grief.

DeFiYield LLP, a decentralized finance yield-farming partnership, has four partners: NodeA (30%), NodeB (25%), NodeC (25%), NodeD (20%). Partnership deed encoded as Ethereum smart contract (governed by Indian Partnership Act 1932 read with IT Act 2000): (i) Goodwill = 2.5 × (Super-profit + Option value of governance tokens). Super-profit = Average profit - Normal return (12% on capital employed). Option value = Black-Scholes value of unissued governance tokens (volatility 80%, risk-free 6%, life 3 years, strike = current token price). (ii) On retirement/death, outgoing partner's goodwill share settled via token transfer (valued at 30-day VWAP) + stablecoin. (iii) JLP: ₹10Cr sum assured each, premium paid in ETH, policy on-chain with parametric trigger (oracle). Surrender value = 90% of premiums paid in ETH valued at death/retirement date. (iv) Revaluation of crypto-assets at fair value (CoinGecko 24h average). (v) Accumulated profits in stablecoin distributed in old ratio. (vi) Continuing partners' capitals adjusted in new ratio via token minting/burning.  

Events: NodeC retires 30-Sep-2026. NodeD dies 15-Oct-2026. Firm continues with NodeA, NodeB. New profit-sharing ratio 6:4 (capital ratio after revaluation at 30-Sep).  

As on 31-Mar-2026 (last audited):  
- Capitals: NodeA 5000 ETH, NodeB 4000 ETH, NodeC 3000 ETH, NodeD 2400 ETH (1 ETH = ₹2,00,000)  
- Stablecoin reserves: 20M USDC (1 USDC = ₹83)  
- Governance tokens: 1M tokens unissued, current price ₹500, volatility 80%, risk-free 6%, life 3 years, strike ₹500.  
- Crypto-assets: BTC 100 (book ₹30L each, fair ₹50L), ETH 2000 (book ₹2L, fair ₹2.5L), DeFi tokens 500k (book ₹100, fair ₹120)  
- Liabilities: Stablecoin borrowings 10M USDC; Smart contract debt 500 ETH  
- Average annual profit (stablecoin) 5M USDC. Capital employed (book) = Total assets book - Liabilities book.  
- JLP: Premiums paid 200 ETH per partner (total 800 ETH). Surrender value = 90% of premiums in ETH at current ETH price.  
- Exchange rates: 30-Sep-2026: 1 ETH = ₹2,20,000, 1 USDC = ₹83.5; 15-Oct-2026: 1 ETH = ₹2,15,000, 1 USDC = ₹83.2.  

Assume Black-Scholes value of option = ₹120 per token. Normal return 12% on capital employed (book in INR).

(C) Journalise JLP on NodeC retirement (30-Sep) and NodeD death (15-Oct). Policies surrendered. Compute surrender value in INR at each date.

Given the following data for average monthly rainfall (cm) in Mumbai: Jan 0.2, Feb 0.1, Mar 0.1, Apr 0.1, May 1.2, Jun 48.5, Jul 61.2, Aug 36.9, Sep 26.9, Oct 4.8, Nov 1.0, Dec 0.2. Construct a line graph on graph paper (1 cm = 1 month on X‑axis, 1 cm = 10 cm rainfall on Y‑axis). What is the approximate slope of the line segment between June and July, and what does it represent?

A researcher surveys 100 families in a village and finds: (1) 80% of upper-caste families have at least one member with a college degree, vs 15% of Dalit families. (2) Average landholding: upper-caste 4.2 hectares, Dalit 0.3 hectares. (3) 90% of upper-caste marriages are within caste; 85% of Dalit marriages are within caste. Using Bourdieu’s three capitals and the three principles of stratification, explain how these findings demonstrate social stratification (not just inequality).

On Saturn’s moon Titan, lakes of liquid methane/ethane (ε ≈ 2) dissolve acetylene (C₂H₂) which undergoes electrophilic addition of HCl (from atmospheric photochemistry) to give chloro‑ethylene intermediates. Further radical chlorination yields 2‑chloropropane (isopropyl chloride) dissolved in the cryogenic solvent (T ≈ 94 K). This secondary alkyl halide can solvolyze via an SN1 pathway assisted by weak complexes with dissolved N₂ (acting as a Lewis base). The solvolysis rate follows k = k₀ exp[−(Eₐ − ΔE_solv)/RT], where ΔE_solv = 5.0 kJ mol⁻¹ stabilization due to N₂ complexation. In pure methane solvent (no N₂), k₀ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁸ s⁻¹ and Eₐ = 120 kJ mol⁻¹. The dissolved N₂ concentration is 0.15 M, giving a complexation equilibrium K_c = [Complex]/([R‑Cl][N₂]) = 2.0 M⁻¹. Assume only the complexed fraction reacts.  
Students must: (a) compute the fraction of R‑Cl complexed with N₂, (b) determine the effective k at 94 K, (c) calculate the half‑life of 2‑chloropropane in Titan’s lake, (d) assess whether competing SN2 with dissolved ethane (as a very weak nucleophile) is feasible given k₂(SN2) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ and [ethane] ≈ 10 M (pure solvent), and (e) discuss how the low temperature influences stereochemical outcome if the carbon were chiral.  
Cross‑subject links: physical chemistry (thermodynamics), astronomy (planetary science), fluid dynamics (solvent properties).

(D) Assess whether SN2 attack by dissolved ethane (acting as a nucleophile via its C‑H bond) could compete with SN1. Use k₂(SN2) = 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ M⁻¹ s⁻¹ and [ethane] ≈ 10 M (pure solvent). Compute the pseudo‑first‑order SN2 rate constant k_SN2 and compare with k_eff from part B.

In early 2024, a Bengaluru‑based artificial‑intelligence start‑up, “VidhyaAI”, sought to launch a cloud‑based language‑tutoring platform targeting rural students across six states. To operate, the company needed three regulatory clearances: (i) a data‑localisation licence from the Ministry of Electronics and IT (fee ₹12 lakh, renewable yearly), (ii) an education‑content accreditation from the National Council for Educational Research and Training (NCERT) (fee ₹8 lakh, one‑time), and (iii) a telecommunications tower‑sharing permit from the Department of Telecommunications (fee ₹5 lakh per tower, with a minimum of four towers required for pan‑India coverage). The Swatantra Party, revived as a pressure group in 2023, issued a statement likening these requirements to the historic licence‑permit raj, arguing that they imposed sunk costs, created barriers to entry for small innovators, and diverted resources from productive R&D. Simultaneously, a geographic‑information‑system (GIS) analysis showed that the six target states contained 140 million potential users, but only 22 % lived in areas with broadband speeds > 10 Mbps, necessitating either costly satellite‑back‑up (additional ₹20 lakh per state) or reliance on existing tower‑sharing agreements. The Swatantra caucus demanded (i) consolidation of the three clearances into a single digital‑service licence with a flat annual fee of ₹15 lakh, (ii) exemption for start‑ups with turnover < ₹10 crore from the data‑localisation fee, and (iii) mandatory spatial‑cost accounting (per ) to disclose the geographic distribution of compliance expenses. Using the data below, evaluate the Swatantra proposal’s financial impact and its ideological consistency.

- Number of states covered: 6  
- Base compliance cost (data‑localisation + NCERT + tower fees):  
   • Data‑localisation: ₹12 lakh/yr × 6 = ₹72 lakh/yr  
   • NCERT: ₹8 lakh (one‑time)  
   • Tower sharing: ₹5 lakh/tower × 4 towers × 6 states = ₹120 lakh (one‑time)  
- Proposed consolidated licence fee: ₹15 lakh/yr (flat, covers all states)  
- Estimated R&D expenditure if barriers lowered: ₹250 lakh/yr  
- Current R&D expenditure: ₹80 lakh/yr  
- Spatial‑cost accounting implementation cost: ₹4 lakh (one‑time)  
- Expected reduction in compliance cost due to exemption for < ₹10 crore turnover (if VidhyaAI qualifies): 40 % of data‑localisation fee

(B) Assuming VidhyaAI’s turnover is below ₹10 crore and thus qualifies for the 40 % exemption on the data‑localisation fee, calculate the new annual recurring compliance cost (in lakh ₹).

In 2024 a student‑led collective “Bhasha‑Mitra” launches a pan‑India Instagram campaign demanding official recognition for Bhili, a tribal language spoken by ~10 million people across Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Rajasthan and Maharashtra. The campaign’s poster shows two hands clasped—one holding a traditional Bhili drum, the other a smartphone—captioned in Hindi: “समान सम्मान, स्वतंत्र बोल” (Equal respect, free speech). Within 48 hours the post garners 2.3 lakhs likes, 1.1 lakhs shares and attracts a legal notice from the State Education Department alleging violation of the “Three‑Language Formula” under Article 29(2). The collective cites the story “HkfDru” where the protagonists recognize each other’s dignity beyond ownership, arguing that language is an extension of personal autonomy. Using the data:  
- Population of Bhili speakers: 10 million (≈0.75 % of India)  
- Instagram reach: 2.3 lakhs likes, 1.1 lakhs shares  
- Legal basis: Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of expression) and Article 29(2) (protection of minority interests)  
Answer the following sub‑parts.

(E) Propose a two‑point policy recommendation that addresses the campaign’s demand while considering India’s linguistic‑geographic distribution (c12_geo_cbse_10_001) and sociolinguistic inequality (drawing on sociological concepts of language prestige).
If you have a cup of hot coffee and a giant lake, both at 60°C, which one has more heat? Why?

India and Japan announce a joint venture to develop a deep‑water port and renewable‑energy hub on Great Nicobar Island, intending to strengthen maritime surveillance and provide a bunkering facility for Quad navies. The project requires acquisition of 250 ha of forest land, displacing a small Shompen tribal settlement. Within weeks, a sophisticated cyber‑attack disables the port’s automated cargo‑handling system; forensic analysis traces the malware to a server cluster linked to a known Pakistan‑based extremist outfit that has previously targeted Indian financial institutions. Simultaneously, China issues a diplomatic note claiming the project violates its “historical rights” in the South China Sea and warns of potential “counter‑measures”. Domestic Left‑Wing Extremist (LWE) groups call for a blockade, alleging the project will exacerbate deforestation and affect local livelihoods, while a recent IPCC report highlights accelerated sea‑level rise (≈4 mm/yr) threatening the low‑lying coastal infrastructure over the project’s 30‑year lifespan. The Sri Lankan government, invoking its power‑sharing arrangement with Tamil minority parties, demands that any regional maritime security arrangement include explicit safeguards for Tamil fishing interests.

(D) Discuss how cooperative security mechanisms could mitigate the Chinese objection while preserving Quad interests.

A 100-year-old family-owned textile mill in Surat produces standard cotton fabric. The 4th generation heir wants to shift from selling wholesale to launching a D2C brand of "premium organic cotton basics" online. The father insists: "Our strength is low-cost volume production. Stick to what we know." Using the five philosophies, analyze both positions. Which philosophy does each represent? What specific market changes make the heir's shift necessary? What single metric would prove the heir right after 18 months?

A 0.5 kg block of ice at -10°C is dropped into a 1.0 kg copper calorimeter (s = 386 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹) containing 1.5 kg water at 50°C. Find the final state and temperature. (s_ice = 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, L_fusion = 3.34 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹, s_water = 4186 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹)

In March 2024, following Russia’s renewed aggression in Ukraine, Finland and Sweden formally join NATO, extending the Alliance’s northern flank to the Arctic Circle. NATO’s Secretary‑General announces a “Enhanced Deterrence Package” that includes pre‑positioned armoured brigades in Norway, increased air‑policing over the Greenland‑Iceland‑UK (GIUK) gap, and a joint Nordic‑Baltic cyber‑defence centre. Simultaneously, the EU activates its Strategic Compass, pledging rapid‑reaction battlegroups capable of deployment within 5 days and earmarking €80 bn for defence innovation, notably in hypersonic glide vehicles and satellite‑based ISR. ASEAN, wary of being drawn into great‑power contests, reaffirms its Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) and proposes a “Maritime Confidence‑Building Initiative” in the South China Sea, inviting both NATO and China to participate in joint search‑and‑rescue drills. China responds by increasing patrols near the Senkaku/Diaoyu islands and launching a diplomatic outreach to Pacific Island nations, framing its actions as a safeguard of “regional stability.” Scholars debate whether this NATO enlargement revives the Cold‑War policy of containment or represents a new form of collective security adapted to multipolar realities. Students must analyse the legal, strategic and historical dimensions of these moves and their implications for the post‑1991 order.

(A) Identify the legal basis for NATO’s Article 5 collective defence and explain how the accession of Finland and Sweden triggers this provision in the context of Arctic security.

The Government intends to develop National Waterway‑1 (NW‑1) on the Ganga‑Bhagirathi‑Hooghly system from Prayagraj to Haldia (1,620 km) to move 20 million tonnes per annum of coal and fertilizers. A satellite‑based Automatic Identification System (AIS) will provide real‑time vessel tracking, integrated with the existing INSAT‑3DR weather satellite for cyclone warnings. Project cost: ₹18,000 crore (₹12,000 crore for dredging and terminal infrastructure, ₹6,000 crore for AIS‑INSAT integration and control centres). Expected benefits: (i) reduction in CO₂ emissions by 0.45 million tonnes/year compared to rail, (ii) saving of ₹9,000 crore annually in logistics cost for users. The scheme is financed through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) that issues bonds; the centre guarantees 60 % of debt service, states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal) guarantee the remaining 40 % proportionally to their share of the waterway length. Assume length shares: UP = 35 %, Bihar = 25 %, Jharkhand = 15 %, West Bengal = 25 %.

(C) Determine the amount of debt service guaranteed by the centre (60 %) and by each state based on their length share, assuming total annual debt service is ₹1,500 crore.

In 2023, Nigeria’s female labor‑force participation rate stood at 56 % compared to 71 % for men, with cultural expectations citing family honor as a key reason for women’s exit from the workforce after marriage. Adeola, 22, lives in Lagos, works as a junior developer at a fintech startup earning ₦180,000/month, and contributes 70 % of her income to support her younger siblings’ education and her mother’s small trading business. Her father, a retired civil servant, expects her to marry soon and cease work to manage the household. Adeola has received an offer to join a Silicon Valley‑based remote team as a senior engineer with a salary of ₦900,000/month, requiring occasional travel to the U.S. for quarterly meet‑ups. She recalls Eveline’s story: a young woman offered escape with a sailor but bound by a promise to her mother and the weight of paternal authority. Using data on gendered labor expectations, startup culture, and Eveline’s portrayal of patriarchal control, analyse Adeola’s conflict through sociological gender‑role theory, economic opportunity cost, and Eveline’s theme of paternal domination.

(C) Which economic principle clarifies why Adeola might still hesitate despite the large net personal gain?

In 2025 a coalition of space‑faring nations proposes a new UN specialised agency, the **UN Office for Space Debris Mitigation (UNOSDM)**, to monitor, track and actively remove orbital debris. The proposal must be adopted by the General Assembly, receive a recommendation from the Security Council, and be financed through the UN’s assessed contributions scheme. Historian advisors note that the League of Nations once used “mandates” to administer territories, suggesting a precedent for international regulation of a global commons. The UN Secretariat is tasked with drafting the agency’s statute, while ECOSOC will later coordinate its reporting. Using the UN scale of assessments, a country contributing 0.75 % of the UN budget would be expected to finance a proportional share of UNOSDM’s inaugural $120 million budget.

(B) If a permanent member of the Security Council vetoes the recommendation to create UNOSDM, can the General Assembly still establish the agency?

Fill in the blank: The Roman army was a professional, paid standing force requiring 25 years of service, distinct from conscripted armies, which became the largest organised body in the empire (600,000 by the 4th century CE) and a key political player alongside the emperor and the Senate; ______ relied on urbanisation, with cities as the bedrock of imperial control, where local provincial elites collaborated with the Roman state to collect taxes and govern territories, leading to a gradual shift of power from Italian to provincial aristocrats by the 3rd century CE.

A smart‑city initiative in City Y aims to mitigate urban heat island (UHI) effects by increasing green cover. The planning department conducts a field survey across 10 selected neighbourhoods, measuring ambient air temperature (°C) at 1 m height using calibrated thermometers, recording surface material type (asphalt, concrete, vegetation, bare soil), and noting canopy cover percentage. Simultaneously, Landsat‑8 thermal infrared band (10.9 µm) provides land‑surface temperature (LST) at 30 m resolution. The field team uses GPS (±2 m) to geotag each measurement point. In GIS, they create a raster of LST, overlay the point temperature data, and compute the coefficient of determination (R²) between field‑measured air temperature and LST to validate the satellite product. To prioritize interventions, the department allocates a climate‑adaptation fund of ₹4.8 crore, with each hectare of new urban forest costing ₹12 lac (including maintenance for 5 years). Allocation follows a socio‑economic equity criterion: funds are distributed proportional to (population density × proportion of households below poverty line), reflecting the principle of “common but differentiated responsibilities” from environmental governance (linked to political‑science concepts of equity). The accounting unit must track expenditures against the fund and report variances.  

Data:  
- Neighbourhood A: pop 1.2 lac, area 2 km², density 60 000 /km², BPL % = 25  
- B: 0.9 lac, 1.5 km², density 60 000, BPL 20  
- C: 1.5 lac, 3 km², density 50 000, BPL 30  
- D: 0.8 lac, 0.8 km², density 100 000, BPL 15  
- E: 1.1 lac, 2.2 km², density 50 000, BPL 35  
- F: 0.7 lac, 0.7 km², density 100 000, BPL 10  
- G: 1.3 lac, 2.6 km², density 50 000, BPL 28  
- H: 0.6 lac, 0.6 km², density 100 000, BPL 12  
- I: 1.0 lac, 2.0 km², density 50 000, BPL 22  
- J: 0.5 lac, 0.5 km², density 100 000, BPL 8  

Field‑survey results (average air temperature): A = 31.2, B = 30.8, C = 32.5, D = 33.1, E = 32.9, F = 33.4, G = 32.0, H = 33.6, I = 31.7, J = 33.9 °C.  
Mean LST from satellite for same neighbourhoods: A = 38.5, B = 38.0, C = 39.8, D = 40.5, E = 40.2, F = 40.8, G = 39.5, H = 41.0, I = 38.9, J = 41.3 °C.

(A) Identify the most suitable field‑survey method for collecting surface material type and canopy cover percentage across the neighbourhoods, and justify why other methods are less efficient.

Compare the rumen fermentation pattern and metabolic risk when a high-yielding crossbred cow (25 L/day) is fed: (A) 60% concentrate + 40% dry fodder vs (B) 40% concentrate + 60% green fodder + 10 kg legume fodder. Which ration minimizes subacute ruminal acidosis (SARA) risk and why?

In an experiment, a skeletal muscle fiber is permeabilized (skinned) to allow precise control of the bathing solution. The fiber is first bathed in a "relaxing solution" (pCa 9.0, 1 mM free MgATP, 20°C). Then, it is rapidly switched to an "activating solution" (pCa 4.5, same ATP). Force development is recorded. The experiment is repeated, but the activating solution contains **2 mM inorganic phosphate (Pi)** added. The peak force developed in the +Pi condition is significantly lower than in the control, but the **rate of force redevelopment (ktr)** after a quick release-restretch maneuver is **unchanged**. Explain these results in terms of the cross-bridge cycle kinetics. Which specific step(s) does Pi affect, and why does ktr remain constant?

"MetroBuild Infra" (partners P, Q, R; profit share 5:3:2) faces dissolution after Partner R is declared insolvent (liabilities ₹5 cr, assets ₹1 cr). The firm has: Land (book ₹20 cr, market ₹35 cr), Machinery (book ₹15 cr, market ₹10 cr), Unrecorded liability: Environmental restoration ₹3 cr. Realisation expenses ₹1 cr. Partner P loan ₹4 cr. Partner Q has private assets ₹8 cr. Partner R has private assets ₹0.5 cr. The partnership deed is silent on insolvency. The firm operates in a smart-city project zone where government has announced a new "Urban Renewal Policy" (public facility) that will increase land value by 40% but requires mandatory environmental restoration (the unrecorded liability). Per capita income in the zone is 3x national average. National development strategy prioritizes infrastructure. Creditors include: Bank loan ₹10 cr (secured on land), Trade payables ₹5 cr. The Bank has filed for court dissolution under Section 44(f) (business at loss) and Section 44(g) (just and equitable). Partners P and Q want to continue by admitting new partner S who brings ₹12 cr. The court must decide: dissolve or allow reconstruction?

(B) The Urban Renewal Policy (public facility) will increase land value by 40% but mandates environmental restoration (₹3 cr). Using cost-benefit analysis, should the court allow reconstruction (admit S with ₹12 cr) instead of dissolution? Consider national development priority and per capita income impact.

A student wants to isolate intact chloroplasts from spinach leaves. They homogenize leaves in ice-cold 0.33 M sorbitol buffer (isotonic) and perform differential centrifugation: 1,000 ×g for 5 min (pellet P1), then 3,000 ×g for 10 min (pellet P2). They resuspend P2 in buffer and layer on a 40%/80% Percoll step gradient, centrifuging at 5,000 ×g for 10 min. Intact chloroplasts band at the 40/80% interface. (a) Why is the homogenization buffer isotonic? (b) Why is P1 discarded? (c) Why use a step gradient (not continuous) here? (d) If they used 10,000 ×g in step 2, what would happen to chloroplasts?

In a survey of 2000 adults in a metro city, the following data was recorded regarding newspaper reading habits:
- 45% read Newspaper A
- 35% read Newspaper B
- 15% read both A and B
A person is selected at random. (a) Given that the person reads Newspaper A, what is the probability they also read Newspaper B? (b) Given that the person reads Newspaper B, what is the probability they read Newspaper A? (c) The survey agency claims: "Reading Newspaper A makes a person more likely to read Newspaper B." Is this claim supported by the data? Justify using conditional probabilities.

In 2024, the government rolled out a new welfare scheme for “Nutrition Support for Pregnant Women” that requires beneficiaries to authenticate via Aadhaar‑linked biometric POS terminals at ration shops. Field surveys in three Dalit‑dominant blocks of Uttar Pradesh found that 22% of eligible Dalit women failed authentication due to worn fingerprints (common among manual laborers), compared to 4% of upper‑caste women in the same blocks. Consequently, 1,100 Dalit women missed monthly benefits of ₹500 each, while only 200 upper‑caste women faced denial. An activist collective filed a petition under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act, 1989, alleging that the biometric denial amounts to an “atrocity” by causing deliberate deprivation of benefits based on caste‑linked occupational traits. The government defends the scheme as technology‑neutral and cites Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 (mandatory authentication for subsidies). Data:  
- Eligible Dalit women: 5,000  
- Dalit auth‑failures: 1,100 (22%)  
- Eligible upper‑caste women: 5,000  
- Upper‑caste auth‑failures: 200 (4%)  
- Monthly benefit per woman: ₹500  
- Minimum punishment under Sec. 3(1)(xi) (intentional insult) = 6 months imprisonment + fine.

(E) If the state argues that the biometric denial is a “technical glitch” not amounting to an atrocity, which judicial principle from the K.S. Puttaswamy (Privacy) judgment could be invoked to reject this defence, and how does it relate to the SC/ST Act’s requirement of “intent”?
Calculate the **effective cost of credit** (interest payable) for the seasonal loan of ₹ 3,000 taken at the raised rate of 25 % per annum, assuming the loan is outstanding for **6 months**.

In 2023 the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy launched the “Ultra‑Mega Solar Parks” (UMSP) scheme targeting 40 GW of solar capacity by 2030 across Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Tamil Nadu. Each park averages 2 GW, requires 5 000 ha of land, and involves a ₹12 000 crore investment per park. The scheme emphasizes rapid land acquisition via the “Land Pooling” model, offering farmers annuity payments of ₹30 000/ha/yr for 25 years. Critics argue that the pace mirrors the Second Five Year Plan’s industrial push, risking social displacement reminiscent of the inadequate land‑reform coverage in the First Plan. Proponents cite the “hasten slowly” principle, suggesting a phased rollout with pilot parks (500 MW each) to test socio‑economic impacts before scaling. Historical analogues include the colonial railway expansion (The Roman Army) that prioritised speed over local consultation, leading to unrest. Using data from the First Five Year Plan (land‑reform coverage 18 %, irrigation potential 7.5 M ha) and the Second Five Year Plan (industrial outlay ₹4 800 crore, steel capacity 2.5 Mt), evaluate whether the UMSP should adopt a gradualist or rapidist approach, and what land‑institutional safeguards are needed.

(C) Estimate the avoided CO₂ emissions (in million tonnes per year) from a 2 GW solar park operating at a 25 % capacity factor, assuming the displaced electricity would have come from coal‑fired plants with an emission factor of 0.9 kg CO₂/kWh.

A group of Theravada monks plans to establish an eco‑village on 5 acres of degraded land near Sanchi, Madhya Pradesh. They intend to install solar panels, run an organic farm, and offer meditation retreats. Lay donors pledge ₹2 crore for the solar project and ₹50 lakhs for water harvesting. 2024 में संसद ने डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षण विधेयक पारित किया, जो व्यक्तिगत डेटा के संग्रह, प्रसंस्करण और सीमा‑партनर हस्तांतरण को नियंत्रित करता है। विधेयक में निर्धारित है कि किसी भी संस्थान को उपयोगकर्ता की स्पष्ट सहमति लेनी होगी, और डेटा स्थानीयकरण के लिए राज्यों को दो विकल्प दिए गए हैं: (a) डेटा केंद्रों का निर्माण within state borders, या (b) केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिकृत बहु‑राज्यीय डेटा पार्क का उपयोग। विधेयक के अनुसार, उल्लंघन पर जुर्माना कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर का 4 % या ₹200 करोड़, जो भी अधिक हो, लगाया जा सकता है। ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ में, 2017 के न्यायाधीश पुट्टास्वामी मामले में最高 न्यायालय ने गोपनीयता को मौलिक अधिकार घोषित किया था, जो ब्रिटिश‑इंडिया era के “सर्विलांस अधिनियम, 1918” के विपरीत है। भू‑राजनीतिक रूप से, विधेयक ने चीन‑आधारित क्लाउड सेवाओं पर प्रतिबंध लगाया है, जिससे दक्षिण‑पूर्व एशिया में डेटा प्रवाह pathways पर प्रभाव पड़ता है। आर्थिक प्रभाव विश्लेषण बताता है कि स्थानीय डेटा केंद्रों से अगले पाँच वर्ष में ₹1.2 लाख करोड़ का निवेश आएगा और लगभग 3 लाख रोजगार सृजित होंगे। लेखक ने विधेयक को “सूचना युग का कवच” कहा है, जबकि कुछ आलोचकों का कहना है कि यह “अधिकारों का अवरोधक” बन सकता है।

(C) लेखक का विधेयक के प्रति総体的 दृष्टिकोण क्या है, और वह इसे किस रूप में वर्णित करता है?

In a QC lab, aniline is diazotized with NaNO₂/HCl at 0–5 °C to form benzenediazonium chloride, which is then hydrolyzed to phenol by warming the aqueous solution to 60 °C. Psychologically, each 10% drop in multigenerational living correlates with a 0.3‑point decline in MMSE score over 5 years, mediated by decreased cognitive reserve (c11_psy_cbse_01_003).
