An Indo‑French consortium plans to build a 200 MW solar farm in Rajasthan, exporting 70 % of its output to France under a long‑term PPA at €0.06/kWh. The remaining 30 % is sold domestically at ₹4/kWh. The project requires an autonomous investment of ₹1 500 crore (equipment, land). The Indian government provides a viability gap funding (VGF) of 15 % of the investment, released in two equal tranches after commercial operation. Domestic households have a consumption function C = 10 + 0.65Y (₹ crore). Autonomous investment elsewhere in the economy is ₹200 crore, government spending G = ₹300 crore, and exports of other goods and services are X₀ = ₹150 crore. Imports are proportional to income with MPM = 0.04. The exchange rate is fixed at 1 EUR = ₹88. Compute the new equilibrium level of income, the open‑economy multiplier, and journalize the VGF receipt and the export revenue recognition.

(B) Derive the open‑economy multiplier (kₒ) for the economy given MPC = 0.65 and MPM = 0.04.

An Indian electronics firm, **IndiChip**, exports semiconductors to the United States. In the last quarter, its export earnings rose by ₹800 crore due to higher global demand. The firm’s marginal propensity to consume domestically (MPC_d) is estimated at 0.55, while its marginal propensity to import (MPM) is 0.20. The remainder of any additional income is saved (MPS). The firm intends to reinvest half of its saved earnings into upgrading its fabrication plant, which is expected to induce further domestic investment of ₹200 crore. To mitigate exchange‑rate risk, IndiChip enters a forward contract to sell USD 10 million at a fixed rate of ₹82 per USD, maturing in three months. The accounting team must: (i) derive MPS from MPC_d and MPM, (ii) compute the open‑economy expenditure multiplier (k_o = 1 / (MPS + MPM)), (iii) estimate the total impact on domestic income (GDP) from the export surge and the induced investment, (iv) record the forward contract’s initial recognition and subsequent fair‑value measurement assuming the spot rate after three months is ₹84/USD, and (v) connect the decision to hedge to the **risk‑management** aspect of the planning function in Business Studies. Assume a simple open economy with price level fixed and that taxes are negligible.

(A) Given MPC_d = 0.55 and MPM = 0.20, calculate MPS and verify that MPC_d + MPM + MPS = 1.

Three partners (X, Y, Z) operate a social enterprise partnership manufacturing affordable solar lanterns for rural households. Their partnership deed (1 Apr 2023) stipulates: profit sharing ratio 3:2:1; fixed capitals X ₹5,00,000, Y ₹3,00,000, Z ₹2,00,000; interest on capital @10% p.a.; monthly salary X ₹20,000 (managing), Y ₹15,000 (technical); commission to Z @5% of net profit after charging such commission; guarantee to Z that total appropriation (interest+salary+commission+profit share) ≥ ₹3,00,000 p.a., deficiency borne by X and Y in 3:2; interest on drawings @12% p.a. (product method). Drawings: X ₹10,000 at beginning of each quarter; Y ₹15,000 at end of each half-year; Z ₹5,000 per month at beginning. Past adjustment: interest on drawings for 2022-23 omitted (X ₹1,20,000, Y ₹1,80,000, Z ₹60,000 evenly throughout, rate 12%, avg period 6 months). Net profit before appropriations 2023-24: ₹12,00,000. Government grant ₹2,00,000 for clean energy credited to capital reserve. Partners evaluate “inclusive development” via per capita income from firm.

(C) Pass journal entry for past adjustment of omitted interest on drawings (2022-23) and show effect on current year’s Profit & Loss Appropriation Account.

AeroSpace Dynamics LLP, an India-Singapore cross-border partnership, has partners Dev (India, 50%), Elena (Singapore, 30%), and Farid (UAE, 20%). They follow **Fixed Capital** method. Deed: 10% interest on capital, ₹1 lakh monthly salary to Dev, 10% commission to Elena on profit after salary. On 1-Oct-2024, they change profit sharing ratio to 3:3:4 (Dev:Elena:Farid) retrospectively from 1-Apr-2024. Assets: Land (book ₹5Cr, fair ₹7Cr), Crypto-wallet (book ₹2Cr, fair ₹1.5Cr), Patents (book ₹1Cr, fair ₹3Cr). Liabilities: Loan ₹3Cr, Provision for warranty ₹50L (reassessed ₹80L). Goodwill valued at 2 years' purchase of average super profit (normal return 12%, average capital employed ₹8Cr, average profit ₹1.5Cr). Deed requires capitals to be proportionate to new ratio via Current Account adjustments. Singapore-India DTAA applies for Elena's salary taxability. Farid guaranteed minimum profit ₹30L p.a. (year ending 31-Mar-2025).

(D) Calculate interest on capital, salary, commission for 6 months (Apr-Sep) under old ratio and 6 months (Oct-Mar) under new ratio. Fixed capitals: Dev ₹4Cr, Elena ₹2Cr, Farid ₹1Cr.

A public‑private initiative plans to deploy a fleet of 150 medical‑grade drones to deliver tele‑consultation kits, diagnostic samples and urgent medicines to 250 remote villages across Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. Each drone has a range of 120 km, payload capacity of 15 kg, and cruising speed of 80 km/h. Ground stations will be equipped with 4G/5G backhaul and satellite uplink for video consultation. The total project cost is ₹4,200 crore, comprising ₹2,500 cr for drones and ground‑control infrastructure, ₹1,000 cr for telemedicine software platforms and EMR integration, and ₹700 cr for training, maintenance and insurance. The system is expected to operate for 8 years. Anticipated annual beneficiary count is 1.8 million consultations (average 1 consultation per person per year). Each consultation generates a notional health‑economic benefit of ₹1,200 (averted travel costs, lost wages, etc.). OPEX is estimated at 22 % of CAPEX per year. The project will be managed by a special purpose vehicle owned 55 % by the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and 45 % by a private health‑tech firm. Using the data, answer the following.

(B) Using the beneficiary count (1.8 million consultations/year) and the per‑consultation health‑economic benefit (₹1,200), compute the annual total benefit in ₹ crore.

A fast‑growing AI startup in Bengaluru uses an automated hiring pipeline. Candidates first take a 30‑minute analytical reasoning test (AR‑Test) patterned after Western technological intelligence items (speed‑based abstraction, pattern completion). Their AR‑Test raw scores are converted to a percentile (P_AR). Next, they complete a Situational Judgment Test (SJT) that measures four buddhi subscales: Cognitive Discrimination (CD), Social Competence (SC – respect for elders, concern for others), Emotional Competence (EC – self‑regulation, honesty), and Entrepreneurial Competence (ECn – persistence, goal‑directed action). Each subscale yields a score 0‑100; the weighted buddhi score (B_W) is computed as 0.3·CD + 0.25·SC + 0.25·EC + 0.2·ECn. Finally, an Emotional Intelligence Questionnaire (EIQ) gives an EI score (0‑200). The startup’s final selection index (FSI) is: FSI = 0.4·(P_AR/100) + 0.35·(B_W/100) + 0.25·(EIQ/200).  

Data for three candidates:  
- **Aarav**: AR‑Test raw = 42/60 (P_AR = 78), SJT: CD=85, SC=70, EC=80, ECn=65 → B_W = ?, EIQ=150.  
- **Bhavna**: AR‑Test raw = 35/60 (P_AR = 62), SJT: CD=60, SC=90, EC=70, ECn=80 → B_W = ?, EIQ=130.  
- **Chaitanya**: AR‑Test raw = 48/60 (P_AR = 90), SJT: CD=50, SC=50, EC=55, ECn=45 → B_W = ?, EIQ=110.  

Assume stress (cortisol) raises AR‑Test error by 5 % for candidates with baseline cortisol > 15 µg/dL; only Chaitanya has elevated cortisol.

(B) Compute the final selection index (FSI) for Bhavna.

An NGO launches “हरित संकल्प”, a nationwide campaign to curb urban air pollution. Its Hindi promotional video opens with a verse:  
“शहर की धड़कन रुक‑रुककर, जैसे फेफड़े में रेत,  
हवा की धार में ज़हर घुलता, जैसे नदी में ज़हर‑बूँद।  
परंतु हर पौधा एक बंधन तोड़ता, जैसे बंधन‑तोड़ने वाला हीरा।”  
The video then displays a bar chart showing projected annual health‑cost savings (₹ 18 000 crore) if PM2.5 levels drop by 20 %, alongside a table indicating that the campaign’s implementation cost is booked under “Environmental Expenditure” as per the Ministry’s Accounting Manual.  
Students must analyze the verse for imagery and metaphor, link the metaphor of “हीरा” (diamond) breaking bonds to the accounting concept of expenditure classification, and critique how the poetic framing may influence policymakers’ perception of the cost‑benefit analysis.

(B) Identify the metaphor comparing a plant to a diamond that breaks bonds and explain what quality is transferred.

A recombinant *E. coli* strain carrying the human insulin gene on a pBR322‑derived plasmid (copy number ≈ 15–20 per cell) is cultured in a bioreactor aboard the International Space Station to produce insulin for astronauts. The culture starts with 1 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, each harboring on average 18 plasmid copies. The cells divide every 20 min under microgravity‑adjusted conditions. Space‑radiation induces plasmid loss with a first‑order rate constant k_loss = 0.0015 min⁻¹ (independent of cell division). An antibiotic (ampicillin) is used for selection; its concentration decays by hydrolysis with a first‑order rate k_deg = 0.0008 min⁻¹. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) for ampicillin is 50 µg mL⁻¹; the initial antibiotic concentration is 200 µg mL⁻¹.  

Answer the following:

(D) Determine the probability that a randomly selected colony after 4 h still retains the plasmid (i.e., has ≥ 1 copy), assuming plasmid loss events per plasmid are independent and follow Poisson statistics with mean λ = k_loss·t.

A boat goes 30 km upstream and 44 km downstream in 10 hours. In 13 hours, it can go 40 km upstream and 55 km downstream. Determine the speed of the stream and the speed of the boat in still water. (Hint: Let speed of boat in still water = x km/h, speed of stream = y km/h. Upstream speed = x-y, downstream speed = x+y. Use time = distance/speed.)

A research team wants to understand how migrant construction workers in Delhi‑NCR engage with platform‑based gig work (e.g., ride‑hailing, home‑service apps). They need to know (i) the proportion of workers who have tried gig work at least once, (ii) the daily earnings pattern, (iii) workers’ perceptions of job security, and (iv) how local municipal policies (e.g., licensing, welfare boards) affect access. The team has 6 weeks, a budget for 2 field investigators, and can approach workers at labour chowks and online forums. Which sociological method(s) should they prioritize for each sub‑question, and why? Consider strengths, limitations, time, and the need for contextual depth.

(D) To understand how municipal licensing policies shape access to gig platforms for a specific locality (e.g., Okhla industrial area), which method provides the deepest contextual insight?

ABC Ltd needs to finance three requirements: (i) ₹15 crore for 45 days to pay seasonal raw material suppliers, (ii) ₹80 crore for 7 years to set up a new plant, (iii) ₹5 crore for 180 days to bridge export receivables. For each, identify the appropriate market (money/capital), specific instrument, and the primary reason for the choice.

A 2025 World Bank report links delayed monsoon onset in the Indo‑Gangetic basin to a 12 % rise in seasonal labor migration from Bihar to Gujarat. The report’s authors cite Donne’s “A Lecture Upon the Shadow” to illustrate how shifting environmental “shadows” (monsoon variability) reshape livelihood patterns, much as changing daylight alters the length of a shadow. They argue that recognizing the poem’s insight into impermanence can guide adaptive social‑protection policies, such as portable benefits for migrant workers. Critics contend that the poem’s metaphysical focus on human emotion distracts from material drivers like groundwater depletion and land‑use change. Using the poem’s conceit, geographical data on monsoon variability, sociological theories of migration, and psychological concepts of risk perception, evaluate the suitability of the poetic analogy for informing climate‑adaptation policy.

(A) Identify the metaphysical conceit in Donne’s poem that links daylight variation to emotional intensity, and explain how it can be repurposed to describe monsoon‑driven livelihood change.

The Rajasthan State Agriculture Department, in collaboration with ISRO’s Bhuvan portal, launches a pilot project “धीरज‑किसान” (Dhiraj‑Kisan) to document traditional drought‑resistant farming practices of elders aged 60+ in the Thar Desert. Satellite‑derived NDVI data shows a 15% decline in vegetative cover over the past decade in the project area. Field teams conduct focus groups with 90 elders, recording techniques such as *khadin* water harvesting, *bawari* step wells, and mixed cropping of *bajra* and *moong*. The recordings are geo‑tagged and linked to NDVI plots to assess efficacy. Preliminary analysis reveals that villages where elders’ practices are actively used exhibit only a 5% NDVI decline, whereas villages relying solely on government‑subsidized hybrid seeds show a 22% decline. However, elders report that younger farmers (aged 25‑40) consider these methods “old‑fashioned” and prefer quick‑return hybrids, citing market pressure and lack of extension support. The project faces opposition from a local agribusiness lobby that argues the funds should be redirected to subsidizing drip‑irrigation systems for large farms. Using the secondary themes from the text and the cross‑subject concepts, answer the sub‑parts.

(D) Using the sociological concept of technology adoption resistance, explain why younger farmers prefer hybrid seeds over elders’ traditional methods, referencing the notions of “relative advantage” and “compatibility” from Diffusion of Innovations theory.

A biotech startup “NutriFerment” aims to launch a fortified, probiotic‑rich drink for urban adolescents. The base is a blend of skim milk powder (SMP) and roasted chickpea flour (CPF), fermented with a selected *Lactobacillus* strain. The product must deliver per 200 ml serving: Energy 150 kcal, Protein 8 g, Calcium 200 mg, Iron 4 mg, and at least 10⁹ CFU of probiotic. The SMP provides 350 kcal/100g, 36 g protein, 1250 mg calcium, negligible iron. CPF provides 360 kcal/100g, 20 g protein, 150 mg calcium, 6 mg iron. Fermentation reduces lactose by 80 % (increasing glucose/galactose) and increases B‑vitamin bioavailability by 25 %. The *Lactobacillus* strain belongs to Kingdom Bacteria, phylum Firmicutes, class Bacilli. The startup must (i) assign ingredients to ICMR food groups, (ii) calculate the blend ratio to meet protein and iron targets, (iii) explain the microbial classification and its safety implications, (iv) estimate the effect of fermentation on calcium bioavailability assuming a 15 % increase, and (v) suggest a cost‑effective fortification strategy using a micronutrient premix.

(D) Estimate the increase in calcium bioavailability (in mg) from the fermented drink if raw calcium contributes 180 mg per serving and fermentation enhances bioavailability by 15 %.
Fill in the blank: Now, walk 200 km south to the same river near ______ — the water is clearer, the flow slower, and the banks show layered deposits of sand and clay.

A ground‑based solar power plant uses an array of identical concave mirrors (radius of curvature **R = 2.0 m**) to focus sunlight onto high‑efficiency photovoltaic cells. Each mirror has a circular aperture of diameter **D = 2.0 m** (equal to |R|). The Sun is treated as an extended object of diameter **S☉ = 1.39×10⁹ m** located at the average Earth‑Sun distance **U = 1.496×10¹¹ m**. The mirrors form a real image of the Sun at their focal planes, where the photovoltaic cells are placed. The cells are square of side **L = 10 mm** and have a conversion efficiency **η = 20 %**. The solar constant (power per unit area received at Earth’s atmosphere) is **I₀ = 1361 W/m²**.  
Using the mirror formula and magnification, determine the size of the solar image on each cell, check whether it fits, and calculate how many mirrors are needed to achieve a target electrical output. Then apply set theory to describe allowable mirror tilt angles that keep the image within the cell, and use basic accounting to evaluate cost‑benefit under a budget constraint.

(B) Determine the diameter of the Sun’s image formed on the photovoltaic cell. Verify whether it fits within the square cell of side **L = 10 mm**.

A NITI Aayog discussion paper (2023) proposes reviving indigo as a natural dye for India’s textile export sector, projecting a demand of 15,000 MT/yr by 2030. The paper estimates current yield of indigo on alluvial Gangetic soil at 0.8 MT/ha, with a market price of ₹250/kg. It suggests providing a subsidy of ₹15,000/ha to farmers who adopt indigo intercropping with rice. Historical note: During Champaran, indigo was forced under the tinkathia system (3/20 of land) at a nominal price of ₹0.02/kg (1917 value). The paper claims that voluntary adoption, backed by subsidy, will increase farmer income by 35 % compared to rice‑only cultivation. Using the scenario, answer the following.

(B) Using the Economic node, evaluate the claim that indigo adoption raises farmer income by 35 % relative to rice‑only, given the subsidy.

A researcher has temperature data (°C) for 100 grid cells in the Himalayan region. The data is highly skewed due to altitudinal variation. She computes range = 30°C, standard deviation = 8°C, quartile deviation = 4°C, mean deviation about median = 5°C. She wants to report a single measure of dispersion that best represents the typical variability experienced by most grid cells (excluding extreme high-altitude cells). Which measure should she choose and why? How would her choice change if she wanted to include the extremes for climate change vulnerability assessment?

In early 2025, a multinational consortium secured a 30‑year lease to extract rare‑earth elements (REEs) from the biodiverse Eastern Ghats, home to 4 million Adivasis belonging to the Kondh, Saora, and Gadaba tribes. The project promises ₹85 000 cr in export revenue but requires clearing 1 200 km² of forest, displacing an estimated 250 000 tribal households and threatening sacred groves. Four response coalitions emerged: (i) **Reformist NGOs** demand a strengthened Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) with mandatory free, prior, and informed consent (FPIC) and a revenue‑sharing trust fund; (ii) **Revolutionary Eco‑Socialists** call for the abolition of private mining, advocating community‑controlled stewardship of the Ghats under a constitutional “Ecological Commons” amendment; (iii) **Resistance Groups** (traditional tribal councils) seek to defend existing forest rights under the Forest Rights Act 2006 (FRA) and block further encroachment by setting up vigilance patrols; (iv) **Reactionary Traders’ Association** argues for maintaining the status‑quo of state‑led mineral licensing, claiming that tribal opposition hinders national technological sovereignty and urging stricter anti‑terrorism laws to curb protests. Satellite data shows forest cover loss of 3.2 % per year in the lease area since 2022, while the national average is 0.4 %. The Ministry of Environment issued a draft order allowing “conditional clearance” contingent on compensatory afforestation elsewhere, which tribes contend violates the FRA’s prohibition on non‑forest‑land compensation.

(A) Classify each of the four tribal‑region coalitions (Reformist NGOs, Revolutionary Eco‑Socialists, Resistance Groups, Reactionary Traders) into the correct social‑movement type from Social Movements.

A research team plans to replicate the Miller‑Urey experiment inside a lunar habitat to test prebiotic synthesis under reduced gravity. The chamber is filled with a gaseous mixture mimicking early Earth (CH₄ : NH₃ : H₂ : H₂O = 2 : 2 : 1 : 1 by volume) at 1 atm and 300 K. UV lamps provide an average photon flux of 2.0 × 10¹⁸ photons m⁻² s⁻¹ at 200 nm (energy per photon = 9.93 × 10⁻¹⁹ J). The interior surface area exposed to UV is 0.5 m². Experiments show that each 10⁶ J of UV energy yields 1.2 µmol of glycine (the simplest amino acid) under these conditions. Glycine then undergoes condensation to form dipeptides with a second‑order rate constant k = 3.0 × 10⁻³ M⁻¹ s⁻¹. Assuming the glycine concentration reaches a steady‑state value of 5.0 × 10⁻⁴ M, calculate: (A) the total UV power incident on the chamber, (B) the glycine production rate in mol s⁻¹, (C) the initial rate of dipeptide formation, (D) the time required for the dipeptide concentration to reach 1.0 × 10⁻⁵ M if starting from zero, and (E) how a ten‑fold increase in UV flux would affect the steady‑state glycine concentration if the yield scales linearly with energy but degradation follows first‑order kinetics with k_deg = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴ s⁻¹.

In 2024, a coastal district of Odisha experienced severe cyclonic flooding, displacing ~150 000 people to temporary relief camps. Each meal comprised 200 g locally sourced rice (carbohydrate), 100 g dal (protein), 20 g fortified oil (lipid + vitamin A), and 50 g traditional pitha (sweet rice cake) prepared using age‑old recipes from the displaced communities. SunHarvest Energies, a startup developing floating solar photovoltaic (FPV) platforms for reservoirs, has completed prototype testing and is preparing for commercial rollout. The founding team consists of five technocrats who previously worked in large EPC firms. To transition from a project‑based to a product‑based organization, they adopt a transformational leadership style, articulating a vision of “clean water, clean power.” The company’s HR policy outlines a motivation process cycle: employees first experience an **unsatisfied need** (e.g., desire for recognition), leading to **tension**, which drives **search behaviour** (e.g., seeking challenging projects or proposing innovations), resulting in **engaged behaviour** (e.g., prototyping, pilot testing) that satisfies the need and reduces tension.  
To operationalize this cycle, the firm offers: (i) a monthly stipend of ₹80,000 (meeting physiological & safety needs), (ii) quarterly innovation bonuses tied to patent filings (addressing esteem needs), and (iii) autonomy to lead cross‑disciplinary task forces (addressing self‑actualization).  
The cost structure for producing one 1‑MW FPV unit includes: fixed monthly overheads (office, salaries of core team) = ₹4 lakhs; semi‑variable cost = ₹1.5 lakhs per unit + ₹0.2 lakhs per MW of capacity installed (reflecting logistics and installation complexity). The selling price per 1‑MW unit is negotiated at ₹3.0 lakhs. Market analysis, based on per‑capita electricity consumption data from various states, estimates an annual demand of 120 units.  
Communication of the vision occurs through monthly all‑hands meetings (formal) and informal Slack channels. However, feedback from field engineers indicates that technical jargon in meeting minutes often leads to misunderstandings with the finance team.

(A) Using the motivation process cycle described, identify which stage corresponds to the employee’s action of proposing a novel floating platform design after feeling a need for recognition.

2024 में संसद ने डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षण विधेयक पारित किया, जो व्यक्तिगत डेटा के संग्रह, प्रसंस्करण और सीमा‑партनर हस्तांतरण को नियंत्रित करता है। विधेयक में निर्धारित है कि किसी भी संस्थान को उपयोगकर्ता की स्पष्ट सहमति लेनी होगी, और डेटा स्थानीयकरण के लिए राज्यों को दो विकल्प दिए गए हैं: (a) डेटा केंद्रों का निर्माण within state borders, या (b) केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिकृत बहु‑राज्यीय डेटा पार्क का उपयोग। विधेयक के अनुसार, उल्लंघन पर जुर्माना कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर का 4 % या ₹200 करोड़, जो भी अधिक हो, लगाया जा सकता है। ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ में, 2017 के न्यायाधीश पुट्टास्वामी मामले में最高 न्यायालय ने गोपनीयता को मौलिक अधिकार घोषित किया था, जो ब्रिटिश‑इंडिया era के “सर्विलांस अधिनियम, 1918” के विपरीत है। भू‑राजनीतिक रूप से, विधेयक ने चीन‑आधारित क्लाउड सेवाओं पर प्रतिबंध लगाया है, जिससे दक्षिण‑पूर्व एशिया में डेटा प्रवाह pathways पर प्रभाव पड़ता है। आर्थिक प्रभाव विश्लेषण बताता है कि स्थानीय डेटा केंद्रों से अगले पाँच वर्ष में ₹1.2 लाख करोड़ का निवेश आएगा और लगभग 3 लाख रोजगार सृजित होंगे। लेखक ने विधेयक को “सूचना युग का कवच” कहा है, जबकि कुछ आलोचकों का कहना है कि यह “अधिकारों का अवरोधक” बन सकता है।

(E) Passage में “सूचना युग का कवच” उपमा का उपयोग डेटा संरक्षण के विषय को कैसे उजागर करता है?

In March 2025, a leading Bollywood actor launched a nationwide Instagram Reels campaign titled “#BreakTheSilence” to destigmatize mental‑health issues. Country X launches a low‑Earth‑orbit (LEO) satellite constellation to provide broadband to underserved regions. Baseline (Year 0): national internet penetration = 35 % (urban 55 %, rural 15 %). After 2 years (Year 2): national = 48 % (urban 60 %, rural 30 %). Total project cost = US $2 billion (CAPEX). The ICT sector’s contribution to GDP is expected to rise from 4 % to 6 % (GDP = US $500 billion). Digital‑literacy index improves from 0.45 to 0.58. Government provides a 5‑year tax holiday for ISPs and a rural‑subsidy fund of US $200 million.

(A) Calculate the absolute increase (in percentage points) and the relative increase (%) in rural internet penetration from Year 0 to Year 2.

A pharmaceutical company produces human insulin in *E. coli* using a pET‑based plasmid. Insulin concentration in the supernatant is measured by a competitive ELISA (anti‑insulin antibody coated plate, HRP‑insulin conjugate). The plasmid integrity is checked by quantitative PCR (qPCR) targeting the antibiotic resistance gene. The process must: (i) generate a standard curve from ELISA absorbance vs. known insulin concentrations to quantify unknown samples, (ii) determine plasmid copy number per cell from Ct values assuming 100 % efficiency, (iii) model insulin expression as a function of IPTG inducer concentration using a Hill equation, (iv) estimate the rate of substrate (glucose) diffusion into spherical bacterial pellets of radius 0.5 mm, and (v) perform a simple cost‑benefit analysis comparing two induction strategies (low‑IPTG long‑duration vs. high‑IPTG short‑duration) using linear programming.

(A) From a competitive ELISA, the following data are obtained:  

| [Insulin] (ng mL⁻¹) | Absorbance (A) |
|----------------------|----------------|
| 0                    | 1.200          |
| 5                    | 0.960          |
| 10                   | 0.780          |
| 20                   | 0.540          |
| 40                   | 0.300          |

Assuming a four‑parameter logistic fit simplifies to a linear range between 5–20 ng mL⁻¹, calculate the insulin concentration (ng mL⁻¹) of an unknown sample with absorbance A = 0.660.

A research consortium aims to study the effect of reduced gravity on the production of the diterpene taxol analogue from *Taxus breviculosa* cell cultures. Experiments are conducted in a 2 L airlift bioreactor aboard the International Space Station (ISS). The medium has viscosity μ = 1.0 × 10⁻³ Pa·s, density ρ = 998 kg·m⁻³, and is sparged with air at a superficial gas velocity U_g = 0.015 m·s⁻¹. Bubbles have a mean diameter d = 2 mm. The dissolved oxygen set‑point is 40 % of air saturation; at ISS temperature (22 °C) the oxygen solubility C* = 8.2 mg·L⁻¹. Oxygen uptake follows first‑order kinetics: OUR = k_O · C_O with k_O = 0.12 h⁻¹. The terpenoid synthesis rate (r_T) is coupled to the intracellular acetyl‑CoA pool via r_T = k_T · [AcCoA] where k_T = 0.03 L·g⁻¹·h⁻¹. Acetyl‑CoA is produced from glucose at a yield Y_AcCoA/Glc = 0.4 g AcCoA · g⁻¹ Glc and consumed by the TCA cycle with a first‑order rate constant k_TCA = 0.05 h⁻¹. Glucose is fed at a constant rate F_Glc = 0.2 g·L⁻¹·h⁻¹. Assume steady state for all intracellular metabolites.  
Answer the sub‑questions below. Derive expressions, compute numerical values, and discuss implications for scale‑up and gravity effects.

(E) Discuss qualitatively how the reduced buoyancy in microgravity would affect the bubble rise velocity and consequently the shear stress τ and kLa in the airlift reactor. Which of the two (τ or kLa) is more likely to become limiting for cell viability and productivity under these conditions?

A single female, Ms. Rao (age 42, financially stable), registered on CARINGS in 2023. She was referred a 6-year-old girl, "Chhavi," in January 2024. She accepted within 48 hours. Chhavi was placed in pre-adoption foster care with Ms. Rao on Feb 1, 2024. On March 15, 2024 (Day 43 of foster care), Ms. Rao informs the SAA that Chhavi has severe behavioral issues (aggression, night terrors) not disclosed in the Child Study Report. Ms. Rao wants to "return" Chhavi and adopt a younger child. The SAA says she must wait for the foster care period to end. Advise Ms. Rao and the SAA on the legal position under Regulations 14, 15, and 16 of the Adoption Regulations, 2022.
Starting from the 10 fetal‑derived chromosome 21 fragments isolated from plasma, calculate the expected number of copies after 30 PCR cycles with 90 % efficiency per cycle.

A trans‑boundary protected area straddles the Himalayan foothills of State X and State Y, governed by a joint conservation treaty that mandates maintaining ≥70 % forest cover in the core zone and facilitating seasonal migration of the Asiatic elephant. Researchers fit 20 elephants with GPS collars transmitting fixes every 30 minutes (L1/L2 signals). Over two years, they collect 350 000 position points. Simultaneously, Landsat‑8 NDVI time series reveals a gradual conversion of riparian grasslands to agricultural plots at a rate of 1.2 % yr⁻¹ within State Y’s sector, while State X shows stable forest cover. The GIS team must (i) assess the positional accuracy of the GPS fixes using PDOP values derived from satellite geometry, (ii) delineate wildlife corridors by kernel density estimation (KDE) of GPS points, (iii) overlay the corridor polygons with the NDVI‑derived land‑use change map to quantify habitat loss inside corridors, (iv) compute the corridor effectiveness index (CEI) = (length of corridor inside ≥70 % forest)/(total corridor length), and (v) advise the joint conservation commission on whether the treaty’s forest‑cover clause is being violated in State Y and propose adaptive management based on the GPS‑derived movement data.

(E) The treaty requires ≥70 % forest cover in the core zone. Satellite analysis shows State Y’s sector has 62 % forest cover, while State X’s sector has 78 %. If the joint commission decides to allocate reforestation funds inversely proportional to the deficit (deficit = 70 % − actual % for those below target, zero otherwise), what fraction of the total fund should State Y receive?

In 2024, a southern Indian state launches an AI‑driven “Samriddhi Portal” that allocates monthly food‑grain quotas to families based on a composite score derived from income, landholding, school attendance, and biometric attendance at health camps. Activists argue that the algorithm systematically under‑scores Dalit households in peri‑urban slums because it penalizes informal labor and treats temporary migration as “non‑residency.” A field study shows that 38 % of eligible Dalit families receive 60 % or less of their entitled quota, while 22 % of upper‑caste families in the same blocks receive over‑allocation due to land‑weighting. The state defends the portal as “transparent, merit‑based, and leakage‑free,” citing a 12 % reduction in overall subsidy leakages. A petition before the High Court invokes Article 21 (right to life) and Article 46 (promotion of educational and economic interests of weaker sections), claiming the algorithmic bias violates the principle of substantive equality and reproduces historic caste‑based deprivation reminiscent of colonial land‑settlement policies. The petitioners cite the Hindi story “èkeZohj Hkkjrh” (from the NCERT text) as a literary parallel where systemic indifference to poverty dehumanizes the marginalized, and argue that technological “charity” without structural redress merely mirrors the narrative’s critique of alms‑giving without justice.

(B) Using the concept of “secondary theme” (c12_hin_ar_cbse_12_007), state the secondary theme of “èkeZohj Hkkjrh” and evaluate whether the state’s claim of “leakage reduction” addresses this theme.

A mid‑size petroleum company plans to launch a **single‑use** project: constructing a 100 kL/day bio‑ethanol plant using agricultural waste. Simultaneously, it updates its **standing plan** – the corporate policy for capital expenditure approvals (a standing plan). The project’s fixed cost is ₹120 crore (plant & machinery). Variable cost per kL of ethanol is ₹25 (feedstock, utilities). The expected selling price is ₹45/kL. The company’s standing plan requires a minimum **post‑tax return on capital employed (ROCE)** of 12 % for any new project. Assume tax rate 30 % and that the plant will operate at 80 % capacity utilization.

(E) Identify which element of the standing plan (capital expenditure policy) is being applied when the company evaluates the bio‑ethanol project’s ROCE against the 12 % benchmark.

A microfluidic bioreactor is installed on the ISS to expand hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) for regenerative medicine. The device consists of a slab‑shaped hydrogel scaffold (thickness L = 200 µm) perfused with culture medium at a volumetric flow rate Q = 0.5 µL min⁻¹ through rectangular channels (height h = 100 µm, width w = 500 µm). The medium is saturated with O₂ at an inlet concentration C₀ = 0.20 mol m⁻³. HSCs consume O₂ at a volumetric rate R = 1.5 × 10⁻³ mol m⁻³ s⁻¹ (assumed uniform). The hydrogel’s effective O₂ diffusion coefficient is D = 2.0 × 10⁻⁹ m² s⁻¹. Metabolic CO₂ production raises the partial pressure of CO₂ in the medium to pCO₂ = 40 mm Hg. The medium is buffered with HEPES (pKₐ = 7.55) at total concentration Cₜₒₜ = 20 mM; initial pH = 7.40. Stem‑cell proliferation follows logistic growth: dN/dt = r N (1 − N/K) with r = 0.03 h⁻¹ and carrying capacity K = 1.0 × 10⁸ cells mL⁻¹. Wnt pathway inhibition reduces the probability of osteogenic differentiation from p₀ = 0.45 to p₁ = p₀ · e^(−α·[I]), where α = 1.2 (L mmol⁻¹) and inhibitor concentration [I] = 0.8 mmol L⁻¹.  
All needed constants: gas‑liquid O₂ solubility at 37 °C = 1.3 × 10⁻³ mol m⁻³ mm Hg⁻¹; universal gas constant R = 8.314 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹; temperature T = 310 K.

(C) Estimate the resulting pH change in the medium due to metabolic CO₂ production. Assume CO₂ dissolves according to Henry’s law (k_H = 1.3×10⁻³ mol m⁻³ mm Hg⁻¹) and the medium is buffered by HEPES (pKₐ = 7.55, total concentration Cₜₒₜ = 20 mM). Use the Henderson‑Hasselbalch equation.

A 2023 NITI Aayog report compares elderly welfare across three Indian states: Kerala (high elderly population, 12% of total, universal pension, high literacy), Bihar (low elderly proportion, 6%, fragmented pension schemes, low literacy), and Punjab (moderate elderly proportion, 9%, strong agricultural economy, rising youth migration to abroad). The report notes that Kerala’s elderly report 30% lower feelings of abandonment than Bihar’s, while Punjab shows a 15% increase in elderly loneliness despite higher income, attributed to transnational migration. Relate these findings to the theme and message of “ल्वज्न्कल ध >कसैम+h” and evaluate which state’s policy best aligns with the author’s message.

(B) Using the data, calculate the absolute number of elderly persons in Kerala if its total population is 35 million.

A battery‑operated infusion pump uses a Li‑ion cell whose voltage drops from 4.2 V (full) to 3.0 V (end‑of‑life). The pump’s microcontroller needs a stable 3.3 V supply. A Zener diode (V_Z = 3.3 V, I_Z(min)=2 mA, I_Z(max)=80 mA) is placed in shunt with a series resistor R_S and a load that varies between 5 mA (sleep) and 50 mA (active). The pump’s firmware samples temperature every 10 s; the Zener’s temperature coefficient is –2 mV/°C. The device must operate from –20 °C to +50 °C. Using exponential decay models for battery voltage (V_batt(t)=V_0 e^(‑t/τ) with τ=10 h) and set theory for acceptable voltage windows, determine R_S, power limits, temperature‑adjusted Zener voltage, cost (resistor $0.03/Ω, Zener $0.12/mW), and the time at which the regulator falls out of spec.

(A) Find the series resistor R_S that guarantees Zener breakdown at the lowest battery voltage (3.0 V) and maximum load (50 mA).

India is hosting a two‑day Indo‑Pacific Strategic Dialogue in New Delhi. Ten delegations (USA, Japan, Australia, France, Indonesia, Vietnam, Philippines, Singapore, UK, and Canada) each bring a delegation LAN of 20 laptops configured with private IP addresses 10.0.X.0/24 where X = delegation ID (1‑10). The venue is a convention centre built on reclaimed land near the coastline, with cable runs up to 250 m between the farthest delegation tables and the central server room. The organisers must:
1. Inter‑connect all delegation LANs so any laptop can reach any other for joint sessions.
2. Provide a shared Internet uplink via a leased line (modem) for live streaming.
3. Translate legacy diplomatic telex traffic (X.25) used by some delegations into TCP/IP for archival.
4. Extend the cable length where necessary using repeaters to keep signal attenuation below 12 dB (Cat6 attenuation = 5 dB/100 m).
5. Ensure minimal intra‑delegation collisions for real‑time video conferencing.
Historically, the dialogue builds on the 1971 Indo‑Soviet Treaty; politically, it addresses sovereignty concerns in the South China Sea; geographically, the venue’s proximity to the sea introduces electromagnetic interference from passing ships. Determine the appropriate network devices and configurations to meet these requirements.

(D) Legacy diplomatic telex terminals of some delegations use the X.25 protocol, while the summit’s backbone runs TCP/IP. Which device is required to translate between these protocol suites, and at which OSI layer does it primarily operate?
Using the Eₐ from Part A and the pre‑exponential factor A derived from k₄₀, calculate the rate constant k at the storage temperature of 5 °C (278 K).

A joint venture between an Indian public sector undertaking and a Japanese conglomerate is building a high‑speed rail corridor through the Gangetic plain. The Indian workforce (predominantly from collectivistic rural backgrounds) expects decisions to be made through consensus‑building meetings that include senior elders and community leaders. The Japanese team (trained in a corporate culture valuing precision, individual accountability, and hierarchical deference) prefers rapid, data‑driven decisions taken by designated engineers. After three months, clashes emerge: Indian workers perceive Japanese engineers as dismissive of local knowledge; Japanese managers view Indian consensus processes as slow and inefficient. Surveys show:  
- Indian workers’ mean self‑esteem (Rosenberg) = 24/30 (SD=2) when consulted, dropping to 18/30 when overruled.  
- Japanese engineers’ mean self‑efficacy = 26/30 (SD=1.5) when autonomy is high, falling to 20/30 when forced into group consensus.  
- Project delay attributable to conflict = 18 days (cost ≈ ₹12 crore).  
The project manager must decide whether to (a) adopt a hybrid decision‑making protocol, (b) provide cross‑cultural training, or (c) restructure teams into culturally homogenous units with liaison officers.

(B) Using the self‑efficacy data for Japanese engineers, calculate the expected change in self‑efficacy points if their autonomy level shifts from “high” (score 8/10) to “low” (score 3/10), assuming a linear relationship where each autonomy point changes efficacy by 1.2 points.

In 2024 the Ministry of Health launches **Garib Beti**, an AI‑driven mobile app that scans ultrasound clinic records linked to Aadhaar to flag potential sex‑selective abortions. The app sends alerts to district health officers when a clinic shows a skewed male‑female ratio over three consecutive months. Supporters cite Article 21 (right to life) and the Pre‑Conception and Pre‑Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, arguing the tool is essential to curb female foeticide. Critics, including women’s rights NGOs, claim the app violates privacy (Article 21) and could enable harassment of women seeking legitimate reproductive care. A pilot in Haryana shows a 12 % drop in reported sex‑selective cases after six months, while Kerala reports no change but a rise in complaints about data misuse. The poem “कन्याजन्म” presents supporting characters – the mother (who laments the birth), the father (who remains silent), the midwife (who performs rites), the nurses (who gossip), and society (which celebrates a son). Students must examine these characters’ attitudes, link them to the ethical‑legal debate around Garib Beti, and evaluate whether the app reinforces or challenges the patriarchal mindset reflected in the poem.

(A) Identify two lines from the poem that reveal the mother’s attitude toward the birth of a girl and explain how this attitude mirrors the societal bias that Garib Beti seeks to counter.

In early 2024 a draft “Data Sovereignty Bill” proposed mandatory localisation of all personal data, broad exemptions for state surveillance, and heavy fines for non‑compliant tech firms. A coalition of women’s rights groups, digital civil society organisations, and student unions launched a nationwide online campaign (“#MyDataMyRights”) demanding withdrawal of surveillance clauses and stronger consent provisions. The campaign used encrypted messaging apps, organised virtual town‑halls reaching 1.2 million unique participants, and filed public‑interest litigations in three High Courts. The ruling party initially defended the bill as necessary for national security, while opposition parties criticised it for threatening privacy and women’s safety (citing risks of misuse of location data to stalk survivors of domestic violence). After sustained pressure, the government amended the bill to remove mandatory localisation and add a judicial oversight clause for surveillance requests. The amendment was passed in August 2024. Concurrently, reports showed a 22 % rise in online gender‑based harassment in states with weak data‑protection enforcement, and a gender‑disaggregated accounting of cyber‑crime victims indicated women constituted 58 % of cases. Using this scenario, examine the interaction between the women’s movement, digital activism, party politics, and constitutional safeguards.

(C) Evaluate whether the state’s initial defence of the bill on national‑security grounds satisfies the proportionality test under Article 19(2), referencing the surveillance exemptions and impact on women’s privacy.

A biotechnology startup wants to produce a virus-like particle (VLP) vaccine in animal cell culture. They have two options: (A) HEK293 suspension culture in serum-free media, transient transfection with plasmid DNA; (B) Sf9 insect cells (baculovirus expression system) in serum-free media. The VLP requires proper assembly of 3 structural proteins with disulfide bonds and N-glycosylation at two sites per protein. The target dose is 10⁹ particles/mL for clinical trials. Compare both systems across five criteria: (1) glycosylation fidelity for human use, (2) scalability to 2000 L bioreactor, (3) transfection/infection efficiency and consistency, (4) regulatory precedent for VLP vaccines, (5) cost and timeline for GMP runs. Recommend one system with justification.
Explain how the desertion rate of the ANSF (>30% annually) reflects limits on US structural power in Afghanistan.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you open a newspaper: the front page screams "India's GDP grows at 7.2%" while the business page says "______ prices surge to ₹80/kg in Delhi mandis".

A GPS station in Bangalore (on the Indian Plate) shows a velocity of 38 mm/yr north-northeast relative to a stable Eurasian reference frame. A station in Perth (Australian Plate) shows 55 mm/yr north. Explain the difference and infer the nature of the boundary between the Indian and Australian plates in the Indian Ocean.

A UNESCO‑funded project aims to map the linguistic diversity of the Hindi heartland by selecting representative localities. The team chooses the quarter described in “फकीर के क्वार्टर” because the text mentions residents speaking a mix of Awadhi, Braj, and colloquial Hindi, reflecting a “bol‑boli” (mixed speech) environment. Socio‑linguistic surveys show 62 % of households use Awadhi at home, 28 % Braj, and 10 % standard Hindi; 15 % are bilingual in Hindi‑Urdu. The project proposes to install interactive kiosks recording oral histories, funded by a ₹3 crore grant, with expected outreach to 200 schools in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh. Local politicians argue the grant should instead fund road repairs, citing the quarter’s low per‑capita income (₹9,500/month). Students must analyze the chapter’s depiction of language, connect it to geographical language‑region concepts, and evaluate sociolinguistic implications for educational policy.

(E) Craft a 150‑word grant proposal excerpt that justifies the UNESCO kiosk project by integrating one Hindi textual detail, one sociolinguistic statistic, and one geographical concept.

A agri‑tech startup “AgriChain” plans to deploy a blockchain‑based traceability system for organic fruits and vegetables in three states. The startup has a seed fund of ₹5 crore. Core activities and estimated costs: (i) Platform development (software, smart contracts) – ₹2 crore; (ii) On‑boarding certified organic farmers – ₹30,000 per farmer (includes training, certification audit, and IoT sensor kit); (iii) Marketing & consumer outreach – ₹15 lakh per 100 000 reach; (iv) Legal compliance & liability insurance – ₹50 lakh annual premium. Expected annual revenue from subscription fees (₹500/farmer/month) and transaction fees (0.5 % of transaction value) is projected at ₹3 crore if 80 % of the 2 500 eligible farmers in the region are on‑boarded and achieve an average monthly transaction of ₹2 lakhs per farmer. However, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) mandates that any digital traceability system must undergo a security audit costing ₹25 lakh, non‑compliance attracts a fine of ₹1 crore. Using utility, accessibility, and interchangeability of resources (funds, farmer participation, legal compliance), answer the following.

(B) Determine the accessibility (as a percentage) of certified organic farmers if the startup can onboard only 1 200 farmers out of the 2 500 eligible due to limited certification agency capacity, which can process at most 150 applications per month.

A 19-year-old female student (inverted triangle figure: broad shoulders, narrow hips) needs a "casual day out" outfit for a museum visit in Mumbai monsoon (humid, 30°C, possible rain). She wants to wear a dress. She has: (A) White cotton sundress, spaghetti straps, tiered skirt, above-knee. (B) Navy blue rayon wrap dress, ¾ sleeves, midi length. (C) Black polyester bodycon dress, sleeveless, mini. Evaluate each using design principles, figure analysis, and climate suitability. Recommend the best and suggest one modification.

An independent filmmaker is producing a documentary on the Inuit community of Nunavut, focusing on how shifting sea‑ice patterns affect traditional hunting. Filming occurs in late April on the frozen Hudson Bay, where the temperature averages –20 °C, winds gust at 40 km/h, and the ice emits a deep, resonant creaking sound underfoot. The director remarks that the “ominous ice creaks, the relentless wind, and the stark white‑blue landscape forge an atmosphere of precarious resilience that mirrors the community’s adaptive struggle.” For production accounting, the filmmaker estimates: (i) $18 000 for specialized cold‑weather camera housings (usable for 25 shooting days), (ii) $12 000 for fuel for snow‑mobiles and generators (consumed at a steady rate), (iii) $6 000 for a local cultural advisor (paid as a lump sum upon arrival), (iv) $5 000 for liability insurance covering the 40‑day shoot, and (v) $3 000 for carbon‑offset credits purchased to mitigate the expedition’s greenhouse‑gas emissions (a voluntary environmental expense). The filmmaker must (a) apply the matching principle to allocate housing and fuel costs, (b) use the concept of **externality** from environmental economics to decide how to treat the carbon‑offset expense, and (c) apply the **social impact assessment** principle from sociology to evaluate whether the cultural advisor fee should be capitalized as an intangible asset or expensed.

(A) Identify **four** distinct setting elements in the scenario and quote the exact sensory detail that conveys each.

In 2024 the governments of State A and State B inaugurated a 1.2 km steel‑concrete “Peace Bridge” over the River Kaveri, intended as a **symbol** of enduring friendship and shared water security. The bridge’s inauguration ceremony featured a speech by the Chief Minister of State A that praised “mutual trust and cooperative stewardship of the river’s bounty” while, unbeknownst to the audience, his administration had just signed a confidential annex to the 1960 Kaveri Water‑Sharing Agreement that allocated 70 % of the river’s lean‑season flow to State A for a new hydro‑project. Satellite imagery shows that, within three months of the bridge opening, freight traffic on the bridge increased by 45 % and enabled rapid deployment of State A’s engineering crews to the upstream dam site, intensifying State B’s protests. Local poets have begun using the bridge as a metaphor for “false promises” in their verses, noting the contrast between the bridge’s sturdy appearance and the fragile trust it actually represents.

(B) Explain how the Peace Bridge functions as a **symbol** of false unity, linking its physical attributes to the abstract theme of broken trust.

GreenSteel Ltd., an established integrated steel producer, intends to set up a 3 Mtpa green hydrogen‑based steel plant in Odisha. The project requires: (a) deciding the plant location (top‑level strategic), (b) designing the organizational structure for the new unit (middle‑level), (c) ensuring day‑to‑day safety and quality checks on the shop floor (lower‑level), (d) classifying costs into fixed and variable for break‑even analysis, and (e) determining the minimum sales volume needed to cover costs given a selling price of ₹55 000/tonne, variable cost of ₹30 000/tonne, and fixed annual cost of ₹900 crores. The finance team must also comply with Cost Accounting Standards (CAS‑4) for cost classification.

(A) Which level of management is primarily responsible for the decision on the plant’s geographic location in Odisha?

You are annotating a hypothetical protein 'HpX' from a pathogen. BLASTp: 28% identity to human 'Protein X' (E-value 0.001) — a nuclear transcription factor with a zinc finger domain. InterProScan: Detects 'zf-C2H2' domain (PF00096) but NO nuclear localization signal (NLS). ProtParam: pI 9.5, Instability 30, GRAVY -0.2. The student annotates HpX as "Transcription factor". Evaluate this annotation. Propose a corrected annotation with evidence, and suggest ONE wet-lab experiment to resolve the ambiguity.

Combine with prior concept (Determinants of Demand - Income). In a tier-2 city, demand for two-wheelers (bikes) is affected by: (a) price of petrol (complement), (b) price of electric scooters (substitute), (c) consumer income. Initially, bike demand at ₹80,000 is 1,000 units/month. Petrol price rises ₹10/litre. Electric scooter price falls ₹5,000. Average income rises 5%. Bikes are normal goods. Predict the net shift direction of the bike demand curve and explain which effect dominates if the income effect is +150 units, petrol effect is -200 units, and e-scooter effect is -100 units.

A 2 L stirred‑tank bioreactor operates in batch mode with HeLa cells secreting a monoclonal antibody (mAb) at a constant specific productivity qₚ = 15 pg cell⁻¹ day⁻¹. Initial viable cell density X₀ = 0.5 × 10⁶ cells mL⁻¹, viability = 95 %. The culture medium contains 4 g L⁻¹ glucose and 2 g L⁻¹ glutamine. Glucose consumption rate per cell r_glc = 2 × 10⁻¹⁶ mol cell⁻¹ h⁻¹. The doubli​ng time in serum‑containing medium is t_d,serum = 22 h; in serum‑free medium t_d,sf = 30 h due to slower growth. Osmolarity contributors: NaCl 0.9 % w/v (154 mM), glucose 4 g L⁻¹ (≈22 mM), glutamine 2 g L⁻¹ (≈14 mM). Assume ideal mixing, no cell death until nutrient depletion, and that antibody accumulates in supernatant without degradation.

(A) Calculate the viable cell concentration (cells mL⁻¹) after 48 h of culture in serum‑containing medium, assuming exponential growth and no death.

Priya, a 32‑year‑old cybersecurity analyst at a national bank, detects ransomware encrypting customer transaction databases at 02:00 am. The attack threatens to expose ₹150 crore of sensitive data unless a ₹30 crore ransom is paid in Bitcoin within 48 hours. She leads a team of four, working 14‑hour shifts, skipping meals, and averaging 5 hours of sleep. Her heart rate variability shows reduced parasympathetic tone, and salivary cortisol is elevated 2.3 × baseline. Priya feels a deep sense of purpose in protecting citizens’ savings (high Commitment), believes her technical expertise can halt the encryption (high Control), and views the incident as an opportunity to prove the bank’s resilience (high Challenge). The bank’s accounting division estimates a potential direct loss of ₹200 crore if data recovery fails, plus reputational damage. Recent flow cytometry shows a 35 % decline in her natural killer (NK) cell activity compared to her baseline measured six months earlier.

(D) The accounting department estimates a potential loss of ₹200 crore if data is not recovered. Compute the opportunity cost of allocating 20 % of the IT budget to cybersecurity insurance that reduces expected loss by 60 %. Assume IT budget = ₹500 crore.

An NGO “Sparsh” works in tribal Madhya Pradesh to reduce school dropout among adolescents with visible scars from fire accidents. Baseline survey: 74% feel ashamed to attend school; 62% report peers call them “chuhia” (bitter). The NGO adapts *On the Face of It* into a street‑play, casting local youth as Derry and Mr Lamb. After three months, focus groups show: 48% willingness to interact with scarred peers (↑26%), 31% drop in self‑reported shame (↓43%). The NGO’s impact team must explain the change using (i) sociological concept of ableism, (ii) psychological concept of cognitive dissonance, and (iii) geographic factor of rural‑urban migration (scarred youth often migrate to cities for anonymity). They must propose two scalable interventions: (a) mobile storytelling vans, (b) peer‑led scar‑acceptance workshops, linking each to theory and geographic data.

Simultaneously, the female partner receives a bolus of LH (luteinising hormone) that triggers ovulation. LH plasma concentration follows first‑order elimination: C(t) = C₀ e^(–kt), with C₀ = 30 IU/L and k = 0.15 min⁻¹. Ovulation occurs when C(t) ≥ 10 IU/L.

**Using the data above, answer the following.**
