Using the concept that gravity holds gases, explain why light gases escape more easily. If Earth's gravity were halved, predict what would happen to the nitrogen and oxygen over geological time.

A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s applies brakes. The braking force is 5000 N. The driver reacts for 0.5 s before braking (constant speed during reaction). Find total stopping distance from the moment the driver sees the obstacle. (Use Work-Energy Theorem for braking phase.)

A biotech startup has engineered a Cas9 nuclease from *Thermus thermophilus* (optimal activity 65 °C) by introducing three point mutations (Ala→Val, Gly→Ser, Lys→Arg) that retain >80 % activity at 65 °C while the wild‑type SpyCas9 loses >90 % activity above 42 °C. The kit comprises: (i) the thermostable Cas9 protein expressed in *E. coli*, (ii) chemically synthesized sgRNA (0.5 mM final), (iii) 20 nm gold‑nanoparticle delivery system, and (iv) a GFP‑based fluorescence reporter (excitation 488 nm, emission 510 nm) to quantify editing efficiency. Prior art includes the US patent US8,697,359 disclosing the wild‑type SpyCas9 sequence and its use in plants. The wheat genome contains ~1×10⁵ potential off‑target sites. Baseline off‑target probability for SpyCas9 is 1×10⁻³ per site; the engineered variant reduces this to 2×10⁻⁵ per site due to heightened specificity. Editing efficiency in wheat protoplasts is 70 % for the thermostable Cas9 versus 30 % for SpyCas9 under heat‑stress (45 °C) conditions. Assume each successfully edited allele confers a 15 % increase in drought‑related yield. The Indian patent filing fee for an individual is INR 1,600; renewal fees average INR 3,000 per year from year 6 to year 20. Use h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3×10⁸ m/s, λ = 488 nm, 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J.

(D) Estimate the total cost (in INR) to maintain the patent in India for the full 20‑year term, assuming filing fee INR 1,600 and average annual renewal fee INR 3,000 from year 6 onward.

A rural preschool in a drought‑prone district faces a 40 % reduction in locally available millet yield and a 25 % increase in market price of pulses due to water scarcity. The school must redesign its weekly menu to meet ICMR 2020 RDAs for 5‑year‑old children (average weight 18 kg) while relying more on drought‑resilient crops (sorghum, cowpea) and incorporating inexpensive animal‑source foods (egg, milk) to maintain protein quality. Additionally, the district administration requires a socioeconomic impact report estimating the change in household food‑security index if the preschool meal program is scaled to cover 80 % of village children, using the preschool’s per‑child cost as a proxy.  
Given data:  
- Baseline ICMR 2020 RDA for 5‑yr: Energy = 1250 kcal/day, Protein = 17 g/day, Iron = 8.5 mg/day.  
- Drought adjustments: Millet yield ↓ 40 % → effective price ↑ 66 % (since same demand, less supply). Pulse price ↑ 25 %.  
- Food composition (per 100 g):  
  • Sorghum (dry) – Energy 330 kcal, Protein 10.0 g, Iron 3.0 mg, PDCAAS 0.60.  
  • Cowpea (dry) – Energy 340 kcal, Protein 23.0 g, Iron 5.5 mg, PDCAAS 0.85.  
  • Egg (whole, boiled) – Energy 150 kcal, Protein 13.0 g, Iron 1.2 mg, PDCAAS 1.00.  
  • Milk (full‑fat, 3 % fat) – Energy 65 kcal, Protein 3.2 g, Iron 0.0 mg, PDCAAS 1.00.  
- Prices (normal): Sorghum ₹28/kg, Cowpea ₹80/kg, Egg ₹6/piece (≈ 50 g), Milk ₹45/litre (≈ ₹0.045/g).  
- Drought‑adjusted prices: Sorghum ₹28 × 1.66 ≈ ₹46.5/kg; Cowpea ₹80 × 1.25 = ₹100/kg; Egg ₹6 × 1.10 ≈ ₹6.6/piece (assuming 10 % price rise due to feed cost); Milk ₹45 × 1.15 ≈ ₹51.75/litre.  
Students must calculate adjusted requirements, formulate a breakfast that supplies 30 % of daily energy and 35 % of daily protein using sorghum, cowpea, egg, and milk, compute digestible protein (accounting for PDCAAS), determine cost‑nutrient ratios, and estimate the per‑child monthly cost and its impact on village food‑security (assuming a baseline index of 0.65 and that each ₹1 reduction in per‑child meal cost raises the index by 0.005).

(C) Assuming a feasible breakfast mix (as determined after adjusting targets in Part B) provides 4.5 g of crude protein, calculate the digestible protein intake using the PDCAAS values of sorghum (0.60), cowpea (0.85), egg (1.00), and milk (1.00).

A state government launches “Samriddhi Yojana”, a blockchain‑enabled conditional cash transfer (CCT) scheme targeting **nuclear families** with at least one child aged 0‑5 years. To receive ₹2,000 per month, families must upload monthly proof of (i) child’s school attendance (if ≥3 years) and (ii) a government‑approved health‑check‑up showing hemoglobin ≥11 g/dL and weight‑for‑height Z‑score ≥‑2. Funds are released via smart contracts on the 1st of each month; the state’s finance department follows **accrual basis accounting** and requires that expenditures be recorded when the obligation arises (i.e., at the start of the month). The scheme’s pilot covers 12,500 eligible nuclear families in District X. Baseline survey shows 18 % of children have hemoglobin <11 g/dL (anemia) and 12 % are wasted (WHZ <‑2). After six months, monitoring reports indicate anemia prevalence dropped to 10 % and wasting to 7 %. The state allocated ₹30 crore for the six‑month pilot, assuming full compliance.  
Using the data, answer the following sub‑parts.

(B) Using accrual basis accounting, calculate the total expenditure to be recorded in the state’s books for the six‑month pilot assuming 100 % compliance.

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs proposes a “Smart City” project in Tier‑2 city X (population 1.2 million) to be completed by 2030. The plan includes: (i) installation of 500 km of fiber‑optic broadband, (ii) construction of 12 GW solar‑powered micro‑grids, (iii) affordable housing for 30 % of slum dwellers, (iv) e‑governance portals for service delivery, and (v) skill‑development centres targeting 200 000 youth. The project budget is ₹18 000 crore, financed 60 % by central grants, 30 % by state bonds, and 10 % by private PPP. An impact assessment must evaluate whether the project advances the four pillars of human development. Relevant data: current literacy rate 78 %, female labour‑force participation 22 %, per‑capita electricity consumption 900 kWh/yr, and Gini coefficient 0.38. The city’s master plan allocates 15 % of land for green belts, but the proposed solar farms will occupy 8 % of that green belt area. Using the concepts of equity, sustainability, productivity, and empowerment, analyze the trade‑offs and suggest policy adjustments.

(D) Identify which pillar(s) are most directly affected by the e‑governance portals and justify using the concept of empowerment.
Two cars A and B move on a straight road. Car A moves east at 20 m/s, car B moves west at 15 m/s. What is the velocity of A relative to B? State the magnitude, direction, and SI unit.

A clinical lab uses SYBR‑Green based qPCR to quantify HIV‑1 RNA copies in patient plasma. After reverse transcription, 2 µL of cDNA (equivalent to 10 µL plasma) is added to a 20 µL reaction containing 200 nM each primer, 200 µM dNTPs, 1.5 mM MgCl₂, and SYBR‑Green I at 0.5×. The fluorescence threshold is set at 10 % of the maximum fluorescence observed in the no‑template control (NTC) after 40 cycles. The instrument records fluorescence per cycle; the baseline cycles 3‑7 are used to calculate baseline standard deviation (σ = 0.02 RFU). The amplification plot yields a threshold cycle (Ct) of 23.4 for the sample. A standard curve generated from 10‑fold serial dilutions of a known plasmid (10⁸ to 10² copies/µL) gives a slope of –3.32 and R² = 0.998. The lab must (i) verify the Ct calculation from raw fluorescence, (ii) determine amplification efficiency from the slope, (iii) compute expected fluorescence at Ct using Beer‑Lambert law, (iv) estimate limit of detection (LOD) based on σ, and (v) design a dilution series for accurate quantification.

(E) Design a 5‑point 10‑fold dilution series (starting from 10⁶ copies/µL) for the standard curve, specifying the volume of stock and diluent needed for each step to prepare 100 µL of each dilution.

Compute the one‑way propagation delay for the inter‑data‑centre backup link (450 km) using fibre with propagation speed 2 × 10⁸ m/s. Compare it to the delay if the same distance were covered by a geostationary satellite link (uplink + downlink ≈ 70 000 km).
Determine the maximum sodium (in mg) contributed by chicken breast if the lunch must stay ≤ 1800 mg Na and other ingredients (cereal, veg, flaxseed, oil) are assumed Na‑free.

A biotech startup plans to manufacture human insulin using a genetically engineered *E. coli* strain harbouring the proinsulin gene under a T7 promoter. The process will be run as a fed‑batch culture in a 5 000 L stirred‑tank bioreactor. Glucose is the limiting substrate; feed solution contains 500 g L⁻¹ glucose. The following kinetic and physicochemical data are known:

- Maximum specific growth rate, µₘₐₓ = 0.45 h⁻¹  
- Monod constant for glucose, Kₛ = 0.2 g L⁻¹  
- Desired steady‑state glucose concentration in the reactor, S = 0.05 g L⁻¹ (to avoid overflow metabolism)  
- Biomass yield on glucose, Yₓ/ₛ = 0.5 g g⁻¹  
- Insulin yield on biomass, Yₚ/ₓ = 0.02 g g⁻¹ (i.e., 20 mg insulin per g dry cell weight)  
- Volumetric oxygen transfer coefficient, kLa = 250 h⁻¹  
- Saturation dissolved oxygen concentration, C* = 0.008 mol L⁻¹ (at 37 °C, 1 atm air)  
- Desired dissolved oxygen set‑point, Cₗ = 0.002 mol L⁻¹  
- Power number for the Rushton turbine, Po = 5.0 (dimensionless)  
- Culture density, ρ = 1 000 kg m⁻³ (approx. water)  
- Impeller diameter, D = 0.5 m  
- Agitation speed, N = 3 rev s⁻¹ (180 rpm)  

The downstream purification train consists of three steps: (i) inclusion‑body solubilisation (yield 85 %), (ii) refolding (yield 60 %), (iii) reverse‑phase HPLC (yield 70 %).  

Using the data above, answer the following sub‑parts. Show all steps, state assumptions, and indicate units clearly.

(D) Estimate the steady‑state biomass concentration (X) achievable in the fed‑batch reactor given the glucose feed rate F = 150 L h⁻¹ of 500 g L⁻¹ glucose solution.

In early 2025, a newly formed national party “Jana Shakti” rises after a fragmented coalition collapses. Its senior state leaders—Kamaraj‑type figures from Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Punjab—form an informal syndicate that controls 70% of ticket allocations, disburses 60% of the party’s election fund, and enforces discipline through a secret “whip” committee. The parliamentary wing, led by the party’s prime‑ministerial candidate, retains only 30% influence over candidate selection and policy formulation, creating a dual power structure reminiscent of the Congress Syndicate of the 1960s.  

During the 2024 party presidential election, the syndicate‑backed candidate lost to a reformist outsider by a narrow 4.8% margin, echoing the 1969 Congress presidential contest where Indira Gandhi defeated the syndicate’s nominee.  

A team of historians notes parallels with the Roman patron‑client system: senators (patrons) mobilized votes and resources for clients (voters) in exchange for loyalty, maintaining a roughly 2:1 ratio of patron‑directed to client‑autonomous actions.  

Meanwhile, an external audit of Jana Shakti’s digital donation platform reveals that 15% of recorded contributions cannot be traced to verified donors, and fund disbursement records show discrepancies between sanctioned amounts and actual expenditures. The party’s accountant is tasked to design a transparent financial oversight mechanism that mirrors internal audit principles while respecting the party’s federal structure.  

Using the data above, students must (i) analyse the dual power structure, (ii) evaluate implications for internal party democracy, (iii) draw comparisons with Roman patronage, (iv) assess financial oversight needs, and (v) propose institutional reforms that balance central coordination with grassroots autonomy.

(C) Compare the Jana Shakti syndicate’s patron‑like control over funds and tickets with the Roman patron‑client system described in c11_hist_cbse_01_005 and c11_hist_cbse_02_003.

The decomposition of NH₃ on a hot Pt surface is zero-order at high pressure. Initial [NH₃] = 0.10 mol L⁻¹, k = 2.5 × 10⁻⁴ mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Calculate (a) [NH₃] after 100 s, (b) half-life, (c) time for 75% decomposition.

In State Z (a Himalayan hill state), glacial retreat has increased the frequency of landslides, prompting seasonal out‑migration of working‑age males (≈ 12 % of the 15‑59 cohort) to urban centres for construction work. Simultaneously, improved healthcare has raised life expectancy, increasing the 60+ share from 8 % (2011) to 13 % (2021). The 2021 age‑sex distribution is: 0‑14 = 20 %; 15‑59 = 57 %; 60+ = 23 %; sex ratio = 940 females per 1,000 males. Using concepts of population distribution , growth , demographic transition , and incorporating insights from environmental geography (Climate Change impacts on mountain ecosystems) and psychology (Stress and coping in displacement), answer the following.

(D) Interpret the sex ratio of 940 in State Z with reference to male‑biased out‑migration and discuss its psychological implications for displaced males.

An enzyme assay shows zero activity when the reaction mixture lacks Mg²⁺. Adding back 5 mM Mg²⁺ restores full activity. However, adding 5 mM Zn²⁺ does not restore activity. What does this tell you about the cofactor specificity of this enzyme, and how would you classify the enzyme–cofactor complex when Mg²⁺ is bound?

A student conducts three trials for the same pendulum. Trial 1 takes 30 s for 15 oscillations, Trial 2 takes 32 s for 16 oscillations, and Trial 3 takes 29 s for 15 oscillations. Calculate the average time period across all trials.

By 1967, the Socialist Party had fragmented into the Praja Socialist Party (PSP) and the Samyukta Socialist Party (SSP). In the 1971 general election, both formations allied with the Indian National Congress (Indira) under a “Grand Alliance” to counter the rising Bharatiya Jana Sangh and the CPI(M). The alliance promised to implement land‑reforms ceiling laws and expand public‑sector employment. However, after the 1971 victory, the Congress reneged on the land‑reform promise, citing fiscal constraints, while the PSP/SSP continued to advocate for cooperative farming. Using concepts of party splits, coalition dharma, fiscal federalism, and the historical experience of the British‑Indian land‑revenue systems, evaluate the ideological and strategic consequences of the 1971 alliance for the socialist formations.

(A) Explain how the 1948 ban on dual Congress‑Socialist Party membership (leading to the formation of the Socialist Party) created an ideological cleavage that persisted through the 1960s splits.

A student cuts a 2 cm segment from the middle of the elongation zone of a maize root and places it in a nutrient medium. Predict whether this segment will increase in length over 24 hours, and justify your prediction using the concept of "determinate vs. indeterminate growth" in that phase.

A multinational tech firm plans to build a new hyperscale data centre in India to support its AI‑driven services. The firm’s sustainability pledge requires that 80 % of the centre’s electricity come from renewable sources within five years. The government’s latest *National Renewable Energy Policy* offers a 15 % tax credit for firms that locate facilities in states with ≥ 30 % renewable‑energy grid share and mandates annual reporting of Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE). The firm’s engineering team has identified three candidate sites:  
- Site A (Gujarat): current grid renewable share 28 %, projected to reach 35 % in 3 years; land cost ₹ 1 200 / sq m; average ambient temperature 32 °C.  
- Site B (Karnataka): grid renewable share 42 % (already above threshold); land cost ₹ 1 500 / sq m; ambient temperature 27 °C.  
- Site C (Maharashtra): grid renewable share 22 %, projected 30 % in 5 years; land cost ₹ 1 300 / sq m; ambient temperature 30 °C.  
Each site’s expected IT load is 150 MW. The firm’s internal model estimates that cooling power = 0.45 × IT load × (T_ambient – 20) / 10 (in MW), where T_ambient is in °C. The base PUE (without cooling) is 1.2. The firm must also plan for e‑waste: servers have a 5‑year lifespan, and the firm aims to recycle 90 % of discarded hardware via certified e‑waste recyclers, as per *E‑Waste Management Rules 2022*.  

Using the data above, answer the following.

(E) Compute the overall annual PUE for each site, given base PUE = 1.2 and cooling power as calculated in Part A.

A school health survey finds 56% of adolescent girls anaemic (NFHS-3 data cited in textbook). The school serves a mid-day meal providing 400 kcal, 12g protein, 3mg iron (from fortified wheat flour), 0mg vitamin C, 100mg calcium. Students typically drink tea at home before school. Using the five food group framework and the food→nutrition→health→fitness chain, design a modified mid-day meal that: (a) adds ≤50 kcal, (b) provides ≥5mg additional absorbable iron, (c) includes vitamin C for absorption, (d) uses locally available foods, (e) respects vegetarian preferences. Justify each addition using Table 1 nutrient profiles.

VaxiGen, a mid‑size pharmaceutical firm, is conducting a Phase‑III trial of its mRNA vaccine across 15 sites in India. Each site employs Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) who verify informed consent, monitor adverse events, and ensure protocol compliance. A supervisor oversees the CRAs, performing functions such as: (i) confirming that every CRA has completed mandatory GCP training before site activation, (ii) reviewing weekly safety reports, (iii) coordinating logistics for sample shipments, (iv) motivating CRAs who face long travel and high workload, (v) fostering a collaborative leadership style to integrate site investigators, data managers, and regulatory affairs, and (vi) addressing communication barriers arising from varied site‑specific SOPs. The firm has capitalized Rs. 120 crore of R&D expenditure, to be amortized over 5 years. Per‑capita income data (Public Facilities) shows significant disparity between states, influencing vaccine price sensitivity.

(B) Calculate the annual depreciation expense for the R&D asset if the company capitalizes Rs. 120 crore over 5 years with zero salvage value using straight‑line method.

Design a hypothetical climate profile for a new town located at 3,500 meters altitude in the western Himalayas, compared to a town at sea level in the Indo-Gangetic plain at the same latitude. Describe their expected temperature differences and explain which geographic factors cause them.

The Union government launched a ₹13 000‑crore Millets Mission under POSHAN Abhiyaan to increase millet procurement for PDS and mid‑day meals, aiming to diversify away from water‑intensive wheat‑rice systems. Punjab and Haryana, reliant on canal irrigation, warn of revenue loss from reduced wheat procurement. Meanwhile, Odisha and Chhattisgarh see an opportunity to boost tribal incomes. The mission invokes lessons from the Green Revolution’s focus on high‑yielding varieties (HYVs) and the White Revolution’s cooperative model, while historians note parallels to colonial cash‑crop pushes that altered regional trade patterns. Using concepts from planning, agricultural‑industry debate, historical trade, and centre‑state fiscal relations, evaluate the mission’s economic and social implications.

(D) Historians argue that colonial emphasis on cash‑crop exports (e.g., indigo, opium) altered India’s terms of trade against manufactured goods. Using the concept of “sectoral terms of trade” from c11_hist_cbse_01_009, explain how a deteriorating agricultural terms of trade would affect the feasibility of a Green‑Revolution‑style HYV push in the 1960s.

Predict the number of unpaired electrons and magnetic moment (spin-only) for [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ and [CoF₆]³⁻. Both are octahedral Co³⁺ (d⁶). Given: Δo(NH₃) = 22,900 cm⁻¹, Δo(F⁻) = 13,000 cm⁻¹, P(Co³⁺) = 21,000 cm⁻¹.

A coastal district frequently affected by flooding and cyclones needs a reliable communication links between block headquarters, relief camps, and the state disaster management centre. The network must support voice, low‑latency data, and live video feeds from rescue drones. Existing infrastructure includes elevated concrete poles along highways, underground ducts in urban towns, and a few legacy microwave towers. The total budget for new outdoor plant (cabling, poles, antennas) is ₹2.2 crore. The solution must integrate with the state’s digital archive of disaster‑response protocols (historical), comply with National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) guidelines on redundancy and interoperability (political), and cope with geographical challenges such as saline soil, river crossings, and high humidity. Students are asked to evaluate transmission media options, propose a resilient media mix, and justify the selection using technical, historical, political, and geographical criteria.

(B) Each block headquarters needs to send a 2 Mbps voice channel and a 4 Mbps video feed to the state centre. If there are 8 blocks, compute the total aggregate bandwidth required (ignore overhead).

PrecisionGears Ltd., a mid‑size auto‑component manufacturer in Pune, produces gear blanks and finished gears for OEMs. The company runs three shifts, consumes 15,000 kWh/day of electricity, and purchases raw material (alloy steel bars) worth ₹2.4 crore monthly. Its legacy accounting system records machine hour usage manually, leading to 10% absenteeism‑related idle time being missed, and raw‑material wastage is estimated at 4% of input weight. Monthly overhead allocation based on direct labour hours results in over‑costing of high‑volume products by 8%. Management is evaluating a CAS package (₹6,80,000 setup, ₹90,000 annual maintenance) that promises: real‑time machine‑hour capture (IoT sensors), automatic scrap‑weight tracking, activity‑based costing (ABC) engine, and role‑based dashboards for shop‑floor supervisors. The firm’s cost of capital is 10%. Using the five explicit CAS advantages, assess the investment while linking to cost accounting concepts (activity‑based costing, variance analysis) and basic statistics (control charts) for monitoring process stability.

(E) Discuss how CAS‑ensured data confidentiality (role‑based access, encryption) protects sensitive production‑cost data, and explain two macroeconomic effects if such data were leaked and used by competitors to undercut prices in the domestic auto‑component market.

A public‑health NGO designs a mobile‑app screening tool for adolescent depression. Clinicians write risk‑rules in infix notation using variables (e.g., **S** = sleep‑hours <6, **A** = anxiety‑score >8, **I** = isolation‑frequency >3 days/week, **F** = family‑conflict score >5) and operators **+** (OR), **·** (AND), **^** (NOT). An example rule: **(S + A) · (I ^ F)**. To enable real‑time evaluation on low‑power phones, the NGO’s backend must convert each clinician‑written infix rule into postfix notation, then evaluate it using a stack. The tool must respect precedence: **^** > **·** > **+**, left‑associativity for **+** and **·** , right‑associativity for **^**. Parentheses override default precedence. The NGO also wants to log the number of stack push/pop operations per rule for performance auditing.

(C) If the clinician changes the rule to **S + A · I ^ F** (no parentheses), what is the resulting postfix expression? Show stack state after each token.
Explain why the Quit India Movement became the most widespread and violent uprising since 1857, despite Gandhi's insistence on non-violence and the arrest of all top leaders within 24 hours.

A field of Bt‑cotton (GM crop) releases transgenic pollen at a uniform rate Q = 1.0 × 10⁶ grains s⁻¹. Pollen transport is modeled by a steady‑state Gaussian plume in a uniform wind of speed u = 2.0 m s⁻¹. The diffusion coefficient for pollen in the turbulent atmospheric layer is D = 0.5 m² s⁻¹. The concentration at ground level on the centreline (y = 0, z = 0) at downwind distance x is given by  

\[
C(x)=\frac{Q}{2\pi u \sigma_y \sigma_z},
\qquad 
\sigma_y=\sigma_z=\sqrt{\frac{2 D x}{u}} .
\]

A wild relative of cotton is considered effectively contaminated if the airborne pollen concentration exceeds C_thr = 10 grains m⁻³ for a continuous exposure of t = 600 s. Pollen deposition onto the stigma follows a Poisson process with mean λ = C·V·t·ε, where the effective inhaled (or intercepted) volume V = 1.0 × 10⁻³ m³ s⁻¹ and deposition efficiency ε = 0.05. Biosafety guidelines require that the expected transgene frequency in the wild population after one cross‑pollination event stay below L = 0.001 (0.1 %). The transgene transfer efficiency per pollen grain is τ = 1.0 × 10⁻⁴.

Using the above data, answer the following sub‑parts.

(B) At the distance x₀ found in Part A, compute the probability P that a stigma receives at least one transgenic pollen grain during the exposure period t = 600 s.

The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) needs rapid mapping of a flash flood in the Alaknanda valley (Uttarakhand) within 24 hours. Cloud cover is 60% at satellite overpass time. Compare three options: (a) Satellite optical (Cartosat-3), (b) Satellite SAR (RISAT-1A), (c) Aerial photography (drone/aircraft). Evaluate each on: geometric fidelity for flood extent, temporal resolution, cloud penetration, and operational feasibility in the Himalayas. Recommend the best option with justification.

A central‑state consortium commissions a GIS‑based impact study of PMGSY‑III roads in the Indo‑Gangetic plain. The study overlays road‑network layers with satellite‑derived crop‑yield maps (wheat and rice) and APMC (agricultural produce market committee) price data. Results show that blocks gaining all‑weather roads experience a 22 % increase in marketed surplus and a 15 % reduction in post‑harvest losses, but also a 9 % rise in fertilizer‑nitrate runoff into adjacent water bodies, correlating with intensive HYV cultivation promoted during the Green Revolution. Farmer cooperatives protest that the road‑induced market integration favours large traders, squeezing smallholders’ bargaining power. The state planning commission proposes a conditional grant: additional PMGSY funding only if districts adopt precision‑agriculture subsidies to curb runoff. Students must analyse the geographical, sociological, and environmental‑economic linkages.

(C) How does the spatial diffusion of PMGSY roads interact with the Green Revolution’s irrigation expansion to produce uneven regional development, according to core‑periphery theory?

Three partners — Aria (40%), Ben (35%), Cara (25%) — run "NexaPay", a UPI-based fintech startup. Their partnership deed states: (i) On retirement, goodwill = 3 years' purchase of super-profits (EVA basis: NOPAT - WACC×Capital Employed); (ii) Intellectual Property (payment gateway algorithm) revalued at fair value using relief-from-royalty method; (iii) Continuing partners acquire retiring partner's share in their capital ratio; (iv) Capitals adjusted via current accounts. Cara retires on 31-Mar-2025. Data: Capital Employed ₹12 Cr (Aria ₹5 Cr, Ben ₹4 Cr, Cara ₹3 Cr); WACC 12%; NOPAT ₹2.4 Cr; Algorithm royalty rate 8% on ₹50 Cr revenue; General Reserve ₹1.2 Cr; Profit & Loss Dr. ₹20 L; Cara's loan ₹50 L at 10% interest. Continuing partners agree to settle Cara via: 30% cash, 40% 2-year zero-coupon bonds (yield 9%), 30% equity in new subsidiary "NexaLend" valued at ₹8 Cr post-money.

(E) Pass journal entries for Cara's retirement (goodwill, revaluation, reserves, settlement).

In a school laboratory, you have convex lenses of focal lengths 10 cm, 15 cm, 20 cm, and 30 cm. You need to make a combination of power exactly +6.0 D using any two lenses in contact. Which pair will you choose? Show calculations. If no pair gives exactly +6.0 D, suggest a third lens (type and power) to add to the closest pair to achieve exactly +6.0 D.

In 2024, Lena, a 27‑year‑old freelance platform worker in Kiruna, Sweden, assembles and sells DIY electronic “rat‑trap” kits (IoT‑enabled motion sensors) through an online marketplace. She purchases cheap components from bulk warehouses, assembles them at night, and ships them to hobby‑farmers across Europe. Her average monthly earnings are €850 after platform fees; she works 12 hrs/day, 6 days/week, and reports chronic fatigue and anxiety (stress score 7/10). Lena lives in a company‑owned apartment near the Kiruna iron‑ore mine, where her great‑grandfather worked as a miner in the 1920s earning the equivalent of €150/month (adjusted for inflation) under hazardous conditions. Sweden’s universal welfare system provides her with basic healthcare and unemployment insurance, but she is ineligible for sick leave because she is classified as “self‑employed.”  
Using the story “The Rattrap,” analyze how Lena’s predicament reflects the protagonist’s struggle to “keep body and soul together,” how the rattrap metaphor operates as a symbol of exploitative labor systems across eras, and what psychological and sociological mechanisms might enable her to experience “unwonted joy” or awaken essential goodness through solidarity.  
Data: Historical miner wage (1920s) ≈ €150/month; current gig‑economy average hourly wage ≈ €1.18; Swedish welfare replacement rate for unemployed ≈ 80% of prior income; probability of developing depressive symptoms in precarious work ≈ 0.35.

(D) Analyze how the metaphor of an “impenetrable prison” in the story reflects geographical constraints on labor mobility in Kiruna’s iron‑ore dependent economy, using the geography node.

A municipal planning agency has collected summer daytime land‑surface temperature (LST) from satellite imagery for 30 wards of a metropolitan city, together with ward‑level average annual household income (in lakhs INR), percentage of green cover, and population density (persons/km²). Preliminary inspection shows LST and income are right‑skewed (skewness ≈ 1.2–1.5) and contain a few extreme wards (e.g., one industrial ward with LST = 45 °C and income = 5 lakhs). To build a heat‑vulnerability index suitable for regression analysis and to compare results with other cities that use different measurement units, the analyst must (i) choose an appropriate transformation to reduce skewness, (ii) normalise the transformed variables to a common scale, (iii) compute association measures between heat exposure and socio‑economic status, and (iv) interpret the findings in light of horizontal power‑sharing arrangements and the accounting branch responsible for evaluating the cost‑benefit of green‑infrastructure investments.  

For illustration, the following data for five representative wards are provided:

| Ward | LST (°C) | Income (lakhs) | Green Cover % | Density (persons/km²) |
|------|----------|----------------|--------------|-----------------------|
| W1 | 30 | 1.5 | 10 | 8 000 |
| W2 | 32 | 2.0 | 15 | 10 000 |
| W3 | 35 | 2.5 | 20 | 12 000 |
| W4 | 38 | 3.0 | 25 | 14 000 |
| W5 | 45 | 5.0 | 30 | 18 000 |

All calculations may be performed on this subset; the same procedures extend to the full 30‑ward dataset.

(C) Normalise the household‑income data using the z‑score method. Provide the z‑score for each ward.

Rising temperatures and erratic rainfall in the Satpura‑Maikal range have reduced mahua flowering by 40 % over the past decade, threatening the livelihood of Gond forest‑dependent communities. A state‑run “Climate Resilient Livelihoods” programme (₹8 crore) proposes to relocate 2 000 families to nearby urban fringes, providing skill‑training in textile weaving. Tribal leaders resist, arguing that relocation severs the link between the Gond baiga’s storytelling and the forest ecosystem that supplies metaphors (river, mahua, tiger). The programme’s environmental impact assessment cites a 2022 IPCC report projecting a 2 °C rise by 2050 for the region. Students must analyse the primary theme of the storyteller in light of ecological loss, evaluate the protagonist’s role as ecological interpreter, decode key metaphors, assess the displacement policy against constitutional safeguards for tribal rights, and suggest an ecologically sensitive alternative using geographical data on forest cover and migration corridors.

(E) Using forest‑cover and migration‑corridor data, propose two alternative interventions that preserve both livelihood and storytelling ecology.

The Cauvery Water Dispute Tribunal’s final award (2020) allocates 404.25 tmcft to Karnataka, 284.75 tmcft to Tamil Nadu, 30 tmcft to Kerala, and 7 tmcft to Puducherry annually. Recent monsoon deficits have reduced actual inflows to 60% of the long‑term average, intensifying tensions. Simultaneously, the NITI Aayog’s Composite Water Management Index shows Karnataka scoring 0.62 (medium) and Tamil Nadu 0.55 (low) in watershed management efficiency. A central water authority must decide whether to (a) treat each riparian state’s claim as unique (areal differentiation) or (b) view the Cauvery basin as an integrated hydrological‑socio‑economic system (regional analysis) when designing a dynamic allocation mechanism that also accounts for agricultural productivity (accounting for crop water‑use efficiency) and constitutional provisions under Article 262 (inter‑state water disputes). Use the data below to assess the suitability of each approach.

State | Allocated Water (tmcft) | Actual Availability 2023 (% of allocation) | Primary Crop Water Use Efficiency (kg grain per m³ water) | Per‑capita Income (₹)
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Karnataka | 404.25 | 55 | 0.45 | 2,10,000
| Tamil Nadu | 284.75 | 48 | 0.38 | 1,85,000
| Kerala | 30.00 | 70 | 0.52 | 1,90,000
| Puducherry | 7.00 | 80 | 0.30 | 2,00,000

(A) Define areal differentiation and explain how it would lead the authority to treat each state’s water claim as unique rather than a proportional share of basin inflow.

In 2024, a 22‑year‑old Hindi poet‑activist named Aarav launches a viral Instagram series titled “कँ वि क्फ़्गट” (Can Vikfgt), posting a new 14‑line poem each day that critiques the government’s new data‑localisation law. Within three weeks, the series garners 1.2 million views, 85 k shares, and triggers a police notice under IT Act §66A (later struck down). Aarav’s followers include 60 % urban college students (average age 20) and 40 % rural youth who access the posts via community‑center Wi‑Fi hotspots. A recent TRAI report shows rural broadband penetration at 38 % versus urban 78 %. Aarav’s poems repeatedly employ metaphors of “broken mirrors” and “silenced drums” to depict existential fatigue, yet end with a refrain “हम अभी भी चल रहे हैं” (We still walk on). Using textual evidence from the poem series, historical parallels to the 1930‑31 Civil Disobedience Movement, constitutional freedom of speech provisions, and the digital‑divide geography, analyze Aarav as the protagonist.

(D) Evaluate how the constitutional right to freedom of speech (pol_12_05) protects Aarav’s poetic expression, considering the IT Act notice and the subsequent judicial striking down of §66A. Identify one limitation of this protection in the scenario.

Write a 4-line stanza in Braj Bhasha (or Hindi approximating its rhythm) from the perspective of a young woman in 1920s rural India who has just discovered Vaddhegnasoh's poems. Let the stanza express what reading her work makes her feel.

A research team wants to over‑express a thermostable lipase (MW ≈ 50 kDa) in E. coli BL21(DE3) for industrial biodiesel production. The gene is cloned into a pBR322‑derived plasmid (copy number ≈ 50) containing a T7 lac operator promoter, a Shine‑Dalgarno sequence, a C‑terminal His₆ tag, and a rho‑independent terminator. Induction is performed with IPTG. The lipase activity follows Arrhenius behaviour with activation energy Eₐ = 50 kJ·mol⁻¹. The culture is grown to OD₆₀₀ ≈ 0.6 (≈ 1 × 10⁹ cells·mL⁻¹), induced with IPTG, and incubated for 4 h at 30 °C. mRNA half‑life is 2 min, translation initiation rate is 20 proteins·mRNA⁻¹·min⁻¹, and protein degradation is negligible over the induction period. Purification via Ni‑NTA gives 80 % recovery. Using the data below, answer the sub‑questions.

**Given:**  
- T7 promoter strength = 100 transcripts·plasmid⁻¹·min⁻¹  
- Basal leak of T7 lac promoter = 1 % of maximal activity  
- Hill coefficient for IPTG binding (n) = 2, dissociation constant Kd = 0.1 mM  
- Avogadro’s number Nₐ = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹

(A) Which promoter system (lac vs T7 lac operator) would minimise basal expression while providing the highest inducible yield for this lipase, and why?

In the industrial production of ammonia (NH₃), 28.0g of nitrogen gas reacts with 6.0g of hydrogen gas to form 34.0g of ammonia. If a different batch uses 14.0g of nitrogen, what mass of hydrogen is needed for complete reaction, and what mass of ammonia will be produced? Assume the law holds.

A 2025 UN‑commissioned report on “Future Cities” proposes a pilot project: a subterranean transit layer beneath Mumbai’s Bandra‑Kurla Complex, designed to replicate 1960s Bombay aesthetics—vintage signage, steam‑era locomotives, and period‑appropriate ticket counters—to combat citizen stress caused by hyper‑digital urban life. The project’s sociologists argue it will foster collective nostalgia, boosting social cohesion. Critics, citing political theory, warn that such manufactured utopias risk creating “false consciousness” by distracting citizens from structural issues like housing inequality and pollution. Meanwhile, a historian notes that actual 1960s Bombay faced severe communal riots, water shortages, and a booming black market for railway tickets. Using the concepts of irony and symbolism from *The Third Level* (Charley’s psychiatrist, his grandfather’s era, the stamp collection, and the description of the third level), analyze how the story’s irony and symbolism serve as a cautionary tale for contemporary utopian urban projects, and assess whether the Mumbai proposal mirrors or diverges from Charley’s escape.

(D) Apply the sociology node (Collective Memory and Nostalgia) to Charley’s stamp collecting. Determine whether his behavior exemplifies *restorative* or *reflective* nostalgia, and discuss the implications for the Mumbai project’s design.

In Berlin, the “Renewal Committee” organizes a commemorative event marking the 80th anniversary of Auschwitz’s liberation. The program includes a symbolic wedding ceremony to represent rebirth. Approximately 120 participants attend: 30 % are second‑generation Holocaust survivors, 25 % are local politicians, 20 % are cultural activists, and the remaining 25 % are community volunteers. The event runs for 3 hours, with 45 minutes allocated to speeches, 60 minutes to the ceremonial wedding, and the rest to open dialogue.

Leah, a 28‑year‑old Jewish historian employed at the city’s archives, is invited to present a paper on survivor testimonies. Her partner, Mark, a freelance graphic designer, repeatedly urges her to skip the academic session and join the evening’s social reception, arguing that “the community needs to see you celebrating, not just mourning.” Leah feels torn: she believes her scholarly work honors the dead, yet she also senses pressure to appear publicly engaged in communal healing.

In the scenario, Mark’s insistence parallels Gretl’s role in the original story, where Gretl urges Dr. Solomon Margolin to attend social events despite his communal obligations. Other supporting‑character analogues include: Mr. Weiss (an elderly survivor who shares fragmented memories) as Abraham Mekheles; Ms. Novak (a matchmaker arranging the ceremonial dance) as Raizel; a group of Romani activists advocating for recognition as the Senciminer/Tereshpoler guests; Amir, a Syrian refugee taxi driver who observes the crowd silently; and Frau Keller, the event’s strict coordinator, embodying the wedding functionaries.

(E) Assess how Frau Keller’s strict enforcement of the event schedule reflects bureaucratic indifference toward trauma‑related narratives, using the political‑science node on minority rights and the supporting‑character node.
Fill in the blank: Imagine you run a small kirana store in Delhi selling ______ milk at ₹60 per litre, selling 100 litres daily.

A 2023 graphic novel “Nagar Ka Darpan” depicts a megacity where every streetlamp doubles as a facial‑recognition camera. The recurring visual motif is a cracked mirror reflected in the glass of each lamp, showing fragmented faces of passersby. The author states in an interview that the mirror “represents the shattered self under constant watch”. Sales data show the novel sold 2.4 lakhs copies in metros but only 12 k in towns with < 5 lakh population, where CCTV density is 0.2 per km² versus 4.8 per km² in metros. Using irony and symbolism concepts, analyse how the cracked‑mirror motif operates as a symbol and whether the novel’s reception exhibits situational irony regarding its intended audience.

(D) Apply the geography node c11_geo_cbse_01_005 to explain why the novel’s symbolism resonates more in metros than in smaller towns, using data on CCTV density and vertical urban form.

Serum Institute of India (SII) became the world's largest vaccine manufacturer by doses. In 2020, SII partnered with AstraZeneca/Oxford to manufacture Covishield (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19). Identify the THREE most critical pre-existing capabilities SII leveraged to scale from zero to 100+ million doses/month within 6 months.

An industrial microbiologist wants to maximize penicillin yield in a 100,000 L bioreactor. The current process uses a batch mode with glucose as carbon source. Penicillin is a secondary metabolite. Propose two specific process modifications (with biochemical reasoning) to increase titer, referencing the growth-production phase relationship.

Fill in the blank: Start with a real-world observation: "Check the IMD rainfall map for your district — you'll see some years get 1200 mm while others get 600 mm, and July might be dry while August floods." Connect to Class 11's monsoon mechanism (ITCZ, jet streams) and rainfall ______.

EduTech, an AI‑driven tutoring startup, plans **autonomous investment I = 600 bn** for server farms and content development. The economy’s saving function is **S = –100 + 0.15Y** (bn). EduTech will capitalize content creation as an intangible asset and amortize it straight‑line over 4 years (no salvage). Annual amortization expense is therefore **80 bn** (assuming 320 bn of content capitalized). Human cognitive research shows that the average sustained attention span for online learning is limited to **20 minutes per day**, imposing a ceiling on monetizable hours per user and thus on the revenue that can justify further investment. This biological constraint means that beyond a certain user base, additional investment in content yields diminishing returns, potentially making part of the planned investment induced rather than purely autonomous. Students must determine equilibrium income, the multiplier, the effect of an investment change, journalize the intangible‑asset amortization, and evaluate how the attention‑span biological limit influences the investment assumption.

(D) Journalize the annual amortization of the intangible content asset (80 bn) and show its effect on the accounting equation.

A metropolitan city experiences an unprecedented heat‑wave with daytime temperatures peaking at 48 °C for five consecutive days. Street vendors selling perishable goods (fruits, vegetables) report spoilage rates rising from 10 % to 35 % due to inadequate refrigeration. The municipal corporation issues an advisory urging residents to stay indoors, but many vendors cannot afford to lose daily income. A survey of 120 vendors shows: average daily income dropped from ₹ 800 to ₹ 460; self‑reported stress scores (on a 10‑point scale) rose from 3 to 7; 62 % report difficulty concentrating on transactions; 41 % admit to increased irritability with customers; 28 % note frequent headaches. Ambient noise levels at marketplaces have risen to 70 dB due to increased traffic rerouting. The city’s disaster‑management fund has been overspent by 18 % (original allocation ₹ 200 cr, actual ₹ 236 cr). Local hospitals report a 22 % rise in cases of heat‑related exhaustion and a 9 % rise in visits for anxiety‑related symptoms. Using this information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(B) For a vendor who thinks, “If I close my stall today, I will not be able to pay my child’s school fee,” identify the **secondary appraisal** component (coping potential) according to Lazarus.

MediLife Ltd., a large pharmaceutical firm, acquires BioNova Ltd., a biotech startup, for an enterprise value of ₹4,200 cr. The deal is financed through a special purpose vehicle (SPV) called MediLife Bio Holdings. MediLife contributes ₹1,200 cr equity, BioNova’s promoters roll over ₹300 cr equity, and the SPV raises ₹2,500 cr term loan at 9 % interest (tax‑deductible) and ₹200 cr of 8 % cumulative redeemable preference shares (treated as equity for accounting but debt‑like for cost). Fixed capital of BioNova includes: land ₹400 cr, R&D building ₹500 cr, specialized bioreactors ₹1,200 cr, and patents (intangible) ₹600 cr. The combined firm expects synergies adding ₹150 cr annual EBITDA for 10 years. Tax rate 25 %. Depreciation on tangible assets straight‑line over 20 years; patents amortized over 10 years. The management must assess (i) whether land, building, bioreactors and patents qualify as fixed capital, (ii) how the financing mix (equity, debt, preference shares) affects the overall cost of capital, (iii) the impact on the firm’s capital structure (debt‑to‑equity ratio), (iv) the NPV of the acquisition using free cash flow to the firm (FCFF), and (v) the working‑capital need assuming 12 % of fixed capital.

(B) Compute the after‑tax cost of debt, cost of preference shares (treated as equity for cost), and the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) for the SPV given: Equity (MediLife + promoters) ₹1,500 cr @14 %; Debt ₹2,500 cr @9 %; Preference shares ₹200 cr @8 %; tax rate 25 %.

A rural primary health centre in Rajasthan serves a population of 12,000, of which 18 % are adults aged ≥ 60 years. Recent screening shows 22 % of these elderly have type 2 diabetes mellitus. The health worker must design a culturally acceptable, low‑cost therapeutic diet using locally available millets (bajra, jowar, ragi) and pulses (moong, urad) that can be procured through the Public Distribution System (PDS) at subsidized rates. The diet must meet the following criteria for a 68‑year‑old woman weighing 58 kg, height 152 cm, lightly active (household chores): total energy ≈ 1,800 kcal/day, carbohydrates 50‑55 % of kcal, protein 15‑20 %, fat 25‑30 %, fiber ≥ 25 g/day, and glycemic load kept low by favoring low‑GI millets (bajra GI 54, jowar GI 62, ragi GI 68) and pulses (moong GI 30, urad GI 43). PDS provides bajra at INR 22/kg, jowar at INR 20/kg, ragi at INR 25/kg, moong dal at INR 70/kg, urad dal at INR 65/kg, and subsidized rice at INR 32/kg (but rice is higher GI). The worker also needs to consider seasonal availability: bajra and jowar are abundant in winter, ragi in monsoon. Using principles of therapeutic diet planning, calculate the energy requirement, macronutrient grams, propose a feasible daily menu (quantities in grams) that satisfies carbohydrate, fiber, and GI constraints, and estimate the daily cost based on PDS prices.

(C) Propose a daily menu (quantities in grams) using bajra, jowar, moong dal, and urad dal that meets the carbohydrate (≥ 230 g) and fiber (≥ 25 g) goals while keeping the overall glycemic index low (weighted average GI < 55). Use the following nutrient approximations per 100 g: bajra (carb 72 g, fiber 11.3 g, GI 54), jowar (carb 75 g, fiber 1.6 g, GI 62), moong dal (carb 60 g, fiber 7.9 g, GI 30), urad dal (carb 58 g, fiber 3.2 g, GI 43). Show calculations for total carbs, fiber, and weighted GI.

A student prepares a 0.8% agarose gel in 1× TAE buffer to separate a restriction digest expected to yield fragments of 8 kb, 5 kb, and 3 kb. After running at 100 V for 30 minutes, the dye front has moved 6 cm, but the 8 kb and 5 kb bands are not resolved (appear as one thick band), while the 3 kb band is sharp and well-separated. The student says, "I need a higher percentage gel to separate the large bands better." Critique this statement and propose a correct solution with reasoning.
Fill in the blank: Observe your electricity bill — over 70% of that ______ comes from burning coal.

In the peri‑urban zone of Gurugram, a cluster of dairy farms reports sudden drop in milk yield and abortions in buffaloes. Laboratory confirmation identifies *Brucella melitensis* as the causative agent, with an estimated 12 % prevalence among the 8 000 buffalo population. The local animal husbandry department has ₹ 2.5 crore allocated for a one‑year extension intervention aimed at reducing brucellosis prevalence to < 2 % through vaccination, test‑and‑slaughter, and farmer education. Stakeholders include peri‑urban dairy cooperatives (40 % of farms), migrant laborers (30 % of workforce), and urban consumers concerned about milk safety. The extension officer must draw on: (i) biological knowledge of Brucella’s life‑cycle and transmission routes (direct contact, ingestion of raw milk, aerosols), (ii) accounting principles for budget allocation across vaccination, compensation, IEC (Information, Education, Communication), and monitoring, and (iii) behavioural insights (health belief model, trust, and incentive structures) to motivate farmers to adopt bio‑security practices and consent to testing. Design a comprehensive programme plan that integrates these domains.

(B) The total budget of ₹ 2.5 crore is to be divided as follows: 45 % for vaccine procurement, 20 % for compensation to farmers whose animals test positive and are culled, 25 % for IEC campaigns, and the remainder for monitoring & evaluation. Calculate the amount (in lakhs) allocated to M&E and identify the accounting principle that ensures this amount is not inadvertently used for vaccine purchase.

The ISS uses a solid‑polymer electrolyte electrolyzer to produce O₂ for crew respiration. Water is split at the anode: 2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻; at the cathode: 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂ (which is vented). The electrolyzer operates at a constant current of 7.5 A and a cell voltage of 1.85 V. The produced O₂ is collected at 298 K and 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa. Determine (i) the moles of O₂ generated per hour, (ii) the volume of O₂ (in litres) produced per hour, (iii) the Gibbs free energy change per mole of O₂ under these conditions, (iv) the theoretical minimum voltage required for water splitting at 298 K, and (v) how the actual voltage compares to the minimum, indicating the overpotential and its origin (activation, ohmic, concentration). Assume ideal gas behaviour and 100 % current efficiency.

(D) Determine the theoretical minimum voltage (E°) required for water splitting at 298 K using standard Gibbs free energy of formation (ΔG_f°[H₂O(l)] = –237.13 kJ mol⁻¹).

(1) Interpret a 24-hour dietary recall of an adolescent and identify at least three deviations from the ICMR food group guidelines and RDA 2020 values, and (2) design a one-day balanced meal plan for a 16-year-old vegetarian girl with moderate activity that meets ≥90% of RDA for energy, protein, iron, and.

A private aerospace firm is preparing for the maiden launch of a reusable rocket. The propulsion lead, Ms. Aria (28 y), witnesses a fuel‑valve leak that forces an abort seconds before ignition. That night she awakens unable to grip tools with her right hand despite normal sensation and strength on neurological exam. Over the next week she repeatedly checks her hand for signs of injury, researches “stroke” online, and reports persistent fear of permanent disability. During the debrief she cannot recall the exact sequence of the valve leak, describing a “blank” for 15 minutes before the abort. Meanwhile, the finance officer, Mr. Rohan, notices that the budget line for “contingency reserves” shows an unexplained ₹12 lakhs overspend, traced to duplicate entries made during the high‑stress abort‑day shift. The firm’s internal audit policy requires dual‑approval for any reserve transfer; both approvals were signed by Rohan under time pressure.  
Using DSM‑5, biology of stress, and accounting control concepts, answer the following.

(A) Which DSM‑5 diagnosis best explains Ms. Aria’s loss of hand function given normal neurological findings and excessive health‑related anxiety?

A miniature imaging spectrometer is to be flown on a CubeSat to measure the ultraviolet‑visible reflectance spectrum of an exoplanet in order to detect ozone (O₃) absorption bands near 250 nm (Hartley band) and 600 nm (Chappuis band). The instrument uses a fused‑silica prism (refractive index described by the Sellmeier equation n(λ)=√[1+ 0.6961663λ²/(λ²−0.0684043²)+ 0.4079426λ²/(λ²−0.1162414²)+ 0.8974794λ²/(λ²−9.896161²)], λ in µm) with refracting angle A = 60°. A collimated beam of wavelength λ enters the prism at angle of incidence i and emerges at angle e. The spectrometer records the angular deviation δ(λ)=i+e−A. To resolve the two ozone bands, the angular dispersion dδ/dλ must be at least 0.02° nm⁻¹ across 250–600 nm. The detector is a silicon CCD with quantum efficiency QE(λ) that peaks at 0.85 at 500 nm and falls to 0.3 at 250 nm and 600 nm. The satellite’s power budget allows a maximum incident optical power of 10 µW on the prism to avoid thermal drift.  
**(a)** Determine the angle of minimum deviation Dₘ for λ = 500 nm using the given Sellmeier equation.  
**(b)** Compute the angular dispersion dδ/dλ at λ = 500 nm and verify whether the required resolution is met.  
**(c)** If the incident beam is angled such that i = 45°, find the corresponding angle of emergence e and the deviation δ for λ = 250 nm.  
**(d)** Estimate the number of photoelectrons generated per second in the CCD pixel collecting the 250 nm band, assuming the prism introduces a transmission loss of 15 % and the pixel subtends a solid angle of 1 µsr.  
**(e)** Discuss how changing the prism material to BK7 (n_BK7(λ)≈1.51+0.0045/λ²) would affect the minimum deviation and dispersion, and whether the instrument would still satisfy the resolution requirement.

(B) Derive an expression for angular dispersion dδ/dλ in terms of dn/dλ and prism angle A, then evaluate it at λ=500 nm for the fused‑silica prism. State whether the required resolution of 0.02° nm⁻¹ is achieved.
Assuming each HSC division consumes 2 ATP per nucleotide incorporated and the genome is 3.2 Gb, estimate the ATP demand per cell per hour at μ=0.03 h⁻¹. (Use 1 mol ATP ≈ 6.022×10²³ molecules.)

In a nuclear physics experiment, a student measures the activity of a radioactive sample at regular intervals and obtains the following data:
Time (min): 0, 10, 20, 30, 40
Activity (counts/s): 1000, 610, 372, 227, 139
The student plots ln(Activity) vs Time and gets a straight line with slope = -0.049 min⁻¹ and intercept = ln(1000). 
(a) Determine the half-life of the sample in minutes.
(b) The student claims the decay constant is 0.049 s⁻¹. Identify and correct the error.
(c) If the sample initially contained 2.0 × 10¹⁰ nuclei, calculate the number of nuclei remaining after 1 hour.
(d) The student's lab partner argues that since the activity drops to ~14% in 40 min, the half-life must be less than 20 min. Evaluate this reasoning.

A remote tribal cluster in Arunachal Pradesh (population ~4,200) gains access to a low‑Earth‑orbit satellite internet service (downlink 30 Mbps, uplink 5 Mbps) in January 2024. The community sets up a cooperative e‑commerce platform to sell handicrafts nationally. Personal communication (WhatsApp groups, voice calls) is used for order confirmation, while mass communication (local FM radio, community‑managed YouTube channel) advertises products. Transport of goods relies on existing roadways to the nearest district hub (120 km) and then rail to major markets. The cooperative invested ₹18 lakhs in satellite terminals and ₹4 lakhs in solar power; expected monthly revenue is ₹2.5 lakhs after 6 months. Using concepts of personal vs mass communication, transport logistics, historical barter (Jon Beel Mela), and basic accounting (revenue, cost, profit), answer the following.

(E) Evaluate how the cooperative’s use of *mass communication* (FM radio & YouTube) aligns with the principle of *power sharing* in Belgium’s accommodation model (The Belgian Accommodation Model) when considering *regional representation* and *cultural autonomy*.

The Ministry of Home Affairs proposes a nationwide facial‑recognition network linked to Aadhaar to curb rising street crime (reported 22% increase in metro areas, NCRB 2023). Civil‑society groups warn of mass surveillance, citing the 1975‑77 Emergency when civil liberties were suspended. Urban migration data shows 35% of India’s workforce now lives in cities with populations >10 million, raising concerns about algorithmic bias against migrants. In the chapter *tc lsD'ku vkfI+kQlj okbZ-Mh- ;'kksèkj*, the protagonist Raju resists an authoritarian landlord who uses spies to control the village, employing metaphors of “watchful eyes” and “iron chains”. Students must write a PEEL‑structured answer linking Raju’s resistance to contemporary privacy debates, using textual evidence, historical parallels, and urban‑geographic trends.

(D) Discuss how the protagonist’s evolution reflects the chapter’s message about resilience against oppressive systems. (150‑word PEEL)

A government think‑tank releases a policy brief proposing a congestion‑pricing scheme for metro cities to reduce traffic and fund public transport. The brief includes:  
- An executive summary citing projected GDP gains of 1.2% from time‑saved commuting (material wealth angle).  
- A section on equity noting that low‑wage workers relying on two‑wheelers would bear disproportionate financial burden, citing NSSO data on income‑expenditure ratios.  
- A historical annex drawing parallels between London’s 1865 Metropolitan Board of Works debates and ancient Indian nagara‑sabhas (urban councils) that deliberated on road maintenance and taxation.  
- A quotation from Amartya Sen: “Development requires expanding the real freedoms people enjoy, not merely increasing their income.”  
- A concluding recommendation to exempt vehicles below ₹5 lakh price and to reinvest revenues in last‑mile connectivity for informal settlements.  
Students must identify how the brief engages with Sen’s secondary themes: tension between material wealth and human capability, inclusivity across class, legacy of religious heterodoxy (via secular deliberative bodies), and public reasoning as democratic practice.

(B) The equity section’s concern about low‑wage workers’ burden illustrates which secondary theme?

In 2025, a Hyderabad‑based couple—one Hindu, one Muslim—plans a livestreamed wedding that blends Vedic rites and Nikah customs, inviting global viewers via a social‑media platform that uses AI‑driven content moderation to filter “offensive” elements. The livestream garners 2 million concurrent viewers, with analytics showing 45% Hindu, 30% Muslim, 25% other/interfaith audiences. Religious authorities protest that the algorithm suppresses certain rituals (e.g., breaking the glass, Quranic recitation) citing “community‑standard” violations, while tech advocates claim the moderation prevents hate speech and ensures broad accessibility. The couple invokes Singer’s portrayal of Margolin’s tug‑of‑war between personal desire and communal obligation to argue that the livestream, like the story’s wedding, becomes a site where external reality (platform rules, audience metrics) shapes internal consciousness (spiritual meaning, identity). Using the story’s discussion points, examine how the livestream functions as a modern narrative space where consciousness and external forces intersect, and assess implications for religious freedom, digital governance, and diaspora identity.

(A) How does AI‑mediated livestreaming create an ironic tension between the couples’ internal spiritual intentions and the external reality of platform governance?

A research group is synthesizing a series of octahedral rhodium(III) complexes of the type [Rh(L-L)₂Cl(H)], where L-L is a chiral bidentate phosphine ligand (e.g., (R)-BINAP) that coordinates through two phosphorus atoms. The complex is intended as a homogeneous catalyst for the asymmetric hydrogenation of prochiral alkenes. The coordination sphere consists of two chelating L-L ligands occupying four coordination sites, and two monodentate ligands: a chloride ion and a hydride ligand. The team needs to predict: (i) how many distinct geometrical isomers exist for this composition, (ii) which of these are optically active and how many enantiomeric pairs arise, (iii) the expected magnetic moment based on the d-electron count of Rh(III) in an octahedral ligand field, (iv) the total number of stereoisomers if the bidentate ligand were unsymmetrical (e.g., containing two different donor atoms such as P and N), and (v) how replacement of the chloride ligand by a weak-field ligand like iodide would influence the spin state and magnetic behavior according to crystal field theory and the spectrochemical series. Assume that the hydride ligand is a strong-field ligand similar to H⁻, and that the complex remains low-spin unless otherwise indicated. Use the following data: atomic number of Rh = 45; common oxidation state in the complex = +3; ligand field splitting parameter Δ₀ for Cl⁻ ≈ 13,200 cm⁻¹, for I⁻ ≈ 9,200 cm⁻¹; pairing energy P ≈ 20,000 cm⁻¹ for 4d metals.

(D) If the bidentate ligand L‑L were unsymmetrical (e.g., containing donor atoms P and N), calculate the total number of stereoisomers (geometrical + optical) possible for the complex [Rh(L-L)₂Cl(H)], assuming the ligand can bind in two orientations (head‑head, head‑tail, tail‑tail) but the chelate ring remains intact.

The Ministry of Tourism plans a “Bhakti Circuit” linking Varanasi, Vrindavan, and the birthplace of Raidas in Varanasi (Seer Govardhanpur). The project brochure highlights Raidas’s message “मन चंगा तो काठ में में गंगा” to promote spiritual tourism. A parliamentary committee raises concerns: (i) the circuit may commodify bhakti, turning sacred teachings into marketable experiences; (ii) inclusion of Raidas’s site risks highlighting caste‑based labor narratives that could clash with dominant upper‑caste pilgrim expectations; (iii) funds are allocated disproportionately to upper‑caste temple renovations (70 %) vs. Dalit‑heritage sites (30 %). Using Raidas’s primary theme, the historical Bhakti movement’s relationship with royal patronage (c11_his_cbse_02_007), the Directive Principles of State Policy (Article 46 – promotion of educational/economic interests of weaker sections – c11_pol_cbse_03_004), and the sociological concept of cultural commodification (c11_soc_cbse_04_008), the committee must recommend reforms.

(A) State the primary theme of Raidas’s poetry and cite one doha and one biographical detail that illustrate it.
Fill in the blank: Observe the air around you right now — ______, odourless, yet precisely 21% oxygen that allows you to breathe.

GreenProtein, a biotech startup, launches a lab‑grown burger priced at $8 per unit. In the first month it sells 10,000 burgers. Market research shows that burgers represent 2 % of an average consumer’s monthly food budget, there are two close substitutes (traditional beef burgers and existing plant‑based patties), and consumers have not yet formed strong habits. The company’s accounting policy follows accrual basis; revenue is recognized when the burger is delivered to the retailer. The production process uses mammalian cell culture with a doubling time of 24 hours, requiring a specific growth medium. After a price increase to $9, monthly sales fall to 8,000 units. Assume all other factors remain constant. Using this information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(E) The cell culture’s doubling time is 24 hours. If a new medium reduces it to 12 hours, how would this affect the ‘time horizon’ factor influencing PED, and what would be the likely impact on demand elasticity?

A student solves the problem: "A train travels 360 km at a uniform speed. If the speed had been 5 km/h more, it would have taken 1 hour less for the same journey. Find the speed of the train."  
They form the equation \(\frac{360}{x} - \frac{360}{x+5} = 1\), simplify to \(x^2+5x-1800=0\), and get roots \(x=40\) and \(x=-45\). They write the answer as "40 km/h or -45 km/h". Evaluate this solution.

In early 2025, the nation‑state of **Indra** drafts the *Digital Harmony Act* (DHA) requiring social‑media platforms to remove content that “undermines the divine virtues of Mercy, Pity, Peace, and Love” as defined by a state‑appointed cultural council. The act cites Blake’s *The Human Abstract* to argue that these virtues arise only from societal cruelty, thus permitting regulation of speech that allegedly cultivates such cruelty. A tech‑rights NGO challenges the DHA, presenting:
- A content‑analysis sample of 10,000 flagged posts shows 62 % contain political dissent, 24 % contain satire about religious symbols, and 14 % contain genuine calls for violence.
- The cultural council’s guidance notes that “any critique of state‑endorsed virtues is prima facie cruel”.
- Historical data (node The decline of the Harappan Civilisation (c) indicates that during the 1930s Press Ordinance, similar virtue‑based censorship reduced political opposition by 48 % but increased underground pamphleteering by 73 %.
Using the scenario, answer the sub‑parts below.

(B) Identify the metaphor in Blake’s line “And mutual fear brings peace, Till the selfish loves increase” that the DHA’s reliance on “divine virtues” most closely parallels.

In 2024 the Government of India creates the “National Green Energy Planning Commission” (NGEPC) by executive resolution to formulate a five‑year plan for attaining 500 GW of renewable electricity capacity by 2030. The commission is tasked with aligning its strategy with Article 39 of the Directive Principles (ensuring that the ownership and control of material resources are distributed to subserve the common good) and with promoting a mixed‑economy approach where public sector undertakings (e.g., NTPC, SECI) coexist with private solar and wind developers. The NGEPC must decide the share of plan expenditure (budgeted support for central schemes, land acquisition, grid strengthening) versus non‑plan expenditure (routine administrative costs, interest on past loans). Historical analogies are drawn from early Mesopotamian irrigation projects (Mesopotamia (Greek) where temple‑administered canals allocated water rights, and from modern accounting principles (Accounting) that distinguish capital from revenue expenditure. The commission’s first draft proposes an outlay of ₹12 lakh crore, with 60 % earmarked as plan expenditure and the remainder as non‑plan. Critics argue that the body, not being a constitutional organ, lacks binding authority, echoing debates about the original Planning Commission’s advisory status.

(A) Why was the NGEPC constituted through an executive resolution rather than a constitutional amendment, and which constitutional provision guides its developmental goals?

A 2023‑produced documentary on the Chipko movement uses archival footage from 1974 showing villagers hugging trees in the Garhwal Himalayas. The narrator states: “The protest was not merely about saving trees; it was a assertion of forest‑dweller rights under Article 21 of the Constitution, later reinforced by the 1980 Forest Conservation Act.” The film intercuts this with a 2022 satellite image showing deforestation rates in Uttarakhand rising 12% YoY. A critic argues the documentary conflates moral appeal with legal precision, noting that Article 21 guarantees life and personal liberty, not explicit forest rights, which derive from the Forest Rights Act, 2006. The film’s director insists the satellite data visually reinforces the urgency of the 1974 struggle, while a historian counters that the 12% figure includes commercial plantations, not natural forest loss. Identify which statements are literally supported by the text and which require inference, citing specific evidence.

(A) Which sentence in the passage provides literal evidence that the Chipko protest involved villagers hugging trees?

A tech NGO launches an AI‑driven app “LinguaGuard” to revitalize the endangered tribal language “Gondi” in central India. The app uses speech‑recognition to correct pronunciation and offers gamified lessons. Early data: 4 000 downloads, 22 % daily active users, but only 8 % of users are over 40. Critics argue digital tools cannot replace intergenerational transmission. As a student volunteer, you must: (1) draft a 50‑word notice for the college notice‑board promoting a “Gondi Hackathon” to improve the app; (2) write a 100‑word PEEL paragraph arguing that digital supplementation, not replacement, is vital for language survival, citing evidence from *The Last Lesson* (irony of forced language shift) and a UNESCO report on digital language tools; (3) compose a 150‑word personal narrative describing how creating a Gondi‑language meme for the app made you appreciate the language’s humor and resilience. Incorporate historical note: Gondi speakers faced marginalization during British colonial censuses; geographical note: the Gondwana forest’s dense canopy historically isolated communities, aiding linguistic preservation.

(D) Explain how British colonial census categorization (1881‑1931) contributed to the perceived decline of Gondi, and how the Gondwana forest’s geography both hindered colonial administration and aided linguistic continuity.

The Golden Quadrilateral (GQ) highway network (5,846 km) connects Delhi‑Mumbai‑Chennai‑Kolkata. A logistics firm plans to shift 1.2 million tonnes per annum of finished goods from Mumbai to Kolkata via GQ, previously moved by coastal shipping. The shift reduces average transit time from 5 days (ship) to 2 days (truck) and lowers inventory holding cost by ₹1,500 per tonne. The firm expects to save ₹18 crore annually in logistics cost. Goods and Services Tax (GST) is levied at 18 % on the freight service. Under the GST regime, the centre collects CGST and SGST is transferred to the consuming state (West Bengal). The firm’s headquarters is in Maharashtra. Assume the freight charge (excluding GST) is ₹25,000 per tonne.

(C) Identify the constitutional principle that permits the centre to levy and collect CGST while states receive SGST, and relate it to the power‑sharing model illustrated.

An AI‑fintech startup offers instant micro‑credit to self‑help groups in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and Tripura using alternative data (mobile‑usage patterns, satellite‑derived land‑use, and social‑media behaviour). The platform’s risk‑engine runs on a GPU‑cluster in Guwahati, accessed via a 5G backbone (1 Gbps) linking state capitals to a national data‑centre in Bengaluru. Loan portfolio stands at INR 2 500 crore with an average interest rate of 14 % p.a.; expected gross NPA is 3.5 %. The platform contributes to financial inclusion, raising the adult‑banking‑rate from 48 % to 58 % in the region. Regulatory hurdles include: (i) RBI’s guidelines on digital lending requiring a nodal bank partner, (ii) the Draft Data Protection Bill, 2023, imposing purpose limitation on alternative data, and (iii) environmental concerns about increased electronic waste from device upgrades.

(D) Analyze how the prudential and moral reasons for power sharing justify RBI’s requirement of a nodal bank partner for digital lending platforms.

During the early phase of a novel respiratory outbreak (COVID‑23), a national health ministry launches a multi‑channel campaign to increase vaccine uptake. The campaign emphasizes safety, efficacy, trust in authorities, and perceived necessity. A stratified survey of 4,000 adults measures attitudes: 40% positive, 35% negative, 25% neutral toward the vaccine. On a 10‑point extremeness scale (1 = neutral, 10 = extreme), the mean score is 6.2. Factor analysis reveals four distinct sub‑attitudes: safety concern, efficacy belief, trust in authorities, perceived necessity (simplicity/complexity index = 4). The attitude’s centrality is high, shown by a strong correlation with intention to vaccinate (r = 0.55). Salivary IgA, a mucosal immunity marker, is assayed pre‑ and post‑campaign; the positive‑valence group exhibits a 12% increase in IgA levels relative to baseline. A health‑economic model estimates: average cost of a COVID‑23 case (treatment, productivity loss) = $15,000; vaccine cost per dose = $20; the campaign aims to raise coverage by 25 percentage points, averting an estimated 5,000 cases. Vaccination cost for the additional doses = (0.25 × population × $20) = $10 million; expected savings from averted cases = 5,000 × $15,000 = $75 million.

(D) Using the salivary IgA data, infer the biological implication of positive vaccine attitudes on mucosal immunity.

In early 2025, India signs a Precautionary and Liquidity Line (PLL) with the IMF amounting to SDR 5 billion, conditional on maintaining a flexible exchange‑rate regime and limiting foreign exchange market intervention to ≤ 1 % of monthly reserves. Simultaneously, the World Bank approves a ₹8 000 crore loan for climate‑smart agriculture in the Gangetic plain, requiring adoption of water‑saving technologies and provision of extension services to smallholders. Historical analysis (c11_hist_cbse_01_009) shows that the Grand Trunk Road facilitated labour mobility between agrarian hinterlands and urban centres during the Mughal era, a pattern mirrored today by seasonal migration from Bihar and Uttar Pradesh to Punjab and Haryana for wheat harvesting. Using this scenario, answer the sub‑parts.

(B) The World Bank loan mandates adoption of water‑saving technologies (e.g., drip irrigation) for smallholders. Calculate the percentage reduction in water use if traditional flood irrigation consumes 15 000 m³/ha/year and drip irrigation consumes 4 500 m³/ha/year.

A 26‑year‑old female software engineer at an AI‑driven health‑tech startup reports, for the past six weeks, hearing clear voices that command her to insert malicious code into the company’s flagship diagnostic algorithm. She obeys the voices at night, inserting subtle bugs that cause occasional misdiagnoses. Over the same period her speech has become markedly brief and monosyllabic (she answers questions in one‑word replies), her facial expression is flat during team meetings, and she has stopped attending informal coffee breaks, preferring to work alone. She holds a fixed, false belief that her coworkers are secretly plotting to sabotage her career and that the voices are “government agents” trying to silence her. Her manager notes a 40 % drop in code‑commit frequency and missed sprint deadlines. She denies any alcohol, cannabis, or illicit drug use. Her family reports that she was socially withdrawn even in college but never exhibited psychotic symptoms before.

(A) From the vignette, identify two positive symptoms and two negative symptoms exhibited by the engineer.

In 2024 a South‑Korean conglomerate, taking advantage of India’s 2020 semiconductor‑manufacturing PLI (offering 50% fiscal support on capital expenditure) and Telangana’s progressive industrial‑policy framework (single‑window clearance, labour‑law flexibility in designated “Emerging Technology Zones”), sets up a 300 mm wafer fab near Hyderabad. The plant hires 4,000 core engineers on regular contracts and 6,000 auxiliary technicians, maintenance staff and logistics personnel through third‑party contractors, offering only 12‑month renewable contracts, no gratuity, and shift‑based overtime governed by an AI‑driven production scheduler. The site is located on the banks of the Musi River, historically part of the Golconda‑Hyderabad trade corridor that linked Deccan cotton and diamond markets to the Arabian Sea ports (see Trade, Commerce and Long-Distance Exchange in Mesopotamia (c). Rapid land acquisition converts peri‑urban orchards into logistics parks, triggering in‑migration of skilled workers from Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, while local Dalit communities complain of exclusion from both employment and compensation packages. Using concepts of informalisation, trade‑union weakness, service‑sector growth, historic trade‑urban links, centre‑state fiscal federalism, and social exclusion, answer the following.
