Recent satellite data show glacier retreat averaging 0.8 m/year in the Sutlej basin, while tourism footfall has risen from 0.4 million (2015) to 2.3 million (2024). The poem’s first stanza reads: “बर्फ की चोटी पर silenzieuse हवा, पत्थर की आँखों में बसी हुई धूप” (Snow‑capped peak, silent wind; sunlight lodged in the eyes of stone). Students must analyse the poem’s theme and message, then evaluate how its imagery supports or critiques specific HCA provisions, using interdisciplinary reasoning from geography (glacier dynamics, tourism carrying capacity) and political science (Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles). All necessary data (tourist numbers, glacier loss rates, Act clauses) are provided above.

(D) Synthesize the poem’s imagery and metaphor to critique the Act’s lack of provision for glacial retreat monitoring, proposing a specific amendment.

A satellite of mass 500 kg is in a circular orbit at a height of 800 km above Earth's surface. Calculate the gravitational potential at the satellite's location. Given: M_E = 6.0 × 10^24 kg, R_E = 6.4 × 10^6 m, G = 6.67 × 10^-11 N·m²/kg².

A plant‑biotech lab grows two wheat cultivars (drought‑tolerant DT and sensitive DS) under control and drought conditions. Leaf RNA is extracted, libraries prepared, and sequenced on an Illumina platform yielding 30 million paired‑end reads per sample. After quality trimming, reads are aligned to the wheat reference genome (IWGSC v2.1) and featureCounts generates a raw count matrix for 85 000 genes. The lab uses DESeq2 (based on negative‑binomial model) to identify genes differentially expressed between DT and DS under drought. The dispersion estimate for a gene of interest is α = 0.12, the mean normalized count in DT is 150 reads, in DS is 45 reads. The Wald test statistic is calculated, and the Benjamini‑Hochberg procedure controls FDR at 5 %. The team must (i) compute the log₂ fold change, (ii) derive the standard error of the log₂ fold change using the dispersion, (iii) obtain the Wald statistic and its two‑tailed p‑value, (iv) decide whether the gene passes the FDR threshold given a raw p‑value of 0.003 and 12 000 tested genes, and (v) select the appropriate repository for uploading the processed count matrix and the corresponding file format.

(A) Calculate the log₂ fold change (log₂FC) of the gene between DT and DS.

A water fountain jet follows a parabolic path. The jet reaches a maximum height of 4 m at a horizontal distance of 0.5 m from the vertical line through the nozzle (origin). The nozzle is at ground level (0,0). Find the height of the jet at a horizontal distance of 0.75 m from the nozzle. Also, determine the length of the latus rectum of this parabolic trajectory.

Compare the experiences of an Indian indentured labourer in Trinidad (1850s) and an Irish famine migrant in New York (1850s). Identify three similarities and two differences in their migration journey and settlement.

In the semi‑arid district of Jodhpur (Rajasthan), the state government proposes installing agrivoltaic systems (solar panels elevated above crops) on 250,000 ha of existing fallow land to generate 2 GW of solar power while cultivating drought‑tolerant millets underneath. The project expects to increase millet yield by 15 % due to micro‑climate moderation, but requires clearing 50,000 ha of scrubland (classified as “other land” in revenue records) for panel foundations and access roads. The district’s total geographical area is 2.2 million ha, with current land‑use distribution: forests 5 %, fallow 30 %, cropland 45 %, scrubland 10 %, built‑up 10 %. The state’s renewable energy fund has ₹ 12,000 crores allocated, of which 40 % is earmarked for solar. The central government provides a viability gap funding (VGF) of 20 % of project cost under the fiscal federalism scheme (Article 282). The levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for agrivoltaic is ₹ 2.8/kWh, while conventional solar (ground‑mounted) is ₹ 2.2/kWh. Using concepts of land capability classification, inter‑governmental fiscal transfers, and energy economics (LCOE analysis), answer the following.

(B) Calculate the expected annual electricity generation (in GWh) from the 2 GW agrivoltaic plant assuming a capacity factor of 20 %.

A state government runs a midday meal (MDM) programme for 12‑year‑old adolescents in a drought‑prone district of Rajasthan. The prescribed menu provides 450 kcal, 12 g protein, 4 mg iron, 200 mg calcium and 150 µg vitamin A per child per day. ICMR RDA for adolescents (12‑14 yr, moderate activity) is: Energy 1900 kcal, Protein 40 g, Iron 16 mg, Calcium 800 mg, Vitamin A 600 µg.  
Recent monsoon failure reduced local millet yield by 30 %, forcing procurement of rice at higher cost; the program now uses polished rice (lower micronutrient density). Additionally, a prevalent caste‑based food taboo prevents consumption of eggs and dairy among 35 % of children.  
Using the data, assess whether the MDM meets the adjusted RDA after accounting for (i) reduced millet micronutrient content (assume 20 % lower iron and calcium in polished rice vs. millet), (ii) 35 % children unable to consume egg/dairy (which normally contribute 30 % of protein and 50 % of calcium in the menu), and (iii) seasonal energy deficit due to lower crop yield (assume 10 % lower energy density of the ration). Recommend one policy intervention.

(A) Compute the effective energy density of the MDM ration after a 10 % reduction due to lower crop yield.

A US‑based analytics firm plans to establish a knowledge process outsourcing (KPO) centre in Hyderabad, employing 1 200 data scientists to serve clients in Europe and North America. The centre requires 10 Gbps internet, proximity to Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, and access to banking services for cross‑border payments. Employees commute via metro (average 12 km @ 30 km/h) and feeder bus (8 km @ 20 km/h). The firm offers wellness programs and uses AI‑based task allocation, raising concerns about cognitive load and stress. The Telangana government provides a tax holiday equal to 20 % of salary cost under a power‑sharing agreement with the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (74th CAA). Data: average monthly salary = ₹1 20 000; employer PF = 12 % of salary; gratuity accrual = 4.81 % of salary; other benefits = 8 % of salary. The firm invoices clients in USD; average billable hours per employee per month = 160; rate = $30/hour. Exchange rate = ₹82/USD. Annual expenditure on data‑security software = ₹5 crore; GDPR legal consultancy = ₹1 crore/year. The digital divide index for Hyderabad is 0.68 (scale 0‑1); surrounding rural districts have index 0.32.

(D) Using the accommodation principle from Belgian power‑sharing, compute the effective tax holiday percentage if the Hyderabad Municipal Corporation opposes the incentive and reduces it by 30 %. Calculate the resulting monthly savings per employee (in INR).

A research lab measures the Hall voltage across a rectangular silicon slab to determine its doping type and quality. The slab dimensions are: thickness t = 0.5 mm, width w = 2 mm, length L = 10 mm. A current I = 5 mA flows along the length, a magnetic field B = 0.2 T is applied perpendicular to the current, and the measured Hall voltage is V_H = +12 mV (positive sign indicates holes). The resistance measured between the ends of the slab is R = 2000 Ω. Each Hall‑effect measurement consumes $0.05 of consumables, and the lab’s daily budget for such measurements is $5. Using the data, answer the following.

(C) From the measured resistance, compute the resistivity ρ and conductivity σ of the sample.

A tissue culture lab initiates micropropagation of orchid (Dendrobium) using 10 shoot-tip explants. The multiplication medium (MS + 2 mg/L BAP + 0.5 mg/L NAA) yields an average of 6 shoots per explant every 4 weeks. The rooting medium (MS + 1 mg/L NAA) gives 90% rooting success. Acclimatization survival is 80%. Calculate the number of saleable plantlets after 3 multiplication cycles.

A viral Hindi poem titled “धधकती धरती” (Burning Earth) circulates on social media ahead of the 2025 UN Climate Summit. The poem uses the metaphor **अग्नि‑मंडल** to describe rising temperatures, and laments that “प्रज्वलित wishes” turn to “राख‑filled hopes”. A stanza reads: “जल‑वहीनता का **संकट** गहराता है, जबकि नीति‑निर्माता **अविचलित** रह जाते हैं”. Environmental scientists note that the Indo‑Gangetic basin’s average monsoon rainfall has declined from 900 mm/yr (1980‑90) to 720 mm/yr (2010‑20), a 20 % drop. Geographically, the basin’s groundwater recharge zone lies between 26°‑28° N latitude, where overexploitation has lowered the water table by 1.5 m since 2000. Sociologically, a survey shows that 62 % of farmers in the region believe that **सामूहिक** action could reverse the trend, but only 18 % participate in collective initiatives.

(B) Infer the meaning of **संकट** as used in the line about water scarcity.

A professional esports team of five players prepares for a $2 million international finals held across three time zones (UTC‑5, UTC+0, UTC+8). Players undergo 12‑hour daily practice for two weeks, with irregular sleep (average 5 h/night) and high‑intensity cognitive load. Pre‑tournament baseline saliva cortisol averaged 8 µg/dL; after 10 days of practice, cortisol rose to 22 µg/dL. Simultaneously, NK‑cell activity measured via flow cytometry fell from 180 LU to 110 LU. Psychometric assessments showed 3/5 players reported high “threat” appraisal (fear of failure, social media backlash), while 2/5 reported “challenge” (excitement, mastery). The team’s coach implements: (i) a sleep‑hygiene protocol (fixed lights‑out, melatonin 0.5 mg), and (ii) daily 30‑minute trust‑building exercises (shared strategy reviews, cooperative mini‑games). Assume each 1 LU loss in NK activity raises upper‑respiratory infection (URI) risk by 0.4 %, and cortisol‑NK relation follows a power law: NK = NK0 · (cortisol/cortisol0)^‑0.3. Answer the following.

(E) Hypothesize how transmeridian travel (jet lag) might dysregulate cortisol circadian amplitude and thereby modify NK‑cell rhythmicity, integrating chronobiology and psychoneuroimmunology.

Combine rural-urban trends with occupational data. In State X (2011): 60% rural, 40% urban. Rural workforce: 70% cultivators+agri labourers. Urban workforce: 15% household industry, 85% other services. If total workers = 50 million, find absolute numbers in each sector and evaluate whether State X fits the "Lewis turning point" (surplus labour exhausted).

A source emits sound at 500 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m/s. The source moves away from a stationary observer at 20 m/s. The observer then moves away from the source at 15 m/s. Calculate the observed frequency in both cases. (Give answers to 1 decimal place.)

The United Nations Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence is drafting a “Charter of Compassionate AI” to ensure that autonomous systems uphold mercy, pity, peace, and love. The committee references Blake’s “The Divine Image” as a philosophical baseline but worries that, as in “The Human Abstract,” institutionalizing these virtues could produce new forms of cruelty (e.g., algorithmic bias, surveillance‑driven poverty). Delegates from three regions present case studies: (1) a facial‑recognition system in a multicultural city that reduced crime but increased false arrests among minority groups; (2) an AI‑driven welfare‑allocation platform in a post‑conflict state that cut administrative costs but left 12 % of the poorest households without aid; (3) a peace‑keeping drone network that lowered combatant casualties yet caused civilian anxiety due to constant monitoring. The committee must decide whether to embed Blake’s virtues as substantive rights, as aspirational goals, or to reject them outright.

(E) Compare the UN Committee’s dilemma with the historical episode of the British East India Company’s “civilizing mission” in India. Identify which Blake poem each scenario aligns with and why.

Delhi's odd-even vehicle rationing scheme was implemented for 15 days in January 2016. Average PM2.5 during the scheme was 310 µg/m³ vs. 340 µg/m³ in the preceding 15 days. Meteorological data shows average wind speed increased from 1.2 m/s to 2.5 m/s during the scheme period. Determine whether the scheme reduced emissions or whether meteorology explains the improvement.

A company takes a loan of ₹10,00,000 at 10% annual interest for 3 years. The CFO wants to see the impact of payment timing (beginning vs end of month) on total interest. Compute both monthly instalments and the total interest paid in each case.

A bio‑engineering lab wants to sort fluorescently tagged DNA fragments (average length 2 kb, effective charge –30e) flowing through a straight microchannel (width 100 µm, height 20 µm) by exploiting lateral deflection in a non‑uniform electric field. Two parallel strip electrodes run along the channel walls: the left electrode is held at +V₀ = +15 V, the right electrode at –V₀ = –15 V. The medium is aqueous buffer (relative permittivity ε_r ≈ 80). The goal is to achieve a lateral displacement of at least 30 µm over a channel length L = 2 cm for the target DNA, while ensuring that field lines never cross (to avoid undefined field direction) and that the field line density correctly reflects the local field magnitude for accurate force estimation.  
Using the given geometry, assume the potential varies linearly between the electrodes (V(x) = V₀·(2x/w – 1), where x measures distance from the left wall, 0 ≤ x ≤ w). The electric field is **E** = –∇V.  
Students must: (i) find the field direction at any point via the tangent to field lines, (ii) justify why field lines cannot intersect, (iii) relate field line spacing to |**E**|, (iv) determine where field lines originate/terminate, and (v) sketch the qualitative field line pattern for the electrode pair, noting any regions of high field intensity that could cause particle trapping.

(A) At a point P located 40 µm from the left wall (x = 40 µm) inside the channel, what is the direction of the net electric field vector? Express your answer as the angle θ measured from the +x‑axis (pointing from left to right).

An NGO files a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in the Supreme Court challenging the Ken‑Betwa River Linking Project. Paragraph 3 of the petition reads: “The parched bed of the Betwa lies like a wounded serpent, waiting for the monsoon’s kiss that never comes.” Paragraph 7 states: “Justice is a dam that holds back the flood of oppression; when its cracks widen, the waters of rights spill over the vulnerable.” The project envisages transferring 1,200 MCM of water annually from the Ken to the Betwa basin, irrigating 6.35 lakh ha and affecting 1.2 lakh tribal households in Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh. The petition invokes Article 21 (Right to Life) and Article 48A (Directive Principle on environment). Using the above excerpt, answer the following.

(D) Calculate the per‑household water allocation (in litres per day) if the project’s annual transfer is distributed equally among the affected tribal households.
Compare the interest earned on ₹10,000 at 8% for 3 years versus ₹12,000 at 6% for 2 years. Which gives more interest, and by how much?

Using TRAI data (Dec 2023), India's total wireless broadband subscriptions = 850 million. Population = 1.43 billion. But unique subscribers (after de-duplicating multi-SIM users) estimated at 650 million. Calculate: (a) raw subscription penetration, (b) unique subscriber penetration. If the "meaningful connectivity" threshold (A4AI) requires 4G smartphone + daily 1GB data + digital skills, and only 40% of unique subscribers meet this, what is the meaningful connectivity penetration? Discuss why raw subscription data overstates access.

A municipal government is launching a “Smart City” initiative to deploy IoT sensors for traffic monitoring, air‑quality sensing, and waste‑management across five administrative wards (Zones A–E). The city has been allocated the IPv4 block **172.16.0.0/16** for all sensor devices. Expected sensor counts are: Zone A – 1 200, Zone B – 950, Zone C – 2 100, Zone D – 800, Zone E – 1 500. Policy requires that the **first subnet** of the allocated block be reserved exclusively for government‑run services (e.g., emergency communications). The remaining address space must be divided among the wards proportionally to sensor load, while allowing at least 10 % future growth in each zone. Students must determine appropriate subnet masks, calculate usable host ranges, and verify compliance with the reservation policy, integrating concepts of IP addressing (primary), geographic ward distribution (Geography), and public‑policy allocation rules (Political Science).

(E) After reserving the first subnet (172.16.0.0/20) for government services, allocate the remaining address space proportionally to the five wards based on sensor counts (including 10 % growth). Compute the number of usable host addresses each ward receives.

In 2025, the Ministry of Education launches an AI‑driven subtitle project that automatically translates live parliamentary debates from Hindi into all 22 scheduled languages, aiming to improve accessibility. Critics argue that the AI, trained predominantly on corpora from North‑Indian Hindi sources, systematically mis‑translates idioms from Dravidian languages, flattening regional nuance. A parliamentary committee hearing is held in a retrofitted television studio resembling the set of "Broken Images": a central chair, a semi‑circular table, a plasma screen displaying the Eliot line in real time as subtitles scroll beneath it, and several muted TV sets showing regional news channels. Witnesses include: (1) a historian citing the 1935 Government of India Act’s language provisions and the post‑independent Three‑Language Formula; (2) a political scientist referencing Article 350A (mother‑tongue instruction at primary stage) and recent Supreme Court rulings on AI bias; (3) a psychologist presenting fMRI data showing that bilingual individuals exhibit heightened activity in the anterior cingulate cortex when encountering mistranslated cultural metaphors, indicating emotional distress; (4) a sociologist noting that English‑language media enjoys 78% of national advertising revenue, while regional language channels combined receive only 12%, affecting perceptions of linguistic worth. The committee chair, a bilingual woman who anchors a national news channel, opens with a monologue lifted from Manjula’s soliloquy, reflecting on how her English‑anchored persona feels like a “heap of broken images” when she witnesses her mother‑tongue being reduced to algorithmic errors. Using this scenario, answer the sub‑parts below.

(A) Identify how the chairperson’s monologue encapsulates the primary theme of "Broken Images" and explain why the AI subtitle error intensifies this theme in the hearing context.

In a drought-stressed wheat plant, metabolomic analysis shows: (1) 3-fold increase in proline (amino acid, MW 115 Da) in leaf cytosol, (2) 50% decrease in Rubisco protein (MW 550,000 Da) in chloroplasts, (3) appearance of a novel flavonoid glycoside (MW 610 Da) in vacuoles, and (4) no change in genomic DNA content. Classify each change as involving a micromolecule or macromolecule, primary or secondary metabolite, and explain the biological significance of this pattern for drought adaptation.

A 45‑minute Hindi‑language documentary titled “धरती की पुकार” (Earth’s Cry), released on Netflix India in July 2024, examines the rapid glacial retreat in the Uttarakhand Himalayas. The narrator, a renowned environmental journalist, employs irony: “We celebrate the ‘new beaches’ formed by melting glaciers, unaware that they are the graves of freshwater reserves.” Symbolism appears through recurring visual motifs: a lone prayer flag fluttering above a cracked riverbed (symbol = fragile spirituality), and a child’s broken toy boat stranded on dry land (symbol = lost future). The documentary intersperses satellite imagery showing a 22% reduction in glacier mass since 2000 (data from ISRO’s RESOURCESAT‑2) with interviews of local farmers describing altered monsoon patterns (increase in extreme rainfall events by 35% over the past decade). Psychologically, the narration uses fear‑arousal coupled with efficacy messages (“Small actions—like planting native saplings—can reboot the hydrological cycle”). Geographically, it links the retreat to altered albedo effect, contributing to regional warming of 0.8 °C.

(C) Explain how the irony and symbolism together strengthen the documentary’s primary theme (anthropogenic climate change threatens Himalayan water security) and support a secondary theme (local communities possess traditional knowledge vital for adaptation).

A student collective launches a hashtag #कविता_की_आवाज़ on Twitter/X to discuss the poems “olar vk;k” and “rksM+ks” in the context of climate activism. The tweets combine poetic lines, infographics on India’s carbon‑emission trends (2020‑2023: rise from 2.4 to 2.7 Gt CO₂), references to the **Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines) Rules 2021** ( – treat as cross‑subject node for digital law), and a map showing the spread of desertification in the Thar region (Subsistence agriculture). The moderator must assess whether the poetic content qualifies as “lawful expression” under the IT Rules, how the theme of perseverance informs the campaign’s messaging, and whether the geographic focus aligns with the poem’s imagery.

(B) Identify two metaphors in “rksM+ks” that depict desertification and relate them to the Thar region’s observed increase in sandy‑soil percentage from 68% (2010) to 74% (2023).

A pharmaceutical company wants to bioprospect in a 10,000 ha tropical evergreen forest in the Andaman Islands for anti-cancer compounds. The forest currently provides: carbon sequestration (8 tC/ha/yr), watershed protection for 200,000 islanders, and habitat for 15 endemic bird species. The company offers ₹50 crore one-time lease. Using TEV framework, advise the forest department on whether to accept. Assume carbon price ₹2,000/tCO₂e, watershed replacement cost ₹500/capita/yr, option value of endemics ₹10 lakh/species/yr.

A coastal district in Kerala faces a choice: 
Option 1: Allow a chemical fertilizer plant creating 2,000 jobs with average annual wage ₹3 lakh, but releasing effluents that will reduce fish catch by 30% (current value ₹200 crore/year) and increase health costs by ₹50 crore/year for 30 years.
Option 2: Invest in sustainable aquaculture and eco-tourism creating 1,200 jobs at ₹2.5 lakh/year, maintaining fish catch and adding ₹30 crore/year in tourism revenue indefinitely.
Assume a social discount rate of 5%. Evaluate which option satisfies sustainable development criteria using a simplified cost-benefit framework over 30 years. (Hint: Calculate Present Value of net benefits for each option.)

In early 2024 a novel zoonotic virus (ZV‑24) emerges in a forested district inhabited by 120 tribal villages. Average household size is 5 persons. Mobile phone penetration is 68 % (one phone per household on average). Functional literacy (ability to read a simple health alert) is 42 %. The district health office sends daily SMS alerts in the official language (Hindi) containing technical terms like “asymptomatic transmission”, “R₀ = 2.3”, and “quarantine”. Field reports show that after three days, 55 % of households have heard rumors that the virus is a government conspiracy, 30 % believe it spreads through eating pork (a local taboo), and only 15 % follow the advised hand‑washing protocol. Focus groups reveal that elders distrust written messages, youth feel anxious and ignore long texts, and the local radio station (coverage 80 % of villages) broadcast the alert in Hindi but with poor audio quality due to terrain‑induced signal loss. Using the data, answer the following.

(C) Compute the number of households that actually read and understood the original SMS alert (assuming only literate households can understand).

CloneThera receives an initial seed investment of ₹ 2 crore from an angel investor in exchange for 20 % equity. The company incurs fixed monthly operating expenses of ₹ 5 lakhs and variable costs of ₹ 0.5 lakh per unit of transgenic goat milk produced. In the first year, they produce and sell 10 units (each unit = 1000 L of milk) at a selling price of ₹ 1 lakh per unit. The company follows Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) and uses straight‑line depreciation for lab equipment costing ₹ 50 lakhs over 5 years with zero salvage value. Using the data above, answer the following sub‑parts.

(A) Calculate the break‑even point in number of units (milk units) that CloneThera must sell to cover its fixed and variable costs, assuming the selling price per unit remains ₹ 1 lakh.

In the arid district of Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, a cluster of 12 villages relies on monsoon‑fed agriculture. Over the past decade, unregulated tube‑well irrigation for cash crops (cotton, guar) has lowered the water table by 1.8 m, increasing salinity. The village panchayat proposes reviving the traditional khadin system: an earthen embankment built across a 5 ha gently sloping field to capture runoff. Historical records show average monsoon rainfall of 200 mm with a spatial coefficient of variation of 0.25. Soil infiltration tests give a runoff coefficient of 0.30 for the loamy‑sandy catchment. The khadin is designed to retain water for 90 days, after which excess flows downstream. The community estimates that irrigating one hectare of wheat requires 400 mm of water per season. Assume the khadin’s storage efficiency (ratio of stored volume to gross runoff) is 70 % due to seepage and evaporation losses. Using this information, answer the following.

(E) Compare evaporation loss from a khadin (open surface) with that from an underground tanka of equal volume, assuming a pan‑evaporation rate of 7 mm/day over 90 days. Which system conserves more water and by how much?

In early 2025, the Gond and Koya tribal communities of Telangana launched a sustained protest against the Upper Godavari Dam project, which would submerge 12,000 ha of forest and displace 35,000 tribals. Protesters claim the dam violates their constitutional right to protect traditional forest habitats (Article 21) and destroys sacred groves central to their identity. They cite the Narmada Bachao Andolan’s use of satyagraha and international media as a mobilisation template. The movement has raised ₹8 crore through crowdfunding, secured legal aid from the Environmental Law Alliance, and employed GPS‑mapped forest‑boundary documentation to strengthen their claim in the National Green Tribunal. Historically, ancient Mesopotamian societies developed irrigation canals that prioritised state‑controlled water allocation, often overriding local customs—a parallel to modern dam‑centric water federalism. Politically, water‑resource projects fall under the Union List (Entry 56) but require State consent under Article 262, creating a power‑sharing tension akin to Belgium’s linguistic accommodation. Analyze the emergence, resource mobilisation, and new‑movement traits of this anti‑dam struggle using the three theories of social movements.

(A) Which element of Relative Deprivation Theory best captures the tribals’ grievance regarding land submergence?

The Ministry of Health launches a real‑time COVID‑19 vaccination dashboard to display district‑wise dose administration, vaccine stock levels, and adverse‑event reports. The portal must be accessible on low‑bandwidth rural smartphones (average 3G speed) and high‑resolution government intranet workstations. Legal compliance requires adherence to Section 43A of the IT Act (reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data) and minimisation of unnecessary data transfer to reduce digital footprints. Societal research shows that users distrust sites that load slowly or expose excessive metadata, influencing adoption rates. The design team has three page types: (1) Home – static summary with minimal interactivity; (2) Stats – interactive charts updating every 5 minutes via AJAX; (3) Vaccine Locator – a map‑based search with custom filters and a prominent “Book Slot” button that must stand out visually. The team must decide where to apply inline, internal, or external CSS for each page type, considering: (a) specificity needs for the Book Slot button; (b) reusability of chart styles across Stats and Locator; (c) caching benefits for repeat visitors; (d) media‑query breakpoints for 320px, 768px, and 1440px widths; (e) legal constraint that excessive inline styling increases HTML size, potentially slowing load and raising data‑exposure risk.

(A) For the Vaccine Locator page, the “Book Slot” button must override all other styles (including any future theme changes) without affecting other pages. Which CSS inclusion method guarantees the highest specificity while keeping the change isolated to this page?

A satellite in a circular low‑Earth orbit (altitude 400 km) uses a star‑tracker to measure its yaw angle θ relative to a reference star. The tracker outputs the angle as θ = sin⁻¹( (v·r)/|v||r| ), where v is the satellite’s instantaneous velocity vector and r is the unit vector toward the star. For a given orbit, the magnitude of v is constant (v₀ = 7.7 km s⁻¹) and the star lies in the orbital plane, so the dot product reduces to v₀ cos ωt, where ω = 2π/T is the orbital angular speed (T = 92 min). Hence θ(t) = sin⁻¹( cos ωt ). The satellite’s attitude‑control system requires dθ/dt to compute the required torque. Simultaneously, the hydrazine thruster’s specific impulse I_sp varies with the yaw angle as I_sp(θ) = I₀ [1 + α sin²θ] (I₀ = 220 s, α = 0.15). The instantaneous thrust power P(t) = T·v₀, where thrust T = ṁ g₀ I_sp(θ) and ṁ is the mass‑flow rate (constant). Using the derivative of sin⁻¹, find dθ/dt and then determine the time‑averaged thrust power over one orbit. (Physics: orbital kinematics; Chemistry: thruster performance dependence on angle.)

(A) Compute dθ/dt for θ(t) = sin⁻¹(cos ωt) and simplify the expression.

After a vasectomy, the severed vas deferens ends may heal and reconnect (recanalization), restoring fertility. Histology shows fibroblast‑mediated scar formation whose tensile strength σₛ(t) increases with time t (days) according to σₛ(t) = σ₀[1 – e^(‑αt)], where σ₀ = 1.5 MPa (ultimate tensile strength of mature scar) and α = 0.03 day⁻¹. Luminal pressure generated by seminal fluid flow during ejaculation can be approximated by Poiseuille’s law in a cylindrical tube of radius r = 0.2 mm and length L = 20 mm, with viscosity η = 1.2 × 10⁻³ Pa·s and average flow rate Q = 0.5 mL min⁻¹. Recanalization is assumed to occur when the instantaneous transmural pressure P exceeds the instantaneous scar strength σₛ(t). The hazard (instantaneous risk) of recanalization per day is modeled as h(t) = λ·[P – σₛ(t)]₊, where λ = 0.02 day⁻¹ MPa⁻¹ and [x]₊ = max(x,0).  
**Task:** Compute the pressure generated during ejaculation, determine the time window when recanalization is mechanically possible, and evaluate the cumulative probability of at least one recanalization event within the first 180 days post‑vasectomy.

(E) Discuss how increasing the vas deferens radius r (e.g., due to postoperative edema) would affect the recanalization probability, referencing the dependencies derived above.

NetLink Ltd. enjoys a monopoly in rural 4G services. Inverse demand: P = 200 – 0.5Q (P in ₹ per GB, Q in million GB). Marginal cost of transmitting data is constant at ₹30/GB. The firm paid a lump‑sum licence fee of ₹12,000 (million) for the spectrum, to be amortised over 10 years. The licence fee is recognised as an intangible asset under AS‑26. Using the data, answer the following.

In 2028, the Republic of Novara adopts a nationwide AI‑driven “Unified Curriculum Platform” (UCP) that delivers lessons via tablets in all public schools. On the morning of the lesson, the school grounds are mist‑filled; the distant hum of drones delivering UCP tablets is audible, while a lone rooster crows near the old oak tree. Mr. Lorne draws the Riven alphabet on the chalkboard, his hand trembling slightly, and explains each character’s origin in ancient river‑trade symbols. He tells the students, “Riven is the silent syllabus that runs beneath the official code. Lose it, and we lose the subroutine that makes us human.”  

As the lesson ends, he writes the phrase “⟨RIVEN⟩ LIVES” in bright yellow chalk. Suddenly, a drone hovers outside the window, its camera lens focusing on the chalkboard. The drone’s AI, programmed to detect “non‑Novaran symbols”, triggers an alert: “Unrecognized glyphs detected. The students watch as the yellow phrase fades, yet the ghost‑outline remains visible under the morning light, resembling a negative photograph.  

The scenario weaves together the theme of linguistic resistance, imagery of mist, drone, and ghost‑outline, symbolism of the chalkboard as a resistant substrate and the drone as an enforcing algorithm, and irony that the very technology meant to homogenize language highlights the persistence of the suppressed script through its failed erasure attempt.

(B) Using the income‑change data (black‑soil +12 %, red‑soil +3 %), compute the inter‑regional inequality ratio and name the related concept from c12_soc_cbse_11_004.

A sudden glacial lake outburst flood (GLOF) threatens a remote valley in Uttarakhand. Rescue teams must establish communication between the base camp (located 30 km from the lake), three forward medical posts (each 8‑10 km apart along the river), and a national disaster‑response hub in Dehradun. The terrain blocks line‑of‑sight radio, so two options are considered:  
1. **Circuit‑switched satellite phone links** – each terminal reserves a 64 kbps channel for the entire session.  
2. **Packet‑switched ad‑hoc mesh** using lightweight drones equipped with Wi‑Fi routers (802.11n) that forward data using UDP‑based lightweight transport.  

Rescue coordinators need to decide which technology to use for (i) real‑time voice coordination, (ii) transfer of high‑resolution thermal‑imagery packets (average 2 MB per frame), and (iii) periodic status updates (100 bytes every 5 s). Historical data from the 2013 Kedarnath GLOF shows that voice latency must stay < 400 ms for effective command, while imagery can tolerate up to 2 s delay. The Disaster Management Act, 2005 mandates redundancy and interoperability with national emergency frequencies (VHF/UHF).

(C) For transferring a 2 MB thermal‑imagery frame via the packet‑switched mesh, compute the transmission time (in seconds) if each drone‑to‑drone link operates at 15 Mbps and the frame is split into 1 KB packets with 20 bytes UDP header and 8 bytes payload checksum. Ignore propagation and processing delays.

The Census of India 2011 reports India's population as 1,210 million. If the average annual growth rate during 2001-2011 was 1.63%, estimate the population in 2001 using the compound growth formula. Verify against Table 1.

A public sector utility plans a 2 000 MW supercritical thermal power plant to meet rising peak demand in the eastern grid. Two sites are under consideration:  
- **Site A** (Jharkhand, near Raniganj coalfield): Gondwana bituminous coal, average GCV 5 800 kcal/kg, ash 22 %, moisture 8 %, located 150 km by rail from the plant site; water availability from Damodar River (1.2 MCM/day).  
- **Site B** (Chhattisgarh, near Korba coalfield): Gondwana bituminous coal, average GCV 5 200 kcal/kg, ash 30 %, moisture 10 %, located 30 km by conveyor from the plant site; water availability from Hasdeo River (0.8 MCM/day).  
Environmental clearance for Site A requires relocation of 12 ha of protected forest and involves a pending NGT case on cumulative impacts; Site B lies within a notified industrial corridor with pre‑approved clearance but faces tribal protests over land acquisition. The utility must select the site that minimizes levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) while satisfying: (i) specific coal consumption ≤0.6 kg/kWh, (ii) annual SO₂ emissions ≤12 kt (based on 0.5 % S in coal), (iii) water intake ≤1.0 MCM/day, and (iv) social‑acceptance score ≥7/10 (tribal protest reduces score by 2 points per 1 % of affected households).  
Using the data, determine which site is preferable and justify the choice with quantitative and qualitative analysis.

(B) Estimate annual SO₂ emissions (kt/yr) for each site assuming 90 % plant load factor, 0.5 % sulphur in coal, and complete conversion of S to SO₂. Which site satisfies the ≤12 kt/yr limit?

In August 2024, a joint parliamentary committee examined the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Bill, 2023. The committee’s proceedings (total 12 hours) featured speeches by MPs, civil society experts, and industry lobbyists. Sen’s opening lines in *The Argumentative Indian* note India’s tradition of “prolixity” and cite Krishna Menon’s nine‑hour UN speech (1960) as a benchmark. The committee’s transcript shows:  
- 4 MPs invoked the Mahabharata’s “sabha” (assembly) debates as precedent for thorough discussion.  
- 3 civil society speakers used the metaphor of a “banyan tree” to describe how data rights should shelter all citizens, especially marginalised groups.  
- The government’s spokesperson claimed the bill balances privacy with innovation, citing a 2022 NITI Aayog estimate that 68 % of start‑ups fear compliance costs.  
- Opposition members countered with data from a 2023 CSDS survey showing 54 % of rural women fear misuse of biometric IDs.  
Using Sen’s method of sequencing claim → evidence → counterexample → qualification → synthesis, answer the following.

(C) Using the historical node, explain how the MPs’ reference to the Mahabharata’s “sabha” debates serves as *evidence* for Sen’s claim about India’s ancient argumentative tradition.

The Government of India plans to extend the Dedicated Freight Corridor (DFC) from Delhi to Mumbai via a new alignment passing through Vadodara (GJ), Ahmedabad (GJ), and Surat (GJ) before reaching the JNPT port. The extension is expected to cut average rail transit time for automobile components from the Delhi‑NCR supplier belt to Gujarat’s ports by 40 %. Current rail transit time is 48 hours; the proposed DFC will reduce it to 28.8 hours.  

Automobile firms in the Gurugram‑Manesar (Haryana) cluster rely on just‑in‑time (JIT) delivery of steel stampings and electronic control units (ECUs). Their current inventory holding cost is ₹150 per unit per day. The proposed DFC would lower inventory holding cost proportionally to transit‑time reduction.  

Simultaneously, a rival cluster in Chennai (Tamil Nadu) is considering a shift to inland waterways via the newly operational Buckingham Canal link to the Ennore port, promising a 25 % reduction in transit time but requiring an initial infrastructure investment of ₹1,200 crore shared equally by the state and private players.  

Assume a mid‑sized automobile manufacturer produces 200,000 vehicles per year, each requiring 0.8 tonnes of steel stampings and 0.15 tonnes of ECUs. The weight‑based freight rate is ₹2,500 per tonne per 1,000 km via rail. The average rail distance from Gurugram to JNPT is 1,400 km; via the Buckingham Canal route the effective distance (including last‑mile road) is 1,600 km.  

Using this information, answer the following sub‑parts.

(C) For the Chennai cluster, calculate the net annual financial benefit (or loss) from adopting the Buckingham Canal waterway, considering only the transit‑time reduction’s impact on inventory holding cost (same ₹150/unit‑day) and annualised infrastructure cost (assume 10‑year straight‑line depreciation, no interest).

Read the case: "In 1944, 29 reindeer were introduced to St. Matthew Island (Alaska, 32 km²). No predators. Lichen (winter food) abundant. Population: 1957 = 1,350; 1963 = 6,000; 1966 = 42 (crash)." (a) Calculate average r for 1944-1957 and 1957-1963. (b) Why did r decrease? (c) The crash to 42 in 3 years — what ecological concept explains this OVERSHOOT below K? (d) If lichen regenerates at 5%/year and each reindeer needs 50 kg lichen/year, estimate K. (e) Why is logistic model insufficient here?

Solaris Ltd., an Indian solar‑panel manufacturer, decides to raise USD 200 million via Global Depository Receipts (GDRs) listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange. The GDRs represent underlying equity shares of face value ₹10 each, with a conversion ratio of 1 GDR = 10 underlying shares. SEBI, acting under its developmental function, approves the issue subject to compliance with the Issue of Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds and Ordinary Shares (FCCB) Scheme, 1993, and mandates that the proceeds be kept in an overseas escrow account until utilized for approved capital expenditure.  

The issue price is set at USD 12 per GDR. The prevailing spot exchange rate is ₹82.50/USD. Solaris’s pre‑issue balance sheet shows: Equity Share Capital ₹150 crore; Reserves & Surplus ₹800 crore; Foreign Currency Loan (USD 50 million) outstanding at the same spot rate.  

Using the data, answer the following sub‑parts.

(D) Assuming Solaris uses the entire GDR proceeds to import solar‑panel manufacturing equipment, calculate the immediate impact on India’s Balance of Payments (BoP) current account and capital account.

A potentiometer wire AB of length 1.00 m has resistance 8.00 Ω. It is connected in series with a driver cell of emf 4.00 V (internal resistance 1.00 Ω) and a rheostat. A test cell of emf 1.50 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected with its positive terminal to A through a galvanometer and jockey. The rheostat is adjusted to give a balance point at ℓ = 60.0 cm. (a) Find the rheostat resistance. (b) If the test cell is replaced by a second cell of emf 2.00 V and internal resistance 1.00 Ω, will a balance point be obtainable? If yes, find the new balance length. (c) What is the maximum emf that can be measured with this potentiometer at this rheostat setting?

A mobile‑based mindfulness app collected anonymized usage logs from 12,000 users over six months. The dataset includes: UserID (int), Age (int), Gender (string), Occupation (string), DailySessions (int), AvgSessionMinutes (float), StressPreScore (0‑21, from PSS‑10), StressPostScore (0‑21), AppRating (1‑5), and Country (string). Roughly 12% of StressPreScore and 8% of StressPostScore entries are missing; Occupation has 5% missing. The analyst must (i) import the CSV, (ii) inspect data shape and column types, (iii) create a new column ‘StressReduction’ = StressPreScore – StressPostScore, (iv) handle missing values by filling numeric columns with median and Occupation with mode, (v) group users by Age brackets (≤18, 19‑35, 36‑50, >50) and Occupation categories, then compute mean StressReduction per group, (vi) produce descriptive statistics (mean, median, mode, std, describe) for StressReduction overall and per age bracket, and (vii) relate findings to Psychological theories of stress coping (Lazarus & Folkman’s transactional model) and Sociological concepts of digital society (e.g., digital divide, technostress). The final report should highlight which age group benefits most and discuss whether occupational stress levels moderate app effectiveness.

(C) Fill missing numeric columns (Age, DailySessions, AvgSessionMinutes, StressPreScore, StressPostScore, AppRating) with their medians and Occupation with its mode.

Zenith Logistics operates a nationwide fleet of 2,500 trucks. After a recent scandal, the firm shifted from a highly centralised dispatch model to a regional decentralised model. Five regional hubs (North, South, East, West, Central) each manage their own fleet, maintenance, and billing. Formal authority: Regional Manager → Fleet Supervisor → Driver Team Leads. Informally, drivers have formed WhatsApp groups that share real‑time traffic alerts, fuel‑price tips, and maintenance shortcuts across regions. Data: each hub oversees an average of 480 trucks; the average number of direct reports to a Regional Manager is 8 (fleet supervisors). Informal tie density (average cross‑hub WhatsApp messages per driver per day) is 12. The CFO provides: total operating cost ₹5,000 million, variable cost per truck‑km ₹6, fixed cost allocation to hubs based on number of informal ties (weight = 0.1 ₹ million per tie).  
Using this, evaluate: (a) correct computation of fixed cost allocation per hub, (b) impact of informal ties on effective span of control, (c) whether the decentralised structure improves cost responsibility, and (d) the trade‑off between formal span and informal communication efficiency.

(D) Assess whether the informal WhatsApp groups improve or undermine cost responsibility in the decentralised hubs. Use the following: (i) Formal responsibility centre: each hub is a profit centre; (ii) After six months, hub‑level profit variance (actual – budget) is: North +₹80 m, South –₹30 m, East +₹15 m, West –₹10 m, Central +₹5 m; (iii) Correlation between informal tie density (messages per driver per day) and profit variance is –0.48.

A radio interferometer surveys the 21 cm line (hyperfine transition of hydrogen ground state) from neutral hydrogen clouds at various redshifts to study reionization. The rest frequency of the 21 cm line is ν₀ = 1420.405751 MHz. Due to cosmic expansion, the observed frequency is ν_obs = ν₀/(1+z). The survey detects three emission peaks at frequencies 355 MHz, 473 MHz, and 710 MHz.  
Assuming the line arises solely from the hyperfine splitting (energy difference ΔE = hν₀), answer the following. Use h = 6.626×10⁻³⁴ J·s, c = 3.00×10⁸ m/s, and 1 eV = 1.602×10⁻¹⁹ J.

(A) Calculate the redshift z corresponding to each observed frequency (355 MHz, 473 MHz, 710 MHz).

EnzymeTech Ltd. produces a generic industrial enzyme sold in a perfectly competitive market at a fixed price of ₹150 per litre. Its total cost function is TC = 500 + 20Q + 0.5Q² (₹), where Q is weekly output in litres. The enzyme is produced using a microbial culture whose yield follows a simple biological principle: each litre of enzyme requires 0.8 units of viable biomass. At the end of the accounting year, the firm must record its profit in the books (Going Concern Concept) and charge depreciation on the fixed‑cost component (straight‑line 10% of the ₹500 fixed cost per year) as per the Cost Concept. The market price is expected to remain unchanged for the next quarter.  
Using the data above, answer the following sub‑parts.

(C) Determine the shutdown price (minimum AVC) and state whether EnzymeTech will continue production at the market price of ₹150.

PayZen’s digital wallet suffered a system outage lasting 4 hours during peak shopping hours. As a result, 8,000 attempted transactions failed, displaying “Service unavailable – try later”. Customers were unable to pay for goods and services, leading to abandoned carts and reported frustration. PayZen’s terms state that the wallet provider is liable for compensation if a transaction fails due to its technical fault, subject to a maximum of ₹250 per failed transaction.  
Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced a stimulus package that is expected to increase the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) in the economy from 0.6 to 0.75. Analysts estimate that the additional consumption generated by the stimulus will raise aggregate demand by ₹12,000 crore.  
Using the information above, answer the following sub‑parts.

(B) Calculate the total compensation PayZen is liable to pay for the 8,000 failed transactions, assuming the maximum permissible amount per transaction applies.

2024 में संसद ने डिजिटल व्यक्तिगत डेटा संरक्षण विधेयक पारित किया, जो व्यक्तिगत डेटा के संग्रह, प्रसंस्करण और सीमा‑партनर हस्तांतरण को नियंत्रित करता है। विधेयक में निर्धारित है कि किसी भी संस्थान को उपयोगकर्ता की स्पष्ट सहमति लेनी होगी, और डेटा स्थानीयकरण के लिए राज्यों को दो विकल्प दिए गए हैं: (a) डेटा केंद्रों का निर्माण within state borders, या (b) केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अधिकृत बहु‑राज्यीय डेटा पार्क का उपयोग। विधेयक के अनुसार, उल्लंघन पर जुर्माना कुल वार्षिक टर्नओवर का 4 % या ₹200 करोड़, जो भी अधिक हो, लगाया जा सकता है। ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ में, 2017 के न्यायाधीश पुट्टास्वामी मामले में最高 न्यायालय ने गोपनीयता को मौलिक अधिकार घोषित किया था, जो ब्रिटिश‑इंडिया era के “सर्विलांस अधिनियम, 1918” के विपरीत है। भू‑राजनीतिक रूप से, विधेयक ने चीन‑आधारित क्लाउड सेवाओं पर प्रतिबंध लगाया है, जिससे दक्षिण‑पूर्व एशिया में डेटा प्रवाह pathways पर प्रभाव पड़ता है। आर्थिक प्रभाव विश्लेषण बताता है कि स्थानीय डेटा केंद्रों से अगले पाँच वर्ष में ₹1.2 लाख करोड़ का निवेश आएगा और लगभग 3 लाख रोजगार सृजित होंगे। लेखक ने विधेयक को “सूचना युग का कवच” कहा है, जबकि कुछ आलोचकों का कहना है कि यह “अधिकारों का अवरोधक” बन सकता है।

(B) Passage में उल्लिखित दो डेटा स्थानीयकरण विकल्पों में से कौन सा राज्यों को अधिक स्वायत्तता प्रदान करता है?

A severe cyclone hits the eastern coast of India, displacing 12 000 families from three low‑lying villages (A, B, C). The state disaster‑management authority plans a phased relocation to inland resettlement sites over 18 months. Each family is entitled to a housing grant of ₹2 50 000, a livelihood‑support package of ₹80 000, and transportation assistance of ₹15 000. The authority must: (i) set relocation objectives (Planning), (ii) organise land acquisition, shelter construction and psychosocial support teams (Organising), (iii) implement the move in three waves (6 months each) while monitoring health, school attendance and grievance redressal (Implementing), (iv) control delays, cost overruns and social tension (Controlling), and (v) evaluate long‑term recovery via indices of income restoration, housing satisfaction and community cohesion (Evaluating). Relevant data: average construction cost per house = ₹3 00 000; land acquisition cost per family = ₹50 000; transportation cost per family actually incurred = ₹12 000; psychosocial support cost per family = ₹4 000; expected annual income loss due to displacement = ₹60 000 per family (mitigated by livelihood package).

(A) In the planning stage, formulate a SMART objective for reducing average commuting time for relocated families and calculate the required average reduction in travel distance if the current average commute is 18 km/day at an average speed of 30 km/h, and the target is to cut commuting time by 40 %.

A district planner observes that 40% of her district's population lives in settlements classified as "rural" by Census 2011, but these settlements have paved roads, piped water, high schools, and >60% households with two-wheelers. She proposes reclassifying them as urban to access JNNURM funds. As a geographer, evaluate her proposal using Census classification principles.

A smart-city initiative, "Project Suvidha," deploys AI-powered facial recognition in public spaces for crime prevention. A survey reveals: 55% of metro residents support it citing safety, while 68% of marginalized communities (Dalit, Adivasi) oppose it due to fears of caste-based profiling. Key dynamics: Familial mediation - 75% of elderly opposition stems from children showing them viral videos of false arrests (e.g., misidentified street vendors). Reference groups: Dalit youth activists organize against Suvidha, framing it as "digital Manusmriti" (algorithmic caste enforcement), gaining traction via Instagram reels. Personal experience: 22% who faced denied entry to malls due to system errors report heightened anxiety and avoidance behaviors. Media exposure: Regional news channels in Bihar/UP emphasize "state overreach" (50% coverage), while national tech blogs highlight "efficiency gains" (60% coverage). Historical context: Colonial criminal tribes act (1871) used hereditary profiling for surveillance; post-Independence, police databases disproportionately tagged Dalit communities as "habitual offenders." Political discourse: Opposition cites Supreme Court's Puttaswamy privacy verdict and UN Special Rapporteur on contemporary forms of racism warning about AI bias. Students must dissect attitude formation through the lens of familial socialization in digital eras, reference group dynamics in social justice movements, and the intersection of historical injustice with emerging techno-political structures.

(A) According to the A-B-C model , why is the anxiety and avoidance behavior reported by 22% who faced denied mall entry primarily indicative of a behavioral component, and how does this behavior reflect the strength of the underlying attitude?
Fill in the blank: Imagine you visit a ______ church in Kerala built by Portuguese missionaries in the 1500s.

A drought‑prone district in Marathwada (Maharashtra) has witnessed a 20 % decline in the area under sorghum (a drought‑tolerant millet) over the past five years, while the area under sugarcane (water‑intensive) has risen by 15 % due to assured irrigation from upstream dams. The state government, under the Thirteenth Finance Commission, allocates a special grant of ₹3.6 crores for CPR‑based climate adaptation. The grant is to be split among three interventions: (i) rejuvenation of village tanks (desilting, bund strengthening) at ₹1 200 per m³ of storage restored, (ii) promotion of drought‑resilient CPRs such as community‑managed fodder banks (cost ₹5 000 per ton of fodder stored), and (iii) provision of interest‑free credit to farmer producer organisations (FPOs) for shifting to pulses (cost ₹40 000 per FPO). The district has 150 village tanks with a combined current storage capacity of 9 00 000 m³; experts estimate that 30 % of this capacity is lost to siltation. The fodder bank aims to store 250 ton of fodder. There are 20 FPOs eligible for credit. The grant is to be distributed in the ratio 4:3:2 (tanks:fodder:credit). Answer the following.

(E) Which qualitative characteristic of accounting information (per Qualitative Characteristics) is most directly challenged if the state’s utilisation report shows the tank‑intervention expenditure as “₹1.6 lakhs” instead of “₹16 lakhs”?

If they walk this distance daily for a week, find the total distance covered by each person in metres.

In 2024, a team of urban engineers discovers an abandoned, intact platform beneath Grand Central Terminal, labeled “Level 3” on old 1930s schematics. The platform contains vintage ticket booths, 1940s-style advertisements, and a functioning telegraph line that sporadically prints messages dated 1918. The city’s mental‑health department commissions a report to decide whether this space should be (a) preserved as a historical artifact, (b) opened as a therapeutic “escape zone” for stressed commuters, or (c) sealed due to safety concerns. As a consultant, you must synthesize: (i) literal details from Finney’s story about Charley’s experience, (ii) the psychiatrist’s interpretation of the third level as a waking‑dream wish‑fulfillment, (iii) Freudian theory of repressed desires surfacing in dreams, (iv) sociological research on urban alienation and commuter stress, and (v) policy frameworks for public mental‑health interventions in transit hubs. Your report must justify each recommendation with evidence from the text and the cross‑disciplinary sources.

(C) Using sociological data on urban alienation, argue whether opening the platform as a therapeutic escape zone would likely reduce commuter stress or exacerbate avoidance behavior.

A chemical plant manufactures cyclohexyl chloride (C₆H₁₁Cl) via free‑radical chlorination of cyclohexane (C₆H₁₂) using Cl₂ under UV light (λ = 365 nm). The reactor operates at 350 K, with initial concentrations [C₆H₁₂] = 0.50 M and [Cl₂] = 0.40 M in a 2 L batch. The bond dissociation energy D(Cl–Cl) = 242 kJ mol⁻¹, D(C–H in cyclohexane) = 395 kJ mol⁻¹ (secondary H). Quantum yield for Cl· formation = 0.9. Termination occurs by combination of two carbon‑centred radicals (kₜ = 2.5×10⁸ M⁻¹ s⁻¹).  

The plant aims for 80 % conversion of cyclohexane within 2 h. After reaction, the product mixture contains cyclohexyl chloride (major) and 1,2‑dichlorocyclohexane (minor) due to radical addition to the double bond formed after H‑abstraction (allylic‑type pathway). The relative reactivity per H for chlorination is: 1° H = 1.0, 2° H = 3.8, 3° H = 5.0. In cyclohexane all H are secondary (2°). After one chlorination, the product cyclohexyl chloride retains five secondary H’s (still 2°) but one primary H (the carbon bearing Cl now has no H).  

The plant also needs to treat the HCl by‑product using a scrubber; the scrubber efficiency depends on the partial pressure of HCl, which can be estimated from the extent of reaction.  

Answer the following sub‑parts.

(C) Estimate the expected molar ratio of cyclohexyl chloride to 1,2‑dichlorocyclohexane after 80 % conversion of cyclohexane, assuming that the second chlorination occurs only on the carbon bearing the first Cl (i.e., gem‑dichlorination is negligible) and that the relative reactivity per H for the remaining H’s is unchanged (2° H = 3.8).

A student writes: "The new farmers' movements of the 1970s were led by rich farmers and ignored the problems of small peasants and landless laborers." Using the NCERT description, evaluate this statement. Is it fully accurate, partially accurate, or inaccurate? Justify with two specific points from the text.

A micro‑fluidic valve requires a fast‑acting solenoid actuator that can generate a pulling force of 0.2 N on a ferromagnetic plunger (relative permeability μᵣ≈5000) located 2 mm from the pole face. The actuator consists of a cylindrical coil (length L=15 mm, N=500 turns, wire cross‑section allowing a maximum current I_max=2 A) wound on a soft‑iron core (relative permeability μᵣ_core=2000). The plunger is a cylinder of radius r=1 mm and length ℓ=5 mm, made of the same soft‑iron material. The design tasks include: (i) estimating the magnetic field at the plunger tip, (ii) computing the resulting force using the energy method, (iii) checking for saturation of the core, (iv) evaluating the impact of coil resistance on power dissipation, and (v) suggesting material changes to increase force without exceeding thermal limits.

(A) Estimate the axial magnetic field B at the tip of the plunger assuming the solenoid produces a uniform field B_s = μ₀μᵣ_core n I inside its length (ignore fringing). Use I = 1.5 A.

A government hospital in Bhopal has a target to treat 500 patients per day in its OPD. The hospital administrator proposes two plans:
Plan 1: Hire 5 additional doctors at ₹1 lakh/month each, extend OPD hours by 2 hours. Expected outcome: 550 patients/day, cost increase ₹5 lakh/month.
Plan 2: Implement a digital token system and reorganise patient flow (one‑time cost ₹10 lakh, no recurring cost). Expected outcome: 520 patients/day with same doctors and hours.
The hospital's monthly budget increase limit is ₹4 lakh. Using the concepts of effectiveness and efficiency, recommend which plan the administrator should choose. Justify with calculations.

A micro‑grid uses a bank of identical lead‑acid secondary cells (PbO₂‖Pb‖H₂SO₄) for load leveling. Each cell has nominal voltage 2.0 V, capacity 100 Ah, and internal resistance r = 0.015 Ω at 25 °C. The bank consists of M cells in series to achieve a bus voltage of 48 V (nominal). During a peak‑shaving event, the bank discharges at a constant current I = 50 A for 2 h, then rests. The ambient temperature rises from 25 °C to 45 °C during discharge due to Joule heating and exothermic reaction (PbO₂ + H₂SO₄ + Pb → PbSO₄ + H₂O). The temperature coefficient of the open‑circuit voltage is dE/dT = –0.5 mV/K. The specific heat capacity of the cell (including electrolyte) is c = 0.9 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹, and each cell mass m_cell = 1.2 kg. Assume all generated heat stays within the cell (adiabatic approximation) and that the internal resistance varies with temperature as r(T) = r₀[1 + β(T–T₀)] with β = 0.003 °C⁻¹.  
Using the data, answer the following.

In early 2025, India signs a Precautionary and Liquidity Line (PLL) with the IMF amounting to SDR 5 billion, conditional on maintaining a flexible exchange‑rate regime and limiting foreign exchange market intervention to ≤ 1 % of monthly reserves. In the fictitious region of Kavir, the central government issues Ordinance 7/2024, effective 1 June 2025, mandating that all public schools use only the state language “Veridian” for instruction and assessment. Elders and parents sit on the back benches, their faces solemn. Ms. Lina begins by writing the Kaviri alphabet on the blackboard, her chalk squeaking softly—a sound she likens to “the whisper of a people refusing to be erased.” She tells her students, “Kaviri is not just a set of sounds; it is the key to our cultural prison. As the lesson ends, Ms. Lina steps back, looks at the board, and writes in large letters: “VIVE KAVIR!” The chalk dust settles like snow over the words. Outside, the Veridian flag is raised atop the school pole, yet the blackboard still holds the Kaviri proclamation, a silent act of defiance.  

The scenario invites readers to notice the imagery of the sunrise over the fields, the symbolic weight of the blackboard and chalk, and the ironic twist that the very order meant to erase Kaviri amplifies its presence in the hearts of the community.

The junction is reverse‑biased at \(V_R = 20\;\text{V}\). Incident monochromatic X‑ray photons of energy \(E_\gamma = 8\;\text{keV}\) create electron‑hole pairs in the depletion region. The average energy required to create one pair in Si is \(\varepsilon_i = 3.6\;\text{eV}\). The Fano factor for Si is \(F = 0.11\). The silicon permittivity is \(\varepsilon_s = 11.7\varepsilon_0\) with \(\varepsilon_0 = 8.85\times10^{-12}\;\text{F m}^{-1}\). The temperature of the detector is maintained at \(T = 200\;\text{K}\). The band‑gap of Si follows the Varshni relation  
\[
E_g(T)=E_{g0}-\frac{\alpha T^2}{T+\beta},
\qquad
E_{g0}=1.17\;\text{eV},\;\alpha=4.73\times10^{-4}\;\text{eV K}^{-1},\;\beta=636\;\text{K}.
\]
The leakage current obeys \(I_{\text{leak}} = I_0\exp\!\big[-E_g(T)/(2kT)\big]\) with \(k=8.617\times10^{-5}\;\text{eV K}^{-1}\). A charge‑sensitive preamplifier with feedback capacitance \(C_f = 0.5\;\text{pF}\) converts the collected charge into a voltage pulse.

A multinational tech firm launches “LinguaGuard”, an AI‑driven mobile app promised to revitalize endangered regional languages by offering interactive lessons, speech‑recognition feedback, and community forums. The app’s interface, however, is available only in English, and advanced features require a subscription priced at €9.99/month. In the fictional nation of Verdania, a minority language spoken by 12% of the population faces decline due to urban migration and prestige of the national language. The government mandates that all public‑school teachers use LinguaGuard for language‑revitalization workshops, arguing that the tool will bridge the digital divide. Teachers, many of whom are elderly and unfamiliar with smartphones, must attend training sessions conducted in English, while students receive lessons in their native tongue via the app’s voice‑guided modules. Ironically, the tool meant to preserve linguistic heritage reinforces English proficiency as a gate‑keeper to its benefits. The app’s logo—a stylized feather losing its barbs—symbolizes the fragility of the language it aims to save. Subscription revenue is recognized under IFRS 15: the firm allocates the monthly fee to lesson delivery (60%) and platform maintenance (40%), recognizing revenue as services are performed. Using the data: 150,000 active users, average revenue per user (ARPU) €8.50/month, monthly operating costs €900,000, students must identify irony (English‑mediated preservation), symbolism (the fading feather), apply revenue recognition (allocating and timing revenue), and use basic political‑science concepts (language rights, digital inclusion) to evaluate the policy.

(D) Explain how the principle of linguistic minority rights (as outlined in the UN Declaration on the Rights of Persons Belonging to National or Ethnic, Religious and Linguistic Minorities) conflicts with the app’s English‑only interface, and evaluate the government’s mandate in light of this principle.

FinPay, a Series‑A fintech startup offering a mobile‑based digital wallet, has deployed an AI‑driven real‑time transaction monitoring system (control mechanism) to flag potentially fraudulent transfers. The system scans every transaction for anomalies (e.g., sudden high‑value transfers to new beneficiaries) and auto‑blocks suspicious ones after a 2‑second review. After six months, management notes: (i) the system flags 0.8 % of genuine transactions as fraudulent (false positives), causing customer complaints; (ii) a sudden RBI guideline change mandating additional KYC fields rendered part of the rule‑base obsolete, increasing manual override work; (iii) the compliance team feels the constant surveillance undermines trust and has shown a 12 % rise in attrition; (iv) the system’s annual operating cost (software licences, data‑storage, analyst salaries) is ₹ 4.8 crore, while the estimated loss prevented from fraud is ₹ 3.2 crore. The CFO asks the controlling team to evaluate whether the control system is effective given its limitations.

(E) Perform a simple cost‑benefit analysis using ROI (Return on Investment) to decide whether the monitoring system should be continued. Use the formula ROI = (Net Gain / Investment) × 100, where Net Gain = Estimated fraud loss prevented – (Actual operating cost + Implicit attrition cost). State the ROI percentage and interpret the result in light of the limitation of high control costs.

Economic forecasts estimate that the finance sector will contribute US$15 billion/yr to Gujarat’s GSDP by 2035, while the technology sector will add US$8 billion/yr. - Residential zone proportion: 30 %

- Projected workforce (2035): 600,000  
- Finance sector GSDP contribution (2035): US$15 billion/yr  
- Technology sector GSDP contribution (2035): US$8 billion/yr

- Projected Gini coefficient (2035) without intervention: 0.42  
- Affordable housing target: 40 % of residential units

(A) Calculate the land area (in hectares) allocated to residential zones in GIFT City.

The Shimla Municipal Corporation proposes to redevelop the 120‑acre colonial‑era Cantonment Board area (established 1864) into a “Heritage‑Live‑Work” zone: boutique hotels, co‑working spaces, and a cultural mall. The plan requires relocating 350 families who have used the adjoining meadows for seasonal grazing since the 1950s. Local historians note the cantonment was originally laid out on the European town‑native town segregation model, with wide boulevards, segregated bazaars, and restricted native access to the ridge. Political activists cite the 74th Constitutional Amendment (municipal empowerment) and demand a Gram Sabha‑style consultation under the Panchayati (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996. Geographers warn that the steep slope (average gradient 1:12) and monsoon‑induced landslide risk limit high‑density construction. Using concepts of colonial urbanism, administrative history, local governance, and hill‑station geography, evaluate the proposal’s social impact.

(B) Explain how colonial capitalism (c12_soc_cbse_08_002) shaped the economic function of the Shimla cantonment beyond military use.

The forested state of Vananchal (population 12 million) has 18 % scheduled tribal (ST) inhabitants (≈2.16 million) living in Protected Areas. A new mining project threatens 500 km² of habitat. The central government proposes an environmental compensation package: ₹15,000 per hectare of degraded forest, to be paid to the Vananchal State Government, which must then disburse 40 % directly to affected ST households as livelihood support and retain 60 % for state‑level reforestation. Simultaneously, the state demands a higher share of central taxes under Article 270 (based on the 1971 census population) to fund its tribal welfare schemes. AutoMakers Ltd. manufactures mid‑size cars. Market demand is Qd = 500 – 3P (P in ₹ lakhs per car, Q in thousand cars per quarter). Original supply, based on domestic steel input, is Qs = –50 + 2P. A sudden 25 % import tariff on steel raises the effective steel price, shifting supply leftward by 30 thousand cars at every price: Qs′ = –80 + 2P. The firm’s quarterly fixed cost is ₹15 crores; variable cost per car is ₹4 lakhs; depreciation on the plant is ₹2 crores per quarter. Assume perfect competition.

(D) Journalise the quarterly effect of the tariff on AutoMakers’ raw‑material inventory (steel) assuming the firm purchases steel equal to the variable cost per car and holds no opening inventory.

A vaccine manufacturer aims to produce hepatitis B virus‑like particles (VLPs) using a yeast *Pichia pastoris* system expressing HBsAg. The process employs a 1 000 L perfusion bioreactor with cell‑retention filter, allowing high cell density and continuous product harvest. The VLPs must assemble correctly, requiring proper disulfide bond formation in the oxidative extracellular environment of the yeast secretory pathway. The following data characterize the system:

- Specific growth rate on methanol (µₘₐₓ) = 0.18 h⁻¹  
- Monod constant for methanol (Kₛ) = 0.5 g L⁻¹  
- Desired methanol concentration (S) = 0.05 g L⁻¹ (to minimize oxidative stress)  
- Yeast yield on methanol, Yₓ/ₛ = 0.4 g g⁻¹  
- VLP yield on biomass, Yₚ/ₓ = 0.015 g g⁻¹ (15 mg VLP per g dry cell weight)  
- Cell‑retention filter permits a bleed rate (F_b) equal to 10 % of the perfusion rate (F_p).  
- Perfusion rate (F_p) = 200 L h⁻¹ (fresh medium with 100 g L⁻¹ methanol).  
- Culture volume V = 1 000 L (constant).  
- Oxygen transfer: kLa = 300 h⁻¹, C* = 0.007 mol L⁻¹, set‑point Cₗ = 0.0015 mol L⁻¹.  
- Power number for pitched‑blade turbine, Po = 1.4.  
- Fluid density ρ = 1 010 kg m⁻³.  
- Impeller diameter D = 0.55 m.  
- Real‑time PAT (Process Analytical Technology) measures extracellular reduced glutathione (GSH) concentration; optimal disulfide formation occurs when [GSH] < 0.2 mM. GSH is produced intracellularly at a rate r_GSH = 0.05 mmol g⁻¹ h⁻¹·X and exported proportionally to extracellular volume with factor f = 0.1 L g⁻¹.  
- The extracellular volume is approximated as the culture volume (since cells occupy < 5 %).  

Using the information, answer the sub‑parts below. Show all steps, state assumptions, and keep units consistent.

(C) Calculate the oxygen uptake rate (OUR) required to maintain the set dissolved oxygen concentration.

A city‑government plans to rehabilitate a 15‑acre slum settlement in Bengaluru, relocating 8,000 residents to newly built tenements. The project’s social‑impact unit proposes a **mandatory “Quiet Hour”** each workday for site supervisors and contractors, during which no machinery may operate and personnel must remain still, inspired by Neruda’s vision of a collective pause to “interrupt this sadness of never understanding ourselves”. The unit must (a) justify the Quiet Hour using the poem’s distinction between quiet reflection and total inactivity, (b) link it to the historical principle of **“Restorative Justice”** applied in post‑conflict urban rebuilding (e.g., Sarajevo, Medellín), (c) evaluate the financial implication using **governmental accounting** concepts of **budgetary control** and **opportunity cost**, and (d) design a Speaking‑and‑Listening framework for community leaders to discuss the Quiet Hour’s effectiveness, drawing on the poem’s call for “brothers in the shade, doing nothing”.  
Provided data: average daily contractor wage ₹1,200, average supervisor wage ₹2,000, 150 contractors and 30 supervisors on site, Quiet Hour duration 1 hour per day, project duration 24 months, estimated reduction in workplace accidents 25 % (baseline annual accident cost ₹1,80,00,000), and a contingency fund of ₹5,00,00,000 set aside for unforeseen expenses. Identify the applicable poetic, historical, and accounting concepts, then calculate the **opportunity cost of the Quiet Hour in monetary terms** over the entire project duration.

(E) Calculate the total opportunity cost of the Quiet Hour over the full 24‑month period (assuming 26 working days per month) and compare it to the accident‑cost saving from SUB_PART_D. State whether the Quiet Hour is financially justified on this narrow metric.

Create a 3-step mini research plan for a local bakery "Sweet Crust" wanting to know if adding sugar-free cakes will increase profits. Include: problem definition, one primary method, one secondary source, and the decision rule (e.g., "If >30% existing customers show interest, launch").

An interdisciplinary team aims to build a quantitative “Climate‑Migration Vulnerability Index” (CMVI) for coastal districts of the Bay of Bengal. They have gathered: (a) satellite‑derived sea‑level rise (SLR) rates (mm/yr) for the last two decades, (b) decadal counts of climate‑induced displacement events (from humanitarian agency records) spanning 1980‑2020, and (c) national asylum‑approval rates (%) for applicants citing environmental distress (from ministry of home affairs). SLR shows modest right‑skew (skewness≈0.9) with a few outlier districts experiencing accelerated subsidence. Displacement counts are highly over‑dispersed (variance ≫ mean) and contain many zeros. Asylum rates are bounded between 0 and 100 % and display a left‑skew. To combine these indicators into a single index suitable for regression analysis and cross‑national comparison, the team must: (i) select appropriate transformations for each series (log for SLR, log‑(x+1) for displacement, logit for asylum rates), (ii) normalise the transformed variables to a common scale (z‑score), (iii) compute association matrices (Pearson for continuous‑continuous, polyserial for mixed types), and (iv) interpret the resulting index in light of historical patterns of climate‑driven migration (c11_geo_cbse_01_008) and contemporary asylum‑law frameworks (c10_civ_cbse_01_001).  

The following data for five representative districts are provided:

| District | SLR (mm/yr) | Displacement (events/decade) | Asylum % |
|----------|-------------|------------------------------|----------|
| D1       | 2.1         | 0                            | 12       |
| D2       | 3.4         | 2                            | 18       |
| D3       | 4.0         | 5                            | 25       |
| D4       | 5.6         | 12                           | 32       |
| D5       | 9.3         | 30                           | 45       |

All calculations may be performed on this five‑district sample; the same procedures extend to the full coastal dataset.

(D) Using the correlation results, decide whether to retain all three transformed variables in a simple additive index or to apply dimensionality reduction (e.g., principal component analysis). Justify your answer with reference to the eigenvalue‑one rule.

A multinational agribusiness operates an olive oil extraction plant in Crete (Greece) processing 50 000 t/yr of olives. Current average yield = 1.6 t/ha, farmgate price = €0.55/kg, processing cost = €0.10/kg, transport cost to port = €0.02/kg. Climate projections (IPCC RCP 4.5) indicate Crete’s summer drought intensity will increase by 25 % by 2040, reducing olive yield by 12 % (linear). Meanwhile, the Moroccan region of Sousse offers projected yield = 2.0 t/ha under same climate, price = €0.50/kg, processing cost = €0.09/kg, transport cost = €0.015/kg (closer to EU market). The firm considers shifting 60 % of its raw material sourcing to Morocco while retaining 40 % in Crete. Capital required to expand Moroccan processing capacity = €12 million (CAPEX), lifespan 10 yr, salvage 10 %, discount rate 6 %. Using accounting (cash flow, NPV), geography (Mediterranean agriculture suitability, market gardening potential for intercropping legumes), and political science (supranational power sharing in EU‑Morocco Association Agreement – horizontal distribution among EU Commission, Council, Parliament, and Moroccan legislature), evaluate whether the relocation yields a positive NPV over 10 years.

(E) Identify which EU institution, under the horizontal power‑sharing model of the EU‑Morocco Association Agreement, has the final say on approving the agreement’s trade‑liberalisation clauses.

In 2025 the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) proposes a “Symbolic Species Initiative” allowing limited, regulated trade in products derived from charismatic megafauna (e.g., tiger bone amulets) to fund community‑based conservation in Southeast Asia, citing the Tiger King’s tale as a cautionary exemplar of unchecked ambition. The proposal argues that regulated trade will reduce poaching by providing legal alternatives, while critics warn it will legitimize demand, spur illegal laundering, and repeat the King’s tragic miscalculation. Supporting data: (a) Global tiger poaching incidents fell 60% after 2010 CITES ban but rose 12% in 2023 in regions with exemptions for “cultural artifacts”; (b) Community surveys show 38% of villagers would consider purchasing a legal tiger‑bone amulet if priced under $5; (c) Ecological models indicate a 0.07 increase in annual mortality could shift source populations to sinks in the Western Ghats.
You must critique the IUCN proposal using: (i) satire and irony from *The Tiger King*, (ii) concepts of legal pluralism and sustainable use from International Environmental Law, (iii) socio‑economic behavior theory (bounded rationality, prospect theory), and (iv) source‑sink metapopulation dynamics.

(B) Evaluate the IUCN proposal under the principle of sustainable use in International Environmental Law, considering the data on poaching trends and community willingness to pay, and determine whether the proposal satisfies the “non‑detriment” requirement.
