A solid is formed by cutting a right circular cone of height 12 cm and base radius 6 cm with a plane parallel to the base at a distance of 4 cm from the base. The top smaller cone is removed. What is the name of the remaining solid, and how many circular faces does it have?

A frustum has radii 10 cm and 6 cm, and vertical height 8 cm. A student computes the slant height as \(l = \sqrt{8^2 + (10+6)^2} = \sqrt{64+256} = \sqrt{320}\). Is this correct? Explain why or why not.

A solid cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 10 cm is melted and recast into a solid cone of the same base radius. A student writes: "Curved surface area of cylinder = Curved surface area of cone" to find the height of the cone. Is this correct? Explain why or why not.

A solid toy is in the shape of a right circular cylinder with a hemisphere at one end and a cone at the other end. The radius of the common base is 3.5 cm. The height of the cylindrical part is 10 cm and the height of the conical part is 6 cm. Write the formula for the total surface area of the toy. (Do not compute the numerical value.)

A decorative block is made of a cube of edge 6 cm and a hemisphere of diameter 4.2 cm fixed on top of the cube. A student computes the total surface area as 6 × (6)² + 2π(2.1)². Explain why this is incorrect and write the correct expression.

A student connects a thick copper wire vertically between a battery and a switch. The current flows upward. A small compass is placed 5 cm east of the wire. When the switch is closed, which direction will the compass needle's north pole point? (Assume no other magnetic fields.)

Two identical long straight wires carry currents of 2 A and 4 A respectively. At a distance of 10 cm from each wire, what is the ratio of the magnetic field magnitudes B₁:B₂? Explain why this ratio does NOT depend on the distance value (as long as it's the same for both).
A circular loop of radius 5 cm carries a current of 2 A. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at its centre? (Take \( \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7} \, \text{T·m/A} \))

A copper wire of length 10 cm carries a current of 2 A and is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the wire is now tilted so that it makes an angle of 30° with the field, how does the force change? Explain why the force depends on \( \sin\theta \).

A circular coil of 50 turns and area 0.02 m² is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.5 T. The field is reduced to zero uniformly in 0.1 s. Calculate the magnitude of the average induced emf. Explain why the emf is zero if the coil is rotated 90° so its plane becomes parallel to the field before the field is reduced.

A modern ultra-supercritical thermal power plant operates at 45% efficiency while an older subcritical plant operates at 33%. Both plants are required to deliver 500 MW of electrical power. Explain why the ultra-supercritical plant burns less coal per second, using the efficiency formula. What happens to the "missing" energy in the older plant?

Explain why binary cycle power plants can generate electricity from lower-temperature geothermal resources (100–180°C) while dry steam plants require >230°C, referencing the working fluid's thermodynamic properties.

A student holds a lens towards the sun and obtains a sharp bright spot on a screen placed 15 cm from the lens. What type of lens is it, and what is its focal length? State the sign of the focal length as per Cartesian sign convention.

A convex lens of focal length 10 cm forms a real image of an object placed 15 cm from the lens. Without calculating, explain whether the image distance will be greater than, equal to, or less than 15 cm, and whether the image will be magnified or diminished.
State the SI unit of power of a lens and write the formula relating power (P) and focal length (f). What is the power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm?

A business purchases a delivery van for ₹8,00,000, paying ₹3,00,000 cash and signing a ₹5,00,000 loan agreement. The van has a useful life of 5 years. Explain why the *entire* van (₹8,00,000) is recorded as an asset, while only ₹5,00,000 is a liability. What happens to the ₹3,00,000 cash paid?

A business owns the following: (i) Land 5 acres purchased at ₹50 lakh, (ii) 20 experienced workers, (iii) Brand reputation built over 10 years, (iv) Bank balance ₹10 lakh, (v) Raw material 1000 kg purchased at ₹200/kg. Explain which items will appear in the Balance Sheet and why, using the Money Measurement Concept.

A company purchases a patent for ₹10,00,000 with a legal life of 10 years. After 10 years, the patent cannot be used. Which cause of depreciation (amortisation) applies here, and why is it NOT wear and tear?

A machine is purchased for ₹5,00,000. Freight and installation cost ₹50,000. The estimated scrap value after 10 years is ₹60,000, and disposal expenses are estimated at ₹10,000. What is the depreciable cost? Explain why the purchase price alone is not the depreciable cost.

A machine is purchased for ₹2,00,000 on 1st July 2023. Installation costs ₹20,000. Estimated useful life is 10 years and scrap value ₹20,000. The firm closes books on 31st March. Explain why the depreciation for the first year (2023-24) is NOT simply 10% of ₹2,20,000.

A machine costs ₹5,00,000 with scrap value ₹50,000 and useful life 5 years. Under WDV method at 20% p.a., the depreciation for Year 3 is ₹64,000. Explain WHY the Year 3 depreciation is lower than Year 1's ₹1,00,000, even though the rate (20%) is constant.

A company purchases a delivery van for ₹10,00,000 with estimated life 5 years, scrap ₹1,00,000. Under SLM, annual depreciation is ₹1,80,000. Under WDV at 30%, Year 1 depreciation is ₹3,00,000. Explain why the WDV charge is higher initially but will be lower in Year 5, and what this implies for profit reporting in early vs. late years.

A machine was purchased on 1st October 2022 for ₹2,00,000. The firm closes books on 31st March and charges depreciation @10% p.a. on original cost under the Provision for Depreciation method. Calculate the depreciation for the first year (2022-23) and show the journal entry on 31st March 2023.

Explain why charging depreciation at 20% per annum on a machine with a useful life of 10 years (instead of 10% per annum) creates a secret reserve. Use the terms "Profit and Loss Account", "Asset Account", and "Balance Sheet" in your explanation.
A business has an operating cycle of 18 months. It holds raw materials that will be used in production in 14 months. Classify this raw material and justify whether it is current or non-current.
A business has an operating cycle of 15 months. On the Balance Sheet date, it has a loan installment of ₹50,000 due in 14 months. Is this Current or Non-Current? Explain.

State the journal entry for depreciation charged on machinery at 10% per annum on Straight Line Method when machinery appears in the Trial Balance at ₹2,00,000 and the adjustment says "Depreciation on machinery @ 10% p.a. on SLM."

A business receives ₹12,000 rent on March 1, 2024 for 12 months (March 2024 – February 2025). The accounting year ends March 31, 2024. The bookkeeper records the full ₹12,000 as Rent Received in the P&L. Explain why this violates the accrual concept and state the correct adjustment with amounts.
State the journal entry for providing depreciation on machinery at 10% p.a. when machinery appears in the trial balance at ₹2,00,000. Also state the dual effect of this entry on final accounts.

A trial balance shows Sundry Debtors ₹80,000, Bad Debts ₹2,000, Provision for Doubtful Debts ₹4,000. The firm decides to maintain a provision for bad debts of ₹1,000 and create a provision for discount on debtors @ 2%. What is the amount of provision for discount on debtors?
State the journal entry for providing interest on capital at 10% p.a. on opening capital of ₹2,00,000.
A proprietor withdrew ₹10,000 on 1st July, 1st October, and 1st January. Rate of interest on drawings is 12% p.a. Explain why we cannot simply calculate 12% on ₹30,000 for the full year.
A cyclist rides 3 km east, then 4 km north in a total of 30 minutes. What is the magnitude of the cyclist's average velocity? (Give answer in km/h with direction.)
A cyclist goes 3 km east then 4 km north. Distance and displacement?
An athlete completes one full lap of a 400 m track. Distance and displacement?
A car covers half a distance at 40 km/h and half at 60 km/h. Average speed?
A train covers 120 km in 2 h, then halts 30 min. Average speed for the whole trip?

Explain in your own words why "the collection of all intelligent students in Class 11" is **not** a set, but "the collection of all students in Class 11 who scored above 90% in the Term 1 exam" **is** a set.

The NCERT text says: "Study of changes tend to be simpler if we study it by considering changes over tiny interval of time (instantaneous) rather than studying changes over a period of time." Explain *why* this is true, using the example of a car accelerating from 0 to 60 km/h in 10 seconds.

In the medical testing example from the textbook (liver disease prevalence 10%, alcoholism rate 5%, 7% of liver patients are alcoholic), a student calculates P(Alcoholic|Liver Disease) = 7% and claims this is the answer to "probability of liver disease given alcoholic." Explain why this reasoning is incorrect and identify the specific probabilities that were confused.
Find SI on ₹10,000 at 10% for 3 years.
Find the CI amount on ₹10,000 at 10% for 3 years.
₹1,000/month for 12 months at 1%/month — why is FV more than ₹12,000?

Explain why the floral formula for a zygomorphic, bisexual flower with 5 gamosepalous sepals, 5 gamopetalous petals (vexillary aestivation), 10 diadelphous stamens (9+1), and a monocarpellary superior ovary is written as: % ⚥ K(5) C(5) A(9)+1 G̅(1). Specifically justify the use of % instead of ⊕, brackets for K and C, and the notation A(9)+1.

A student observes two cells under a microscope: Cell A has a distinct nuclear membrane and 80S ribosomes; Cell B lacks a nuclear membrane and has 70S ribosomes. Which cell is prokaryotic and which is eukaryotic? Justify your answer using two structural criteria.
Why does the plasma membrane remain fluid at body temperature (37°C) despite phospholipids being tightly packed? Explain the role of cholesterol in this context.
Why do mitochondrial ribosomes in eukaryotic cells resemble prokaryotic (70S) ribosomes rather than cytoplasmic (80S) ribosomes?
Define 'optimum temperature' for an enzyme and state what happens to the enzyme's tertiary structure when the temperature rises 10°C above this optimum.
What are the two main phases of the cell cycle, and which phase occupies more than 95% of the total cycle duration in a typical human cell?
State Blackman's Law of Limiting Factors and identify which factor would limit photosynthesis in a well-watered C3 plant at 10% full sunlight, 35°C, and ambient CO₂ (0.04%).

Explain why increasing CO₂ concentration from 0.04% to 0.05% boosts photosynthesis in C3 plants but has little effect on C4 plants at high light intensity, referencing the CO₂ compensation point and RuBisCO kinetics.

Define "critical photoperiod" and explain why a short-day plant like chrysanthemum (critical night length 12 hours) fails to flower when exposed to a 14-hour day / 10-hour night cycle, but flowers under 10-hour day / 14-hour night.

A long-day plant (spinach, critical night length 8 hours) is grown under 16L/8D and flowers. The same plant is given a 1-hour red light pulse in the middle of an otherwise 16-hour night (8L/1D/15D). Will it flower? Justify using phytochrome interconversion.

A batch of apple seeds fails to germinate after being sown in moist soil at 25°C. The seed coats are permeable, and embryos are fully developed. Explain why these seeds are likely dormant and name the specific type of dormancy.
Why does CO₂ diffuse from blood to alveoli even though its partial pressure gradient (5 mm Hg) is much smaller than that of O₂ (64 mm Hg)?
Define the oxygen dissociation curve and state the percentage saturation of haemoglobin at a pO₂ of 100 mm Hg under normal physiological conditions.
Name the specific nephron segment where 100% of filtered glucose is normally reabsorbed, and identify the transport mechanism (including the co-transported ion) responsible.
Explain why Louis Pasteur's work (1850s-1860s) represents a fundamental epistemological break from all prior fermentation practices, using the phrase "black box" in your answer.

A student observes a cell under an electron microscope and notes: (1) genetic material in a nucleoid region, (2) 70S ribosomes, (3) a cell wall containing peptidoglycan, and (4) flagella with a 9+0 microtubule arrangement. Identify the cell type and list the four structural features that confirm this classification.

Explain why the presence of 70S ribosomes in both prokaryotes and eukaryotic mitochondria/chloroplasts does NOT contradict the classification of mitochondria-containing cells as eukaryotic. Use the concept of compartmentalization in your answer.
A student claims: "Mitochondria have 70S ribosomes because they are prokaryotes." Explain why this statement is incorrect while identifying the valid evolutionary insight it contains.
Name the three distinct compartments created by the chloroplast membrane system and state which compartment contains the 70S ribosomes and circular DNA.
What are the two subunits of a eukaryotic 80S ribosome and their respective Svedberg values?
Why do mitochondrial ribosomes (70S) resemble prokaryotic ribosomes rather than the cytoplasmic 80S ribosomes of the same eukaryotic cell?

A student claims: "Water has a high boiling point because its molecules are heavy." Critique this statement using the concept of hydrogen bonding and compare water (M = 18 g·mol⁻¹, bp = 100°C) with hydrogen sulfide H₂S (M = 34 g·mol⁻¹, bp = –60°C).

In a test cross of a dihybrid F1 (AaBb) with a double recessive (aabb), you observe the following progeny: 42% AB, 42% ab, 8% Ab, 8% aB. Are the genes linked? If so, is it complete or incomplete linkage? Justify using the expected ratio under independent assortment.

In Morgan's Drosophila experiment, grey body (B) and long wings (V) are dominant over black body (b) and vestigial wings (v). A test cross of F1 heterozygote (BbVv) with double recessive (bbvv) produced 83% parental and 17% recombinant offspring. Explain why the recombinant frequency is 17% and not 50%, and what this reveals about the physical relationship between the two genes.

A student writes: "During translation initiation in prokaryotes, the 30S ribosomal subunit binds directly to the AUG start codon on the mRNA." Is this statement correct? If not, identify the missing molecular component and its function.
Why is colchicine added to lymphocyte cultures during karyotype preparation, and what would be the consequence if the incubation time exceeded 2 hours?
Explain why maternal age over 35 years is a risk factor for Down syndrome, but paternal age is not significantly associated.

A researcher in India submits a novel DNA sequence to GenBank today. Explain why the same sequence will appear in EMBL and DDBJ within 24 hours without the researcher submitting separately to those databases.

A student says: "For aligning two sequences that are 30% identical, I should use PAM30 because the number matches the percentage identity." Explain why this reasoning is incorrect and state which matrix (PAM or BLOSUM, and which number) would be more appropriate.

A student claims: "If I have 40% sequence identity between my target and a template, the homology model will be as accurate as an experimentally determined structure." Explain why this statement is incorrect, referencing specific sources of error in homology modelling.

A student runs BLAST on a query sequence and gets a hit with 35% identity over 80% length to a "serine protease" (E-value 1e-50). They conclude the query is definitely a serine protease. Explain why this conclusion might be premature, using the concept of conserved domains vs. full-length homology.

Define magnification and resolution of a microscope. A student uses a compound microscope with a 40× objective and a 10× eyepiece. What is the total magnification? If the image of a cell appears 8 mm wide, what is the actual width of the cell in micrometers?
What is the primary function of fetal bovine serum (FBS) in animal cell culture media, and why is it typically used at 5-10% concentration rather than 100%?

A student prepares MS medium for plant tissue culture but forgets to add agar. The medium remains liquid after autoclaving. When they place a leaf explant on this liquid medium, the explant floats and turns brown within 3 days. Explain why the explant failed to form callus, referencing both physical and physiological factors.

A trader in Kolkata purchases 500 kg of tea from a plantation in Assam and sells it to a retailer in Mumbai. Classify this trade transaction and justify your classification using two distinct criteria.

Rahul runs a sole proprietorship grocery store. He takes a loan of ₹5 lakh for expansion but the business fails. The business assets are worth ₹2 lakh. Explain whether Rahul's personal car (worth ₹8 lakh) can be seized by the bank to recover the remaining ₹3 lakh.

Two partners, A and B, start a firm without a written deed. A contributes ₹10 lakh capital; B contributes ₹2 lakh but works full-time. After one year, the firm earns ₹6 lakh profit. A demands 5:1 profit sharing (capital ratio); B demands 1:1 (equal sharing as per Act default). Who is legally correct, and which deed clause would have prevented this dispute?

A student claims: "Since the government owns 51% of a Government Company, the company is just a department of the government and its employees are government servants." Explain why this statement is incorrect by contrasting any two features of Government Companies with Departmental Undertakings.

A factory owner insures his machinery worth ₹50 lakh under two policies: Policy X for ₹30 lakh and Policy Y for ₹40 lakh. A fire causes ₹20 lakh damage. The owner claims ₹20 lakh from Policy X and ₹20 lakh from Policy Y, totalling ₹40 lakh. Explain why this claim violates the Principle of Contribution and state the correct amount each insurer should pay.

A manufacturer in Ludhiana needs to send 50 tonnes of machinery parts to a client in Kolkata. The parts are heavy, non-perishable, and the client wants delivery within 10 days at the lowest possible cost. Explain why rail transport would be more suitable than air transport for this consignment.

A public company limited by shares adopts Table F of Schedule I as its Articles of Association without any modifications. Six months later, the company passes a special resolution to alter its articles to introduce a provision that "no shareholder holding less than 5% of paid-up capital can vote at general meetings." Is this alteration valid? Explain with reference to the Companies Act, 2013.

A public company files a prospectus and receives applications for 85% of the issue size. The directors want to proceed with allotment to those applicants and use the funds. Explain why this is not permitted under the Companies Act and SEBI guidelines.

A student says: "Fixed capital and long-term sources are the same thing because both are for more than 5 years." Explain why this statement is incorrect using the distinction between *need* (capital requirement) and *source* (financing instrument).

A company issues 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹10 face value at a premium of ₹40. The floatation costs are 3% of issue price. Explain why the 'cost of equity' is not simply the dividend rate, and calculate the net proceeds per share to the company.

A service enterprise has investment in equipment of ₹8 crore and annual turnover of ₹45 crore. Classify it as Micro, Small, or Medium and explain why it cannot be classified as Micro even though its turnover is below ₹50 crore.

A micro enterprise in the handloom sector has an investment in plant and machinery of ₹80 lakh and an annual turnover of ₹4 crore. According to the MSMED Act 2006 (as amended in 2020), this enterprise is classified as a micro enterprise. State TRUE or FALSE and justify your answer using the investment and turnover criteria.
Name the scheme that provides collateral-free credit guarantee cover to Micro and Small Enterprises for loans up to ₹5 crore, and state the maximum guarantee coverage percentage available under it.

A first-generation entrepreneur wants to set up a manufacturing unit with a project cost of ₹15 lakh. She has no collateral and belongs to the General category. Explain why PMEGP is more suitable than MUDRA for her, and calculate the maximum margin money subsidy she can avail under PMEGP (urban area, general category).

A student classifies a roadside fruit seller who operates from a fixed wooden cart parked at the same street corner every day for 10 years as an "itinerant retailer" because "he sells on the roadside." Is this classification correct? Explain why or why not using the defining characteristic of itinerant retailers.

When 10.0 g of solid calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) is heated strongly in an OPEN test tube, the solid residue masses 5.6 g. A student claims this violates the Law of Conservation of Mass. Explain why the student is wrong, identifying the missing product and its mass.

In the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), 100 mL of N₂ reacts completely with 300 mL of H₂. Explain why the total volume of reactants (400 mL) does not equal the volume of product (200 mL), and why this does not violate Gay Lussac's Law.
Chlorine exists as two isotopes: ³⁵Cl (75.77%, 34.9689 u) and ³⁷Cl (24.23%, 36.9659 u). Calculate the average atomic mass of chlorine. Why is the result closer to 35 than to 37?
Explain why the molar mass of water (H₂O) is 18.02 g mol⁻¹ while its molecular mass is 18.02 u. Why are the numerical values identical but the units different?
Explain why the molar mass of sodium chloride (NaCl) is calculated using the formula mass (58.5 g mol⁻¹) rather than a molecular mass, even though both are expressed in g mol⁻¹.
A student calculates %O in H₂SO₄ as (16/98)×100 = 16.33%. Explain why this is incorrect and give the correct calculation.
A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen, and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is the first step to determine its empirical formula?
In the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) → 2NH₃(g), if you start with 2 moles of N₂ and 4 moles of H₂, which reactant is the limiting reagent and why? State the answer in one sentence.

A student claims: "In any reaction, the reactant with the smaller mass in grams is always the limiting reagent." Explain why this statement is chemically incorrect using the reaction 2Mg(s) + O₂(g) → 2MgO(s) with 10 g Mg and 10 g O₂ as a counterexample.
A student prepares 500 mL of 0.2 M NaOH solution by dissolving 4.0 g NaOH in 500 mL water. Is this procedure correct? Explain why or why not.
A solution contains 2 mol of ethanol (C₂H₅OH) and 3 mol of water. Calculate the mole fraction of ethanol. If a student answers 0.6, what conceptual error have they made?
What is the molar volume of an ideal gas at STP (Standard Temperature and Pressure: 0°C, 1 bar) as per current IUPAC convention, and how does it differ from the pre-1982 convention?

In the reaction 2Al + 3Cl₂ → 2AlCl₃, 5.4 g Al reacts with 7.1 g Cl₂. A student calculates moles Al = 0.2 mol, moles Cl₂ = 0.1 mol, and concludes Al is limiting because 0.2 > 0.1. Explain why this reasoning is chemically incorrect.
Why does a baseball (mass 0.15 kg, speed 40 m/s) not exhibit observable diffraction while an electron (mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg, speed 10⁶ m/s) does? Calculate both wavelengths to justify.
State the shape of a 3s orbital and the number of radial nodes it possesses. How does its boundary surface diagram differ from that of a 1s orbital?
Explain why the 4s orbital fills before the 3d orbital, even though n=4 > n=3. Use the (n + l) rule in your explanation.

Explain why the 4th period contains 18 elements while the 3rd period contains only 8, even though both start with an s-orbital filling (4s and 3s respectively). Use the (n+l) rule in your explanation.
Explain why the boiling point of Cl₂ (−34°C) is higher than that of F₂ (−188°C) despite both being nonpolar diatomic molecules with zero dipole moment.
Explain why HF forms stronger hydrogen bonds than H₂O, yet water has a higher boiling point (100°C vs 19.5°C).
A gas occupies 500 mL at 1 atm pressure. If the volume is reduced to 250 mL at the same temperature, what is the new pressure? Explain why the pressure changes in terms of particle collisions.
A student writes V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ and substitutes T₁ = 27°C and T₂ = 127°C directly. The calculated V₂ is wrong. Explain why this substitution is invalid and what the correct temperatures in Kelvin are.
A student writes: "At STP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L. Therefore, at 273 K and 1 bar, 1 mole occupies 22.4 L." Identify the error and calculate the correct molar volume at 1 bar and 273 K.
A mixture contains 2 moles of N₂ and 3 moles of O₂ in a 10 L vessel at 300 K. The total pressure is measured as 12.3 atm. Explain why the partial pressure of N₂ is 4.92 atm and not 6.15 atm.

Two gases A and B have molar masses 16 g mol⁻¹ and 64 g mol⁻¹ respectively. At the same temperature and pressure, gas A diffuses 4 times faster than gas B. Is this statement correct? Explain using kinetic molecular theory.

A student argues: "Since gas molecules move at ~500 m/s at room temperature, a perfume molecule should cross a 5 m room in 0.01 s. But we smell it after minutes. Therefore KMT is wrong." Identify the flaw in this reasoning using KMT postulates and the concept of mean free path.
State the van der Waals equation for 1 mole of a real gas and define each term with its SI units.

A student measures the force required to pull a thin wire frame of length 5.0 cm from the surface of water at 25°C and records 7.28 × 10⁻³ N. Calculate the surface tension of water. If the same experiment is repeated at 75°C, would the measured force increase, decrease, or remain the same? Justify your answer in terms of molecular kinetic energy and hydrogen bonding.

Two liquids A and B have the same molar mass (60 g/mol) but different intermolecular forces: A has only London dispersion forces, while B has hydrogen bonding. At 25°C, liquid A has viscosity 0.3 mPa·s and surface tension 18 mN/m; liquid B has viscosity 1.2 mPa·s and surface tension 72 mN/m. Explain why both viscosity and surface tension are higher for B, and why the ratio η_B/η_A (4.0) differs from γ_B/γ_A (4.0) even though both properties originate from intermolecular forces.
A gas expands from 2.0 L to 5.0 L against a constant external pressure of 1.5 atm. Calculate the work done BY the system in joules. State the sign of w according to IUPAC convention.
Explain why the melting of ice (H₂O(s) → H₂O(l)) is spontaneous at 27°C but non-spontaneous at -10°C, even though ΔH and ΔS are both positive for this transition.
Explain why the entropy change for melting of 1 mol of ice at 0 °C and 1 atm is positive, even though the temperature of the system remains constant during the phase change.

A student places 50 g of ice and 50 g of water in a perfectly insulated, sealed container at 0°C and 1 atm. After 2 hours, they measure the mass of ice and water. What will they observe, and why does this represent a physical equilibrium?

Why does water in an open beaker at 25°C eventually evaporate completely, while water in a sealed bottle at 25°C reaches a constant vapour pressure? Explain using the concept of dynamic equilibrium and system closure.
For the reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), write the expression for Qc. If initial concentrations are [N₂] = 0.5 M, [H₂] = 1.5 M, [NH₃] = 0.2 M, calculate Qc.

For the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), Kc = 2.5 at 700 K. At equilibrium, [SO₂] = 0.4 M, [O₂] = 0.2 M, [SO₃] = 0.5 M. If the concentration of SO₂ is suddenly doubled to 0.8 M while keeping volume and temperature constant, what is the immediate value of Q, and in which direction will the reaction proceed to re-establish equilibrium?

For the equilibrium N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), ΔH = -92 kJ/mol. If the temperature is increased from 400°C to 500°C at constant pressure, what happens to the equilibrium constant Kp and the equilibrium yield of NH₃?

Consider the equilibrium 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2SO₃(g), ΔH = -197 kJ/mol. The system is at equilibrium in a 10 L vessel at 500 K. If the volume is suddenly halved to 5 L at constant temperature, predict the immediate effect on Qp vs Kp and the subsequent shift direction.
A 0.10 M solution of a weak acid HA has pH = 3.00. A student calculates Ka = (10⁻³)²/0.10 = 1.0 × 10⁻⁵. Is this calculation correct? Explain why or why not, and provide the exact Ka value.

A student measures the pH of 0.01 M HCl and 0.01 M CH₃COOH (Ka = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵) at 298 K. Without calculation, predict which solution has lower pH and explain why the difference exists despite identical molar concentrations.

For a 0.10 M NH₃ solution (Kb = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵), a student writes the equilibrium as NH₃ + H₂O ⇌ NH₄⁺ + OH⁻ and sets up: Kb = x²/(0.10 - x). They approximate 0.10 - x ≈ 0.10 and get x = 1.34 × 10⁻³ M, pOH = 2.87, pH = 11.13. Is the 5% approximation valid here? Show the check.

A student dissolves 0.1 M solutions of four salts: NaCl, NH₄Cl, CH₃COONa, and NH₄CN. Without calculation, predict the pH order (from lowest to highest) and justify each prediction based solely on the nature of the parent acid and base.

In the reaction 2H2S + SO2 → 3S + 2H2O, identify which species is oxidized and which is reduced using the classical concept of electronegative/ electropositive elements. Explain why oxygen-transfer definition fails here.
Explain why water has a higher boiling point than H₂S (b.p. –60°C) despite sulfur being larger and more polarisable. Use the concept of hydrogen bonding in your answer.
What is the result of binary addition 1 + 1 + 1 (three 1s added together) in a single column, and what carry is generated to the next column?
Explain in your own words how decomposition helps in solving a problem like "calculate the total price of items in a shopping cart with a 10% discount on items over ₹500".
State the Harrod-Domar growth equation and explain why the First Five Year Plan's actual growth rate (3.6%) exceeded its target (2.1%) despite a savings rate of only 5-6%.

The First Plan allocated 44.6% to agriculture/irrigation but only 4.9% to industry. Using the concept of wage-goods constraint, explain why this allocation was necessary for a labour-surplus economy with 72% workforce in agriculture.
Why did the Green Revolution initially benefit only wheat-growing regions (like Punjab, Haryana, Western UP) and not rice-growing regions to the same extent in Phase I (mid-1960s to mid-1970s)?

Explain why Indian planners in the 1950s believed import substitution was necessary for a newly independent country. Use the concepts of 'infant industry' and 'foreign exchange conservation' in your answer.
Explain why a persistent fiscal deficit (government expenditure > revenue) in the 1980s led to a current account deficit and reserve loss, even though the fiscal deficit was financed domestically.

India agreed to reduce its bound tariff rate on industrial goods from an average of 100% (1990) to 40% by 2005 under WTO. If the applied MFN tariff on a specific machinery item was 15% in 2005, what is the "tariff water" and why does it matter for policy credibility?
Explain why a rise in aggregate GDP growth from 5.6% (1980-91) to 9.4% (2021-22) does not necessarily mean proportional improvement in living standards for agricultural households.
Explain why the Education Commission (1964-66) recommended 6% of GDP for education, and why the current ~4.5% level is considered inadequate despite absolute spending increases.
Explain why the Education Commission (1964-66) recommended 6% of GDP for education, and why the current level of "a little over 4%" is considered inadequate despite absolute spending rising.
Explain why rural development remains crucial for India's overall progress even though agriculture's share in GDP has fallen to around 15% (2023-24).

A farmer borrows ₹1,00,000 from a moneylender at 3% per month simple interest for 6 months to purchase seeds and fertiliser. He repays the principal plus interest after selling his crop. Calculate the total interest paid and the effective annual interest rate. Why does this rate matter for distinguishing formal from informal credit?

A farmer in a rainfed region of Rajasthan grows bajra during Kharif but has no irrigation for Rabi. His family of 5 works on the farm for 4 months and remains idle for 8 months. Using the concept of seasonal unemployment, explain why diversification into goat rearing would be more effective than simply switching to a different Kharif crop.

Explain why the traditional dairy marketing channel (farmer → local trader → wholesaler → retailer → consumer) resulted in farmers receiving only 30-40% of the consumer price, while the Operation Flood cooperative channel enabled 70-80% share.

**UNDERSTAND LEVEL:** Explain why the worker-population ratio for rural women (34.8%) is higher than for urban women (20.7%) in 2023-24 (Table 6.1), despite urban areas having more diverse employment opportunities.

Using Table 6.2 (2023–24), the primary sector employs 46.1% of the workforce but contributes only about 18% to GDP. Explain why this gap exists and what it implies for per-worker productivity in agriculture versus services.

State the formula for calculating the annual employment growth rate (%) between two years using workforce data. If the workforce was 400 million in 1999–2000 and 460 million in 2004–05, what is the approximate annual growth rate? (Assume compound growth over 5 years.)

Using Table 6.3, explain why the secondary sector's employment share stagnated at ~24% between 2011–12 and 2023–24 despite "Make in India" and manufacturing push. Identify two structural reasons from the chapter's logic.

According to the NSO (PLFS), a person who worked for only 1 hour on at least one day during the reference week of 7 days is classified as which of the following? (a) Unemployed (b) Employed (c) Not in labour force (d) Underemployed

Explain why the NCERT states "70% of water in India is polluted" leads to "increased incidence of water-borne diseases" AND "rising health expenditure" — trace the complete causal chain from pollution to fiscal burden.
Using Table 8.1 data, explain why China's annual population growth rate is negative (-0.10%) while Pakistan's is 1.96%, despite both having low sex ratios.

From Table 8.2, China's GDP growth rate declined from 10.3% (1980-90) to 5.0% (2024), while India's rose from 5.7% to 6.5%. A student claims "India's growth performance has overtaken China's." Using the concept of base effect and absolute GDP size, explain why this conclusion is economically flawed.

Table 8.3 shows India's agriculture employs 43% workforce but contributes only 18% GVA, while China's agriculture employs 23% workforce for 8% GVA. Calculate the labor productivity ratio (GVA share ÷ workforce share) for agriculture in both countries. What does the difference imply about disguised unemployment?
Using Table 8.5 data, explain why China's HDI rank (78) is substantially better than India's (130) and Pakistan's (168) despite all three countries having similar per capita incomes in the 1980s.
What were the two main components of Pakistan's regulated policy framework in the late 1950s and 1960s for import-substitution industrialisation?
Why did Pakistan's Green Revolution in the 1960s lead to a dramatic change in the agrarian structure, and what was its limitation as a long-term growth driver?
Explain in your own words how Mary's reaction to the disaster differs from the captain's reaction in the first 24 hours after the wave strike.
Explain how the author uses the contrast between Howard Carter's 1920s investigation and the 2005 CT scan to reveal different dimensions of Tut as protagonist.
In the chapter, the author contrasts Howard Carter's 1920s investigation with the 2005 CT scan. What secondary theme does this contrast primarily illustrate?
Explain in your own words why the Green Movement shifted from "conservation of nature" to "sustainable development" by the 1980s, using the Brundtland Report (1987) as a reference point.
Who was Elizabeth Jennings and which literary group was she associated with in the 1950s?
Explain in your own words why the setting of a "London suburb in the 1950s" is crucial to understanding the conflict in "Mother's Day".
In your own words, explain why understanding the social status of a "cabdriver" in 1880s St. Petersburg is essential to interpreting Iona Potapov's interactions with his passengers.
Explain in your own words why the narrator feels "mortified" when he learns Mrs. Croft is 103 years old.

Explain in your own words why the "bank collapse" mentioned in the story's opening would have been catastrophic for a Managing Director like Satyajit in 1960s India, considering both his personal assets and social standing.
What is the primary reason geologists use the continental shelf break (1000 m isobath) rather than the present coastline for the jigsaw fit reconstruction of continents?
Why do deep-focus earthquakes (depth > 300 km) occur exclusively at convergent plate boundaries and never at divergent or transform boundaries?

A student finds a dark-coloured, heavy rock with visible interlocking crystals of pyroxene and plagioclase feldspar (each 3–5 mm) in a road cut in the Deccan Traps. Name the rock and state whether it is intrusive or extrusive.

Two rocks have identical mineral composition (50% plagioclase, 40% pyroxene, 10% olivine). Rock A has 1 mm crystals; Rock B has 5 mm crystals. Explain the geological history that produced this difference.
Define frost action and state the approximate volumetric expansion of water when it freezes at 0°C. Why does this expansion generate stress in rock joints?
Explain why mushroom rocks (pedestal rocks) develop a narrow base and broad top, and why abrasion is most effective within 1–2 metres of the ground.

On a physical map of India, a student marks the boundary between the Peninsular Plateau and the Northern Plains along the 300 m contour line. Is this an appropriate physiographic boundary? Justify your answer in two sentences.
An UNDERSTAND level question: Explain why Leh (34°N, 3500m) has a mean January temperature of -8°C while Srinagar (34°N, 1585m) records -1°C, despite nearly identical latitudes.

A meteorological station records the following annual data: coldest month mean temperature = 16.5°C, driest month rainfall = 45 mm, annual rainfall = 1120 mm. Using Köppen's criteria, what is the *first* (major group) and *second* (precipitation) letter code for this station?

Two stations, Station X (15°N, 75°E) and Station Y (27°N, 88°E), both have annual rainfall ~2500 mm. Station X has a distinct dry month in January (12 mm); Station Y has no month below 100 mm. Explain why Station X is classified **Am** while Station Y is **Af**, even though both are tropical.

Explain why a delay in monsoon onset by 10-15 days over the core rice-growing belt (Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal) disproportionately reduces rice yields compared to a similar delay over the cotton belt (Maharashtra, Gujarat).
Explain why a tsunami wave that is only 0.5 metres high in the open ocean can become a 10-metre wall of water at the coast.

A farmer in the Ganga-Yamuna Doab finds white calcareous nodules (kankar) at 1-2 metres depth in his field. The soil is clayey loam, light grey, and requires regular nitrogen fertiliser. Identify the soil type and its local name.
Name the three Himalayan river basins that together account for approximately 60% of India's total surface water potential, and state the primary source of their perennial flow.
Why does the Godavari basin, despite being the largest Peninsular basin (≈3.1 lakh km²), exhibit a highly seasonal discharge compared to the much smaller Ganga basin?
Explain why a 226 m high gravity dam was necessary at Bhakra rather than a lower barrage, given the Sutlej's hydrological regime and the project's multiple objectives.
Explain why water conservation is critically needed in India despite the country receiving an average annual rainfall of about 1170 mm.

Explain why Tropical Thorn Forests have an **open canopy (cover < 10%)** and **tree height rarely exceeding 10 m**, linking your answer to the water balance equation (P - PET) and plant allocation strategies.

A student states: "The tree line in the Himalayas is at 4000 m everywhere because temperature drops uniformly with altitude." Identify the specific error in this statement and name two factors other than altitude that cause the tree line to vary spatially.

Using the normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1000 m, calculate the expected temperature at 2500 m if the temperature at 500 m (foothill station) is 30°C. Then explain why the actual temperature at a north-facing slope at 2500 m might be 2–3°C lower than your calculated value.
Why does the Western Ghats have higher amphibian endemism (over 90%) compared to the Eastern Ghats? Explain using geological history and climate.

According to the Indian Census, a worker is defined as a person who participates in any economically productive activity with or without compensation. Which of the following would be classified as a MAIN WORKER in the primary sector? (a) A student who helps on family farm during holidays (b) A full-time agricultural labourer working 180 days a year (c) A retired teacher doing kitchen gardening (d) A software engineer who grows vegetables on weekends.

In 2011, India's workforce distribution was approximately: Primary 46%, Secondary 23%, Tertiary 31%. By 2021 (PLFS estimates), it shifted to Primary 42%, Secondary 25%, Tertiary 33%. A student claims: "The primary sector share fell by 4 percentage points, so 4% of the workforce moved directly into factories." Explain why this reasoning is geographically flawed.
Explain why India's death rate began declining sharply after 1921 while the birth rate remained high until the 1970s, linking this to specific public health interventions and socio-cultural factors.

A village has a population of 6,500, 85% of male workers engaged in agriculture, and is governed by a Gram Panchayat. A nearby town has a population of 5,800, 70% workers in manufacturing and services, and has a Municipal Council. According to Census of India criteria, which is urban and which is rural? Explain why the village is NOT urban despite its larger population.

Explain why the "Forest" category in land use statistics has remained nearly constant at 22-23% of geographical area since 1980-81 despite the Forest Conservation Act (1980), afforestation programs, and the National Forest Policy target of 33%.
Explain why agriculture's share in GVA has declined from 35% (1990-91) to 18.3% (2022-23) while its employment share fell only from 61% to 43% over the same period.
Explain why wheat cultivation is concentrated in the northwestern plains (Punjab, Haryana, western UP) despite these regions receiving less than 75 cm annual rainfall.
What were the three core technological components of the Green Revolution package introduced in India during the mid-1960s?

Explain why the jute industry remains concentrated in the Hooghly basin (West Bengal) despite the partition of 1947 placing 75% of jute-growing areas in East Pakistan (now Bangladesh), while the cotton textile industry decentralised widely across India.

Explain why the abolition of the MRTP Act's asset threshold (₹100 crore) in 1991 was geographically significant for industrial location patterns in India, particularly for large private conglomerates like Tata, Birla, and Reliance.

Why is the Brahmaputra (NW-2) navigable for larger vessels (up to 2000 DWT) in its Assam stretch despite having a braided channel, while the Ganga (NW-1) requires constant dredging to maintain 2.5m depth for 1500-2000 DWT vessels?

Why does India's urban tele-density exceed 130% while rural tele-density remains below 60%, despite BharatNet laying optical fiber to 1.8 lakh gram panchayats? Explain using the concept of "last-mile connectivity" and demand-side constraints.

A map has a Statement of Scale: "2 cm represents 1 km". If this map is reduced to half its original size during photocopying, what happens to the accuracy of the Statement of Scale, the R.F., and the Graphical Scale? Explain why.
On a Survey of India 1:50,000 topographical map, what does a **solid blue circle** of 0.5 mm diameter represent, and how does it differ from a **blue curved line** of the same width?
On a 1:50,000 map, a student measures a curved river length as 8.5 cm using a thread and then multiplies by 50,000 to get 425,000 cm = 4.25 km. Is this correct? Explain why or why not.
Why does a statement scale "1 cm = 500 m" printed on a map become incorrect if the map is photocopied at 80% linear reduction?
What is the Representative Fraction (RF) equivalent of the Statement Scale "1 cm represents 500 m"? Show the unit conversion step.
A map has an RF of 1:25,000. Write the Statement Scale in the form "1 cm represents X km". Explain why the RF denominator (25,000) is divided by 100,000 to get the ground distance in kilometers.

On a 1:50,000 toposheet, you see a series of contour lines forming a distinct V-shape with the apex pointing towards higher elevation (contour values increase towards the apex). The contour interval is 20m. What landform does this represent, and what is the direction of stream flow if a blue line runs through the apex?

Two students examine a contour pattern showing a narrow, elongated projection of contours extending from a main hill mass (contour values: 300m, 320m, 340m on the projection; 360m, 380m on the main hill). Student A calls it a "spur"; Student B calls it a "ridge." Who is correct, and what specific contour evidence distinguishes a spur from a ridge?
On a 1:50,000 SOI toposheet, what does a solid black square of size 0.5 mm × 0.5 mm represent, and how does it differ from a hollow square of the same size?

In the SOI numbering system, the letters A through P are assigned to the sixteen 1:250k sheets within a 1:1M sheet. If letter 'A' represents the north-westernmost 1°×1° sheet, which letter represents the south-easternmost sheet and why?

A vertical aerial photograph was taken with a camera of focal length 152 mm from a flying height of 2500 m above mean sea level. If the average terrain elevation is 500 m above mean sea level, what is the representative fraction (RF) scale of the photograph for the average terrain?

On a vertical aerial photograph, the distance between two road intersections measures 8.5 cm. The same distance measured on a 1:50,000 topographical map is 4.2 cm. What is the scale of the photograph? Explain why this method works even without knowing the focal length or flying height.

Why does a drone (UAV) flying at 120 m altitude typically achieve higher spatial resolution (e.g., 5 cm) than a satellite like Cartosat-3 at 500 km altitude (25 cm PAN), even though Cartosat-3 has more advanced optics? Explain using the geometric relationship between altitude, instantaneous field of view (IFOV), and ground sampling distance (GSD).

Explain why IRS-1A was placed in a sun-synchronous near-polar orbit at ~900 km altitude instead of a geostationary orbit at ~36,000 km, referencing at least three orbital or sensor-performance factors.

Why does the same IRS LISS-IV image (5.8 m resolution) show individual tree crowns in a teak plantation in Madhya Pradesh but cannot distinguish separate trees in a dense sal forest in Jharkhand, even though both are captured at the same spatial resolution?
Why did the Byzantine Empire lose control of Egypt to the Arabs in the 640s despite having a larger, professional army?
Why did the Golden Horde's conversion to Islam under Berke (1250s) and Uzbek Khan (1313) produce a different political outcome than the Il-Khanate's conversion under Ghazan (1295)?

Liang Qichao famously described India as "a country destroyed by a non-country (the East India Company)." Explain why this specific comparison was politically potent for Chinese reformers in the 1890s-1900s, linking it to the fear of "Partition" (like Poland).
Why did the Qing Dynasty's 'Self-Strengthening Movement' (1860s–1890s) fail to prevent China's military defeats, whereas Japan's Meiji reforms succeeded in building a modern military?

A 14-year-old girl writes in her journal: "I'm so lazy and undisciplined. I should be waking up at 5 AM, studying 4 hours daily, and helping at home — but I sleep till 8 and waste time on my phone." Identify which statements reflect her real self and which reflect her ideal self. Then explain why this discrepancy feels more painful at 14 than it would have at age 8.

Radha (3 years 8 months) says: "I am good because I write as well." When asked to explain more, she falls silent. A 9-year-old says: "I am good at making friends and finishing homework on time, but I'm not as fast at running as Kiran." Compare the SELF-DESCRIPTION STRUCTURE of these two children using the developmental framework from the text.
Define "Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA)" as per ICMR and explain how it differs from "nutrient requirement" for an adolescent girl aged 14 years.

A 16-year-old vegetarian boy consumes 3 chapatis (90g wheat), 1 cup cooked dal (30g raw), 1 cup curd (200g), 100g spinach, and 10g oil daily. He eats no fruits, no other vegetables, and no nuts/seeds. Using the five food group guidelines, identify which groups are underrepresented and predict the two most likely micronutrient deficiencies.
According to NFHS-3 (2005–06), what was the reported prevalence of anaemia among adolescent girls (15–19 years) in India, and how did it compare with adolescent boys of the same age group?

Explain in your own words why the bioavailability of iron from a typical Indian vegetarian adolescent diet is often less than 5%, and name two dietary factors that inhibit and two that enhance non-haem iron absorption.

A student says: "I have 6 hours of free time after school, so I should be able to finish my project, exercise, and relax — but I always end up scrolling social media and feel guilty." Explain why "having 6 hours" is misleading using the three dimensions of time, and identify which dimension is being neglected.
A student claims that "100% cotton fabric always shrinks more than 100% polyester fabric." Is this statement universally true? Explain your answer in two sentences.

Two fabrics — Fabric A (cotton, plain weave, 20s yarn, no finish) and Fabric B (cotton, twill weave, 40s yarn, sanforised finish) — are washed identically. Predict which will show greater dimensional change and explain why, referencing at least two factors beyond fibre type.
Explain why wool fibres are scoured with alkaline detergent at 50–60°C while silk is degummed with mild soap at 95–100°C, linking each condition to the fibre's chemical structure.
Explain why a 100% polyester fabric cannot be dyed with direct dyes used for cotton, and name the dye class suitable for polyester.

A student claims: "Since we spend 70% of our active time in verbal communication, verbal communication is more important than non-verbal communication." Using the sensory retention data from NCERT, explain why this reasoning is flawed.
Explain in your own words why Bluetooth is classified as a wireless technology even though it operates only over very short distances (typically 10 metres).

A pregnant woman in a remote village receives iron-folic acid tablets and antenatal check-ups from an ANM at the Sub-Centre. At 36 weeks, she develops severe anaemia (Hb 7 g/dL) and is sent to the Community Health Centre (CHC) for IV iron therapy. Classify the care received at Sub-Centre and CHC into primary/secondary/tertiary levels and justify each classification.

A street food vendor keeps cooked chole (chickpeas) in a large aluminium pot at room temperature (32°C) from 11:00 AM until 8:00 PM, reheating it briefly before serving. Using the concept of the "temperature danger zone" and the three necessary conditions for food-borne illness from the textbook, explain why this practice is hazardous even if the chole was cooked thoroughly in the morning.

A student says: "I have 24 hours like everyone else, but I still can't finish my work. Time management doesn't work for me because my schedule is unpredictable." Identify the TWO fundamental characteristics of time as a resource that this student is ignoring, and explain why unpredictability makes planning MORE necessary, not less.

A family complains that their living room feels cramped despite being 4 m × 5 m. They use dark brown curtains, a large sectional sofa against the long wall, and a floor-to-ceiling bookshelf on the opposite wall. Explain, using the principle of Roominess, why the room feels small and suggest two specific changes.

An infant doubles birth weight by 6 months and triples it by 12 months. Explain why the energy requirement per kg body weight (108 kcal/kg at 0-6 months) is nearly double that of an adult doing heavy work, despite the infant's much smaller absolute size.
State the three primary anthropometric indicators used to assess physical growth in infancy and the expected quantitative change for each by 12 months of age.

Explain why an infant's energy requirement per kilogram of body weight (108 kcal/kg/day at 0-6 months) is nearly double that of an adult doing heavy work, despite the infant being far less physically active.
State the ICMR 2010 recommended dietary allowance for Energy and Protein for an infant aged 0–6 months, including the units used in the table.
Why is the BCG vaccine given at birth while the Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine is delayed until 9 months?
An UNDERSTAND level question: Explain why the ICMR balanced diet for preschoolers (Table 5) specifies 500 ml of milk for both 1-3 years and 4-6 years, while cereal quantity doubles from 60g to 120g.

A parent asks: "The ICMR table says 120 g cereals for a 5-year-old. Does that mean 120 g of dry wheat flour, or 120 g of cooked chapati?" What is the correct interpretation according to ICMR guidelines?
Why does ICMR recommend the same 500 ml milk for both 1-3 years and 4-6 years age groups, while cereals increase from 60 g to 120 g and pulses stay constant at 30 g?
Explain why the ICMR RDA for iron jumps from 16 mg (7–9 years) to 27 mg for girls aged 10–12 years, but only to 21 mg for boys of the same age.

A 10-year-old boy weighs 42 kg and is 138 cm tall. Using the BMI-for-age formula (weight in kg / height in m²), calculate his BMI and state whether this value alone is sufficient to classify him as obese according to WHO growth standards for school-age children.

Explain why the Mid-Day Meal Scheme (MDMS) has been more effective in reducing gender gaps in school attendance than in eliminating undernutrition among enrolled children, despite providing 450 kcal and 12g protein per meal as per norms.
A mother buys a 100% wool sweater for her 3-year-old because it is "warm and natural." According to NCERT guidelines, what is the primary reason this choice may be unsuitable for daily wear?

A 13-year-old girl has grown 8 cm in height over 6 months. Her mother buys her three expensive formal dresses for a wedding season. Two months later, the dresses are tight at the shoulders and short at the hem. What is the PRIMARY clothing principle violated here, specific to adolescence?

A family puts ₹1,00,000 in a bank fixed deposit at 6% p.a. and another ₹1,00,000 in a residential plot expecting 12% p.a. appreciation. Classify each as savings or investment using the NCERT distinction of "productive in economic sense" and explain why the plot is NOT productive in economic terms despite higher returns.

Explain why a family saving for a daughter's marriage in 12 years might prefer Public Provident Fund (PPF) over a 5-year bank Fixed Deposit (FD), even if the FD currently offers a slightly higher interest rate.

A family earns ₹50,000/month and spends ₹45,000 on essential expenses. They want a ₹5 lakh home loan. The bank asks for their property papers as security. Identify which TWO of the Four Cs are being assessed here and explain why the family's high expenses weaken one specific C.
What is the result of the expression `17 // 5` and `17 % 5` in Python, and how do these two results relate to each other mathematically?

A teacher has the monthly attendance percentages of 40 students for the whole year. She wants to identify students with consistently low attendance (<75%) across months. Which visualisation would be MOST effective and why? (Options: Pie chart, Line chart, Bar chart, Scatter plot)
Explain in your own words why a Money Bill cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha, and what happens if the Rajya Sabha does not return it within 14 days.
Define 'State' under Article 12 of the Constitution of India and explain whether a private university receiving 90% government funding and performing public functions qualifies as 'State'.

A Municipal Corporation passes a bye-law: "No street vendor shall operate within 500m of any mall." A vendor challenges it claiming the Corporation lacked the power to impose a *distance-based* restriction, only a *licensing* power under the Parent Act. Explain the legal test the court will apply to decide if this bye-law is *ultra vires* (beyond powers).

A village in Rajasthan has practiced a unique form of adoption (adopting a nephew as heir) for 150 years. The Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, codifies adoption rules but Section 5 says the Act applies "save as otherwise provided by custom." Can this village custom override the statutory requirement that only a Hindu male can adopt? Apply the *tests for a valid custom* to justify your answer.
Explain why the RTI Act, 2005 is considered a "demand-driven" law reform, unlike the Hindu Code Bills of the 1950s which were "supply-driven."

A private engineering college receives 90% of its funding from the State Government, its governing body is nominated by the Government, and it performs the public function of higher education. Is it "State" under Article 12? Explain using the instrumentality test.

A person is arrested for an offence punishable with 5 years imprisonment. The police file a chargesheet after 60 days. The accused applies for statutory bail under Section 167(2) CrPC. Will the bail be granted? Explain the legal reasoning.

A person is arrested for an offence punishable with 3 years imprisonment and fine. The offence is listed as bailable in the First Schedule of CrPC. The police refuse bail, saying 'it's a serious offence'. Is the police action legal? Explain using the distinction between bailable and non-bailable offences.

A person is arrested for an offence punishable with 3 years imprisonment. The police officer refuses to release them on bail, saying it's a non-bailable offence. Is the officer correct? Explain using CrPC classification.

What is the constitutional definition of a 'child' in India for the purpose of Fundamental Rights, and which Article explicitly prohibits employment of children below 14 years in factories and hazardous occupations?

A Hindu wife earning ₹30,000/month files for maintenance against her husband earning ₹2 lakh/month. The husband argues she is "not unable to maintain herself" because she has income. Explain whether she can claim maintenance and the legal test applied.

A Hindu wife files for maintenance under Section 125 CrPC. Her husband argues she is "able to maintain herself" because she has a Master’s degree and worked for two years before marriage. She has not worked in 10 years and has two minor children. Can the husband’s argument succeed? Answer in 2-3 sentences with legal basis.

A function \( g(t) = 50 - 4.9t^2 \) gives the height (in metres) of a ball thrown upward from a 50 m building after \( t \) seconds. Explain why the domain of \( g \) in this physical situation is NOT all real numbers, and find the largest possible domain.
State the exact radian measure of an angle of 150° in terms of π, and explain why the answer is not approximately 2.62 radian when asked for an exact value.
A ball is dropped from a height of 128 m. Each rebound reaches 3/4 of the previous height. Identify the type of progression and find the height after the 5th rebound.

A parabolic arch bridge has a span of 40 m and a maximum height of 10 m. If the vertex is at the highest point and the axis is vertical, which standard form should you use and why? What are the coordinates of the endpoints?
State the number of significant figures in each of the following measurements: (a) 0.00450 kg, (b) 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹, (c) 1500 m, (d) 1.500 × 10³ m.

A student measures the diameter of a wire using a screw gauge and records it as 0.00250 cm. Another student says this has 5 significant figures because there are five digits. Explain why the second student is incorrect and state the correct number of significant figures.
A student calculates the volume of a cube of side 3.204 cm using a calculator and gets 32.896128 cm³. The side length has 4 significant figures. What should the student report as the volume, and why?

A student measures the thickness of a human hair as 0.000085 m. Express this in scientific notation and state its order of magnitude. Explain why the order of magnitude is not simply the exponent of the original decimal form.

The mass of an electron is 9.11 × 10^-31 kg and the mass of a proton is 1.67 × 10^-27 kg. A student claims the proton is "about 4 orders of magnitude heavier" because -27 - (-31) = 4. Is this correct? Justify using the rounding rule for order of magnitude.

A student measures the diameter of a wire using a screw gauge. The main scale reading is 3 mm and the circular scale reading is 45 divisions. The pitch of the screw gauge is 0.5 mm and it has 50 divisions on the circular scale. What is the least count of this screw gauge?

Why does a vernier calipers with 20 divisions on the vernier scale matching 19 divisions on the main scale (1 MSD = 1 mm) have a smaller least count than one with 10 divisions matching 9 main scale divisions?

A student measures the length of a rod five times using a vernier caliper (least count 0.01 cm) and gets: 3.21 cm, 3.22 cm, 3.21 cm, 3.22 cm, 3.21 cm. The true length is 3.25 cm. Are these measurements accurate? Are they precise? Justify.

A student measures the time period of a simple pendulum using a stopwatch. The stopwatch consistently starts 0.2 seconds late due to the student's reaction time. If the true period is 2.00 s, what type of error is this, and what will be the measured value after 20 oscillations?

A student measures the side of a cube as L = 5.0 ± 0.1 cm. They calculate the volume V = L³ and claim the absolute error in volume is ΔV = 3 × 0.1 = 0.3 cm³. Explain why this reasoning is incorrect and state the correct method.

A particle moves along the x-axis. Its positions at t = 0 s, 2 s, 4 s, and 6 s are x = 0 m, +5 m, +2 m, and +8 m respectively. What is the displacement of the particle between t = 0 s and t = 6 s? State the SI unit.

A car travels 60 km north in 1 hour, then 40 km south in 1 hour. Without calculating, explain whether the magnitude of average velocity equals the average speed for this trip. What physical principle determines the answer?
A particle moves along the x-axis with velocity given by v(t) = 3t² - 12t + 9 m/s. What is the average acceleration of the particle between t = 1 s and t = 3 s? State the SI unit.

For the same particle v(t) = 3t² - 12t + 9 m/s, find the instantaneous acceleration at t = 2 s. Explain why the instantaneous acceleration at t = 2 s is not zero even though the average acceleration between t = 1 s and t = 3 s is zero.

A ball is thrown vertically upward with initial speed 20 m/s. At the highest point of its motion, what are the values of velocity and acceleration? Explain why acceleration is not zero even though velocity is momentarily zero.
Two cars A and B move on a straight road. Car A moves east at 20 m/s, car B moves west at 15 m/s. What is the velocity of A relative to B? State the magnitude, direction, and SI unit.

A police van moving at 30 km/h fires a bullet at a thief's car speeding away at 192 km/h in the same direction. Muzzle speed of bullet is 150 m/s. Explain why the speed relevant for damaging the thief's car is the relative speed of the bullet with respect to the thief's car, not the muzzle speed.
A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. What is the magnitude and direction of its acceleration at the instant it is released? State the SI unit.

A student throws a ball vertically upward with initial speed 20 m/s. At the highest point of its motion, the ball's velocity is zero. Is the acceleration zero at that instant? Explain why or why not using the concept of force.

A car travelling at 20 m/s stops in 40 m with constant deceleration. If the same car travels at 40 m/s with the same deceleration, what will be its stopping distance? Explain why the answer is not simply double.
A car travels at 20 m/s. The driver's reaction time is 0.5 s. What is the reaction distance traveled before brakes are applied?
A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial speed of 20 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s² and upward as positive, what is the velocity of the ball at the highest point of its motion? State the SI unit.

A car moving at 72 km/h applies brakes and stops in 50 m. A student writes: "u = 72 km/h, v = 0, s = 50 m, find a using v² = u² + 2as" and gets a = -51.84 m/s². Why is this answer physically unreasonable, and what step did the student skip?
A velocity vector has components vₓ = -12 m/s and vᵧ = 5 m/s. In which quadrant does the vector lie? Explain why the angle calculated using tan⁻¹(vᵧ/vₓ) must be adjusted by adding 180°.

Two vectors **A** = 3î + 4ĵ m and **B** = −5î + 2ĵ m are added. A student claims the resultant magnitude is 10 m because "3 + 4 + 5 + 2 = 14, close to 10". Explain why this reasoning is physically incorrect and find the actual resultant magnitude.

A car moves from point A(2, 1) to point B(5, 5) on a flat field. The driver actually takes a winding path of length 8 m. Find the displacement vector and its magnitude. Explain why the displacement magnitude is different from the path length.
A stone is thrown horizontally with a speed of 10 m/s from a cliff 80 m high. What is the horizontal component of its velocity 2 seconds after projection? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
State the horizontal and vertical components of initial velocity for a projectile launched with speed 25 m/s at 30° above horizontal. Give the formulas and compute numerical values with units.
A projectile is launched with speed 20 m/s at an angle of 30° with the horizontal. What is the maximum height reached by the projectile? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

A 2 kg book lies at rest on a horizontal table. The weight of the book is 19.6 N downward. A student claims: "The normal reaction force from the table is also 19.6 N upward because action and reaction are equal and opposite (Newton's Third Law)." Is this reasoning correct? Explain why or why not.

A 2 kg block rests on a smooth horizontal table. A horizontal force of 10 N acts on it for 3 seconds. The force is then removed. Describe the motion of the block *during* the 3 seconds and *after* the force is removed. Use F = ma and F = dp/dt in your explanation.
A 0.5 kg ball moving at 10 m/s hits a wall and rebounds at 8 m/s in the opposite direction. Calculate the change in momentum. Explain why the change is not simply 0.5 × (10 - 8) = 1 kg·m/s.

A 0.15 kg cricket ball moving at 40 m/s is caught by a fielder who brings it to rest in 0.1 s. Explain why the momentum of the ball alone is not conserved, but the momentum of the ball+fielder+Earth system is conserved. Identify the external impulse.

A block of mass 2 kg rests on a horizontal table. The coefficient of static friction between the block and table is 0.4. What is the maximum value of static friction that can act on the block? (Take g = 10 m/s²)

A block of mass 5 kg rests on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of static friction is 0.4. A horizontal force of 15 N is applied. Explain why the block does not move, and state the magnitude and direction of the friction force acting on it. (Take g = 10 m/s²)

A car of mass 1000 kg takes a circular turn of radius 50 m on a flat road at 20 m/s. The coefficient of static friction between tyres and road is 0.8. Explain why the car does not skid, and calculate the required centripetal force. Compare it with the maximum available friction force.
A circular race track of radius 200 m is banked at an angle of 12°. What is the optimum speed (in m/s) for a car to negotiate the curve without relying on friction? Take g = 9.8 m/s².

A 5 kg block rests on a rough horizontal floor (μs = 0.4). A horizontal force F = 15 N is applied. The block does not move. A student draws the FBD and writes: "fs = μs N = 0.4 × 50 = 20 N acting opposite to F." Identify the conceptual error in this statement and explain why it violates the nature of static friction.
A porter carries a 20 kg load on his head and walks 50 m on a level road at constant speed. What is the work done by the porter's upward force on the load? State the SI unit of your answer.

A block is pulled by a force of 10 N at an angle of 60° to the horizontal. The block moves 4 m horizontally. Explain why the work done by the force is not simply 10 N × 4 m = 40 J. What is the actual work done?

A truck of mass 2000 kg and a bicycle of mass 20 kg are both moving at 10 m/s. Which has more kinetic energy? Explain why the factor \( \frac{1}{2} \) appears in the formula \( K = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \) but not in momentum \( p = mv \).
A 5 kg object is raised from a table (height 0.8 m) to a shelf (height 2.3 m). What is the change in its gravitational potential energy? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)

Two students discuss a 1 kg book on a table 1 m above the floor. Student A says its potential energy is 9.8 J. Student B says its potential energy is 0 J if we choose the table as reference. Who is correct? Explain.

A spring of force constant $k = 200\ \text{N/m}$ is compressed by 10 cm. A student calculates the stored energy as $U = kx = 200 \times 0.1 = 20\ \text{J}$. Identify the error and explain why the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ appears in the correct formula.

A constant force of 10 N acts on a block moving at a constant velocity of 2 m/s in the direction of the force. What is the instantaneous power delivered by the force? Explain why this equals the average power over any interval.

Two identical balls of mass m undergo a head-on elastic collision. Ball A moves at 4 m/s toward stationary Ball B. After collision, Ball A stops and Ball B moves at 4 m/s. Explain WHY this happens using the concept of momentum and energy transfer, not just the formula.

A system consists of three particles of masses 2 kg, 3 kg, and 5 kg placed at coordinates (1, 2), (3, -1), and (-2, 4) metres respectively. What are the coordinates of the centre of mass of this system?

Two particles of masses m and 2m are separated by a distance d. A student claims the centre of mass is exactly at the midpoint between them. Is this correct? Explain why or why not using the definition of centre of mass.

A force **F** = 10 N acts on a particle at position **r** = (2 m, 0, 0) from the origin. The force is directed along the positive y-axis. Calculate the torque vector **τ** about the origin. Explain why the torque is not zero even though the force is applied at a distance from the origin.

A particle of mass 2 kg moves with velocity (3î + 4ĵ) m/s. At a certain instant its position vector from origin is (5î + 2ĵ) m. What is the angular momentum of the particle about the origin? Express in vector form with units.
A uniform metre rule is balanced on a knife-edge at the 50 cm mark. A 20 g mass is suspended at the 10 cm mark. At which mark must a 40 g mass be suspended to restore balance? (Assume g = 9.8 m/s²)

A crowbar of length 1.5 m is used to lift a heavy stone. The fulcrum is placed 0.2 m from the stone. If a person applies a downward force of 150 N at the other end, what is the maximum weight of the stone that can be lifted? Explain why the mechanical advantage is greater than 1.

A thin rod of length L has two point masses m and 2m attached at its ends. The rod rotates about an axis perpendicular to it passing through the centre. A student writes I = m(L/2) + 2m(L/2) = 1.5mL. Explain why this is incorrect and write the correct expression.
Two balls of different masses (100 g and 500 g) are dropped from the same height in a vacuum. Which one has greater acceleration? Explain why using Newton's laws.
What is the orbital velocity of a satellite in a circular orbit just above Earth's surface (h ≈ 0)? Express in terms of g and R_E, and give the numerical value using g = 9.8 m/s², R_E = 6400 km.
Why does an astronaut in a satellite experience weightlessness even though the gravitational force on them is nearly 90% of their surface weight? Explain using Newton's second law.
What is the total mechanical energy of a 500 kg satellite in a circular orbit at a height of 400 km above Earth's surface? (Given: Rₑ = 6400 km, Mₑ = 6.0 × 10²⁴ kg, G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²)
A steel rod of cross-sectional area 2.5 cm² is subjected to a tensile force of 10 kN. What is the magnitude of stress developed in the rod? Express your answer in pascals.
A steel wire of original length 2.0 m stretches by 1.5 mm when a load is applied. What is the longitudinal strain in the wire? Express your answer in scientific notation.

A cylindrical rod is subjected to a tangential force on its top face while the bottom face is fixed. The top face displaces horizontally by 0.2 mm over a height of 50 cm. A student calculates shearing strain as 0.2/50 = 0.004. Is this correct? Explain why or why not, and give the correct value.

A steel wire of original diameter 2.0 mm and length 1.5 m is stretched by a force within its elastic limit. If the wire elongates by 0.3 mm and its diameter decreases by 0.0012 mm, what is the Poisson's ratio of steel? State the SI unit of Poisson's ratio.

A crane is designed to lift a maximum load of 5 tonnes. The yield strength of the steel rope is 300 × 10⁶ N/m². If a safety factor of 10 is used, what is the minimum required cross-sectional area of the rope? (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)

A rectangular beam of length 4 m, breadth 10 cm, and depth 20 cm is supported at its ends and loaded at the centre with 1000 N. The Young's modulus of the material is 2 × 10¹¹ N/m². Calculate the depression at the centre. If the depth is doubled to 40 cm while keeping breadth constant, by what factor does the depression change?

In a hydraulic lift, the input piston has area 5 cm² and the output piston has area 500 cm². A student claims: "The output force is 100 times the input force, so we are creating energy from nothing." Explain why this reasoning is incorrect using the concept of work done.

A solid iron cube (density 7800 kg/m³) and a hollow iron shell of the same outer dimensions are both fully submerged in water. Which experiences a greater buoyant force? Explain using the pressure-depth argument, not just the formula.

Two identical horizontal plates of area 0.02 m² are separated by 2 mm of glycerine. The top plate is pulled horizontally with a force of 0.5 N and moves at a constant velocity of 0.1 m/s. Calculate the coefficient of viscosity of glycerine. If the same experiment is done with water, would the required force be larger or smaller? Explain why at molecular level.

Water flows through a horizontal pipe of diameter 2.0 cm at 0.5 m/s. If the pipe diameter is doubled to 4.0 cm while keeping the volume flow rate constant, what happens to the Reynolds number? Explain physically why.

A soap film is formed on a rectangular wire frame with a movable slider of length 10 cm. The slider is pulled outward by 2 cm with a constant force of 0.03 N. Calculate the surface tension of the soap solution. Explain why the factor 2 appears in the force formula F = 2Sl.

Two identical copper blocks A and B are at 80°C and 20°C respectively. They are placed in thermal contact in an insulated container. Describe the direction of heat flow and the final equilibrium temperature. Explain why the final temperature is exactly 50°C.

Two identical copper rods, one 10 cm long and the other 1 m long, are heated through the same temperature rise ΔT. Which rod experiences a larger fractional increase in length (Δl/l)? Explain why the absolute expansion Δl differs but the fractional expansion is the same.

Two rods of identical dimensions but different materials (copper K = 385 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹, steel K = 50.2 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹) have their hot ends at 100°C and cold ends at 0°C. Without calculation, which rod has a steeper temperature gradient dT/dx along its length? Explain why.

Two rods of identical dimensions but different materials (copper and steel) are joined end-to-end. The free ends are kept at 100°C and 0°C. In steady state, is the heat current through the copper rod greater than, less than, or equal to that through the steel rod? Explain why.

A student claims: "If I double the Celsius temperature of a hot plate from 100 °C to 200 °C, its radiative power increases by 2⁴ = 16 times." Identify the error and calculate the actual factor using absolute temperatures.

A student claims: "If I increase the source temperature T₁ while keeping sink temperature T₂ constant, the Carnot efficiency increases. But if I decrease T₂ while keeping T₁ constant, efficiency also increases. Therefore, to maximize efficiency, I should make T₁ as high as possible and T₂ as low as possible - ideally T₂ = 0 K giving 100% efficiency." Identify the correct physical reasoning and the practical flaw in this statement.
A student claims: "The COP of a refrigerator is always less than 1 because efficiency can never exceed 100%." Explain why this reasoning is incorrect, using the First Law and the definition of COP.
Two gases, hydrogen (molar mass 2 g/mol) and oxygen (32 g/mol), are at the same temperature. Which has a higher rms speed? Explain why the rms speed depends on molar mass but not on the gas pressure.

A 0.5 kg mass attached to a spring (k = 200 N/m) oscillates in a fluid providing viscous damping with constant b = 2 kg/s. Write the differential equation of motion and identify whether the system is underdamped, critically damped, or overdamped.

Explain why the motion of a damped oscillator with x(t) = A₀e^(-bt/2m) cos(ω't + φ) is NOT strictly simple harmonic motion, yet the NCERT textbook says it is "approximately so only for time intervals much less than 2m/b".

A block on a frictionless horizontal surface is attached to a spring (k = 200 N/m). The block is pulled 5 cm to the right and released from rest at t = 0. Explain why the displacement equation must be x(t) = A cos(ωt) and not x(t) = A sin(ωt) for this specific initial condition, without solving for A and ω.
State Newton's formula for the speed of sound in air and the thermodynamic assumption behind it. What is the predicted value at STP (P = 1.013 × 10⁵ Pa, ρ = 1.29 kg/m³)?

Two harmonic waves traveling along a string are given by y₁ = 0.02 sin(2x - 4t) and y₂ = 0.02 sin(2x - 4t + π/3), where x is in meters and t in seconds. Without calculating the exact resultant, explain whether the resultant amplitude will be greater than, equal to, or less than 0.04 m, and justify using the phase difference.
